comment: Human-reviewed creative worlds for concept-seed.mjs, organized into seven inspiration wells: the distinct places designers actually mine for award-level work. Every entry must create an immediate mental image, inherit concrete material, spatial, or compositional laws, translate those laws into reusable interface grammar, and exploit the web medium. Literal software archetypes, style names without inherited laws, and tacked-on spectacle are rejected before review.

qualityBar.principle: Catalog visual worlds a designer could mine on sight: every concept must name a magnetic world, artifact, or graphic tradition whose look immediately yields a palette and material vocabulary, a type voice, at least three distinct interface component roles, and one signature state change, then stay structurally generative, product-legible, and responsibly executable across a whole product rather than one opening page. Prefer worlds people already recognize and love: built-in cultural resonance beats equal lawfulness in obscurity.
rejectIf: The form starts from a generic software or operations container (a dashboard, control room, workflow, planner, tracker, queue, or management console) or mistakes ordinary product chrome for a visual world. Craft tools, scientific instruments, media systems, and working environments are welcome when their materials, gestures, and traditions are specific and generative, and so are culturally tested graphic artifacts and display languages (tickets, labels, stamps, forms, signage, notation, instrument displays) when their information structure becomes the interface's.

The concept names a design movement, era, or style as a label instead of inheriting its laws through a canonical two-dimensional artifact (a poster, page, sleeve, specimen, standards manual) or a place whose surfaces, not furniture, carry the grammar; geometry, ornament logic, materials, and information structure must become reusable interface language.

The world's organizing medium is sound, scent, taste, or unaided touch and it owns no canonical visual notation or artifact: a world may sound or smell like something, but its laws must arrive through the eyes as color, form, and composition.

The world is a single prop, specimen, or instant rather than an expansive system: if it cannot supply at least three distinct component roles plus a hierarchy of display and body voices, it is a detail inside a larger world that should be cataloged instead.
The idea survives only as styling over cards, sidebars, or ordinary application chrome.
Spectacle is unrelated to product meaning or disappears when the core task is explained.

The source world lacks its own topology, states, motion, material behavior, or memorable human experience. Mythic, speculative, and impossible worlds are welcome when their laws are vivid and coherent rather than borrowed franchise decoration.
The same information and decisions cannot remain available through semantic structure.

The concept differs from its nearest catalog neighbor only by subject matter, specimen, industry, lineage wording, or visual styling rather than by memorable experience and at least two reusable system laws.
The source is merely respectable or technically interesting, not magnetic enough that a person would choose to experience it.
The concept is an atmosphere or material world whose material carries no intrinsic two-dimensional pattern or graphic system; mood, light, or texture alone never yields component grammar.
The concept is an abstract notation or symbol lineage with no produced-artifact tradition behind it; notation qualifies only as a designed, printed, or displayed artifact.

The world's rendered look coincides with a currently AI-colonized trend (glassmorphism waves, aurora gradients, soft neon glass): however legitimate the historical lineage, if this month's AI-generated design already wears the aesthetic, the entry reads as slop on arrival and cannot recover.

provenSeams: broadcast graphics: weather boards, election-night graphics, scorebugs, channel and network idents
packaging and collectible cultures, including non-Western print: matchbox labels, ekiben wrappers, lucha libre, hand-painted film posters
title-card and credits traditions across film, TV, and anime eras
sports identity: liveries, kits, crests, race graphics
computing and instrument display eras with era-specific screen language
authoringStrategy.tierWeighting: Overweight interaction-tier display languages: highest flagship share, smallest pool. Graphic tier stays the core. Atmosphere qualifies only through the intrinsic-pattern rule.
authoringStrategy.exemplars: Author against the reviewer three-star approvals as positive exemplars; rejection and rating notes are the negative space.
authoringStrategy.renderSafety: No brass or metal interface chrome, no non-Latin interface copy, no AI-cliche motifs (glyph rain, recording dots). Board and hero must read as one system.
authoringStrategy.territoryStrategy: Proven seams saturate: hunt the canonical peak of territories the catalog has never touched, and gate every candidate on system-level distinctness (palette plus type voice) from approved entries, not name-level.
authoringStrategy.culturalCare: Two separate gates. Care: skip living sacred or ceremonial traditions without an established commercial graphic lineage, and skip highly religious material outright. Extraction: skip a tradition when a living community holds it as identity and that community has a history of dispossession, even where a commercial lineage exists, because the catalog output is an uncredited imitation for an unrelated product. The line is not Western versus non-Western; majority-culture craft and commercial print traditions stay in, and more non-Western systems are still wanted. Never strip a lineage field to keep a surface-level entry.
authoringStrategy.shelfDedup: Dedup at shelf level, not entry level: every candidate names its seam (the store shelf it would sit on), and a candidate whose seam appears in provenSeams or already holds approved entries is dead on arrival unless it is argued as a different tier AND a higher canonical peak than what the shelf holds. Never justify a candidate by naming its nearest existing neighbor; that framing selects for redundancy. The authoring-context artifact (scripts/catalog-authoring-context.mjs) is the mandatory input for sourcing agents; ad-hoc corpus exports are a protocol bug.

wells.label: Human Graphic Systems
wells.description: Human graphic languages: print, editorial sequence, typography, notation, and cartography, whose two-dimensional compositional laws transfer to interface almost directly.

wells.label: The Graphic Canon
wells.description: Design movements and schools entered as concrete worlds and artifacts that carry each movement's laws: grid, geometry, ornament logic, palette, and conviction, never a style name alone.

wells.label: Vernacular & Ephemera
wells.description: Anonymous designed artifacts proven by decades of real use, from tickets and labels to forms and scoreboards, dense with graphic law and latent interaction structure.

wells.label: Instruments & Signals
wells.description: Machines, instruments, and display hardware that already solved showing state and inviting manipulation under hard constraints, supplying interaction physics as well as looks.

wells.label: The Medium Itself
wells.description: The browser and computation as the material itself: scroll, cursor, shaders, generative systems, and web-native culture whose work can exist nowhere else.

wells.label: Material & Imagined Worlds
wells.description: Natural, material, and imagined worlds with their own physics and topology: space, terrain, life, light, craft matter, food, and impossible geographies.

wells.label: Performance, Place & Time
wells.description: Sequence and choreography of attention through time and space: cinema, stage, music, ritual, play, inhabited places, and remembered time.

families.label: Graphic Worlds & Publishing
families.description: Print, pigment, typography, photography, editorial sequence, broadcast graphics, and worlds composed through marks and pages.

concepts.form: a botanical folio following one plant through seed, leaf, flower, fruit, and winter husk, where each plate keeps the same exact scale and ground
concepts.lineage: Botanical illustration, herbarium folios, and phenological observation
concepts.spark: Five cream plates align on the same stem: a tight green bud opens scarlet, swells into black fruit, then remains as a dry silver cage.
system: Palette/material: warm cream plate ground with hairline sepia rules, botanical greens and scarlet-to-black fruit as the only saturation, graphite gray for labels at rest
Type/composition: engraved italic species names over small-caps stage labels, five fixed-scale plates banded on one shared baseline with captions ranked beneath
Topology/navigation: Move by life stage, date, plant part, plate detail, and recurring fixed landmark.
Controls/state: Align, overlay, compare, and annotate with dormant, emerging, flowering, fruiting, and senescent states.
Responsive/motion: Use registered overlays or a stage strip and provide descriptive change summaries.
concepts.webLeverage: Image registration can make subtle seasonal transformation directly comparable without automatic morphing.

concepts.form: a cyanotype herbarium exposed beneath leaves and lace, where sunlight records direct contact as white silhouettes inside Prussian blue
concepts.lineage: Cyanotype photography, botanical specimen recording, and contact printing
concepts.spark: After rinsing, a fern appears as a white branching ghost in saturated blue, with every curled tip edged by a faint halo of sun.
system: Palette/material: saturated Prussian blue ground with white contact silhouettes as figures, pale sun-halo cyan edging the active specimen, wash-gray for unexposed margins
Type/composition: handwritten specimen labels in white pencil on blue, plates ranked in an even herbarium grid, one Latin name anchoring each sheet's lower edge
Topology/navigation: Connect placed object, contact edge, exposure region, wash, and final print.
Controls/state: Arrange, expose, mask, rinse, and compare with coated, latent, exposed, developing, and fixed states.
Responsive/motion: Use discrete exposure proofs and pair silhouettes with specimen names and tactile descriptions.
concepts.webLeverage: Time-based exposure masks can demonstrate contact, occlusion, and overexposure from a lightweight image model.

concepts.form: a six-panel paper screen carrying a storm over black pines and white surf, where a split reed brush drags dry pine-soot ink across gold-flecked fibers so untouched paper flashes as rain
concepts.lineage: Japanese suibokuga ink landscape, byobu screen composition, split-brush dry-ink technique, and pine-soot ink craft
concepts.spark: Across six gold-flecked panels, one broken black stroke bends a pine toward the sea; the paper left between its fibers becomes a sheet of hard white rain.
system: Palette/material: pine-soot black in dry broken strokes over gold-flecked paper ground, untouched fiber white reading as rain, the wet saturated stroke marking the active passage
Type/composition: a single vertical seal and brushed signature as the only lettering, six hinged panels composing one horizon with weight massed low against empty sky
Topology/navigation: Read the storm across hinged panels, then trace each wave, pine, rain gap, and brush passage back to its gesture.
Controls/state: Load, split, drag, hinge, and compare with saturated, broken, skipping, pooled, dry, and folded states.
Responsive/motion: Preserve the full horizon as an accordion sequence and expose brush direction and untouched negative space without simulated painting.
concepts.webLeverage: Registered stroke, fiber, and panel layers let users connect scenic weather to the exact physical gesture, then fold or flatten the panorama without losing place.

concepts.form: a mezzotint plate rocked entirely to black and polished back toward light, where images emerge by removing darkness rather than drawing shadow
concepts.lineage: Mezzotint engraving and tonal print traditions
concepts.spark: The first proof is absolute velvet black; after hours of burnishing, a pale face and one silver sleeve surface from the darkness.
system: Palette/material: total rocked velvet black as the ground, burnished silver-white as the only light, warm plate-tone brown at half-scraped passages, nothing ever drawn on white
Type/composition: engraved roman captions confined to the lower margin, the plate itself untitled and dark, tonal masses composed from the black downward toward light
Topology/navigation: Navigate tonal regions from fully rocked ground through scraped and burnished highlights.
Controls/state: Rock, scrape, burnish, proof, and compare with black, opening, luminous, flattened, and worn states.
Responsive/motion: Use stepped tonal proofs and include a high-contrast contour reading for low-vision access.
concepts.webLeverage: A reversible tonal mask can reveal subtractive image formation while retaining every proof state.

concepts.form: a moonlit brass-band procession screenprinted across translucent mulberry-paper curtains, where cyan instruments, amber lanterns, and scarlet figures cohere at exact overlap while deliberate drift releases rhythmic ghost companions
concepts.lineage: Serigraph poster workshops, procession graphics, translucent paper installation, and transparent spot-color overprinting
concepts.spark: Amber lanterns cross the scarlet dancers and ignite orange faces; one cyan horn slips half an inch out of register, sending a blue echo ahead of the marching player.
system: Palette/material: translucent cyan, amber, and scarlet inks over mulberry-paper white, overlaps mixing to orange and violet, the drifting ghost pass marking live motion
Type/composition: stencil-cut poster caps in one procession banner line, registration crosses in the margins, figures massed as flat spot-color shapes on open paper
Topology/navigation: Move between complete procession, paper curtain, color pass, overlap event, registration mark, and drifting ghost figure.
Controls/state: Expose, pull, align, offset, and compare passes with separate, registered, overprinted, drifting, veiled, and complete states.
Responsive/motion: Stack the translucent curtains as explicit layers and pair every color mixture or offset with names, values, and patterns.
concepts.webLeverage: Direct manipulation of registered spot-color layers reveals how pass order and offset change both image and narrative, with every separation selectable and shareable.

concepts.form: a copperplate sentence written with one pointed nib, where hairlines and swelling shades make pressure visible as a continuous ribbon
concepts.lineage: English roundhand, pointed-pen calligraphy, and engraved copybooks
concepts.spark: The nib climbs in a silver hairline, turns, and descends under pressure into a black stroke broad enough to reflect the window.
system: Palette/material: iron-gall black on laid cream paper, hairlines thinning to silver gray at rest, the swelled full-pressure shade carrying the active stroke's weight
Type/composition: english roundhand at a constant steep slant, ascender and descender loops ruled to shared guidelines, one continuous joined line composing the page
Topology/navigation: Follow letter, stroke, word, line, and sentence while entry and exit joins preserve continuity.
Controls/state: Write, swell, lift, revise, and compare with hairline, shaded, joined, blotted, and corrected states.
Responsive/motion: Reflow by phrase without breaking stroke evidence and provide pressure curves beside the rendered hand.
concepts.webLeverage: Pointer pressure can drive variable stroke geometry while editable text and stroke data remain fully accessible.

concepts.form: a single illuminated initial growing into a margin of gold leaf, blue vine, beasts, and tiny narrative scenes, an inhabited threshold compressed into one letter
concepts.lineage: Medieval manuscript illumination, gilding, and historiated initials
concepts.spark: A red letter opens into a gold chamber; a blue vine escapes its stem, circles three lines of text, and ends in a fox playing a lute.
system: Palette/material: burnished gold leaf chambers on vellum cream, lapis blue vine as the wayfinding line, minium red initials marking every entry point into the text
Type/composition: one giant historiated initial outranking three lines of compact gothic bookhand, the margin composed as an inhabited frame around the measured text block
Topology/navigation: Enter through initial, branch, marginal figure, text passage, and referenced story while return remains obvious.
Controls/state: Open, trace, gloss, and compare with letter, ornament, scene, annotation, and restored states.
Responsive/motion: Turn the margin into a linked companion rail on phones and keep ornament optional to the reading path.
concepts.webLeverage: Deep vector zoom can connect minute marginal scenes to semantic text without loading separate pages.

concepts.form: a persian miniature page, interior and exterior held on one plane in stacked registers, figures at symbolic scale inside gold-ruled margins dense with ornament, text floating in calligraphic cartouches
concepts.lineage: Safavid and Mughal miniature ateliers, Herat school, Shahnameh manuscripts, Kamal ud-Din Behzad
system: Palette/material: lapis lazuli blue and vermilion over cream burnished paper, gold leaf ruling the margins, malachite green for the active pane, ink black for body text
Type/composition: nastaliq-voiced script held in bordered cartouches, headings as illuminated panels, the page split into simultaneous registers on one flat plane
Topology/navigation: interior and exterior views share one plane; sections stack as architectural registers and you step between rooms without perspective or depth
Controls/state: the selected register takes the gold-ruled border and full pigment saturation, resting panes fade toward the cream ground, actions sit in cartouches
Responsive/motion: registers restack into a single column with margins intact at narrow widths; motion is a slow gold shimmer on rule lines
concepts.spark: You lean over a Shahnameh page under lamplight, a battle filling the lower register and a palace garden above it on the same plane, gold margins glinting, a cartouche of nastaliq floating over the lapis sky.
concepts.webLeverage: css grid stacks simultaneous registers on one plane while svg draws the gold rule work and cartouche borders at any scale

concepts.form: a zoomorphic calligram, arabic script bent into a lion or a bird where the sentence is the image, diacritics turned to plumage, meaning discovered by tracing the line
concepts.lineage: Ottoman tughra composition, Persian and Sufi zoomorphic calligraphy, Bismillah lion and bird calligrams
system: Palette/material: dense black ink mass on aged cream paper, gold illumination dots as secondary marks, one deep saffron highlight tracing the phrase currently read
Type/composition: thuluth-weight strokes compose the figure itself, letterforms stretch to fill the animal silhouette, small annotations sit clear of the beast
Topology/navigation: the figure is the map; you navigate by following the baseline of the sentence through the body, entry at the first letter, exit at the tail
Controls/state: hovering a passage inks its stroke to full black while the rest of the figure thins to outline, the read path stays saffron behind you
Responsive/motion: the calligram scales as one object, annotations tuck below on narrow screens; motion draws the stroke along the reading path
concepts.spark: You trace a lion made entirely of a prayer, your finger following the baseline through the haunch and up the mane, diacritics scattering like feathers, and the sentence resolves only when you reach the tail.
concepts.webLeverage: svg path stroke-dashoffset animation draws the sentence through the figure, and pointer events on each segment expose the reading order

concepts.form: a chinese handscroll, painting and poem unrolling right to left through time, vermilion collector seals accumulating across centuries, colophons extending the work at its tail
concepts.lineage: Song and Ming handscroll painting, literati colophon culture, seal carving, Dong Qichang provenance chains
system: Palette/material: pale silk and mulberry paper ground, carbon ink washes for content, vermilion seal red reserved as the only accent, marking approvals and ownership
Type/composition: vertical columns of running script read right to left, poem and image sharing one horizontal band, colophons appended in later hands at the tail
Topology/navigation: one continuous horizontal band unrolls right to left; you see an arm's width at a time and position is felt as how much scroll remains rolled
Controls/state: acting on a passage stamps it with a vermilion seal that stays; history reads as accumulated seals and appended colophons, never as deletion
Responsive/motion: the band keeps its height and scrolls horizontally at every width; motion is the easing glide of silk unrolling
concepts.spark: You unroll a mountain slowly with both hands, mist giving way to a fisherman, then a poem in a collector's hand, then his red seal beside three older ones, each one a century of someone holding this same silk.
concepts.webLeverage: horizontal scroll-snap with sticky seal marks, and scroll-driven animation paces the unrolling of the ink washes

concepts.form: a busytown cross-section spread, a cutaway world where every building loses its wall, every vehicle its hull, and every object wears a small printed label, dozens of workers mid-task in one continuous gouache scene
concepts.lineage: Richard Scarry's Busytown books, Golden Books production, What Do People Do All Day cutaway spreads
system: Palette/material: cheerful gouache flats on paper white, brick red, school-bus yellow, and grass green in even midtones, a thin warm brown outline holding every shape
Type/composition: small roman labels beside every object with a hairline pointer, one hand-lettered headline per spread, constant scale so no label outranks another
Topology/navigation: one continuous scene pans edge to edge; entering a building slices its facade away as a cutaway, and roads carry you between districts
Controls/state: hover names anything with its printed label, busy items show a worker mid-task, and an opened building swings its wall aside while neighbors keep working
Responsive/motion: small screens frame one building at a time and pan along the road; motion is the facade swinging open like a dollhouse hinge
concepts.spark: You lie on the rug tracing a tiny car through a page where the bakery has no front wall, the flour sack says flour, and every fireman, pig, and pickle truck is busy doing exactly what its label promises.
concepts.webLeverage: svg cutaway layers toggle facades while css transforms pan one continuous labeled scene under pointer or touch

concepts.form: a Massin stage page, where a play's dialogue is typeset as performance: each voice its own face, shouts swelling across the spread, faces printed as inked stamps
concepts.lineage: Robert Massin's typographic staging of La Cantatrice Chauve and French expressive book design
concepts.spark: Two voices argue across the gutter in colliding sizes; her words print solid black and slightly angry, his dissolve letter by letter into the margin as he loses the point.
system: Palette/material: high-contrast black ink on white with occasional single-color voices; rough stamp-print portrait textures
Type/composition: one face per speaker with size carrying volume; lines bend, collide, and overlap by intent while captions stay calm
Topology/navigation: Move by scene, by speaker, and by outburst.
Controls/state: Follow a voice, mute a voice, and replay an exchange; emphasis changes scale, never color alone.
Responsive/motion: Dialogue enters in reading order with theatrical timing; narrow screens stack voices but keep their faces and angles.
concepts.webLeverage: Variable font axes as volume with the play rendered in semantic dialogue markup

concepts.form: an edo woodblock print coming together one color block at a time, the keyblock outline printed first and each pigment block registered against carved kento notches until the sheet is whole
concepts.lineage: Edo ukiyo-e publishing, keyblock and kento registration, bokashi gradient wiping, publisher and censor seals
system: Palette/material: mineral indigo, safflower red, and clove brown on warm kozo paper, each color a flat sealed area bounded by a black keyblock line
Type/composition: vertical title cartouches sit in the upper corners, publisher and censor seals cluster at one margin as small red furniture
Topology/navigation: the sheet builds in registered layers, so moving deeper adds a block rather than a page, and the keyline never moves
Controls/state: controls read as carved cartouches, an active state prints its color layer in, and an inactive one shows the keyline alone
Responsive/motion: narrow frames drop pigment blocks in reverse carving order, and motion is the soft bokashi wipe of one field into another
concepts.spark: the outline lands first in black, a ghost of a wave with nothing inside it. then indigo drops in, then safflower, each one nudged against a carved notch, and on the fifth pull the sea is suddenly deep enough to fall into.
concepts.webLeverage: layered svg color plates composited over one keyline, a css gradient wipe for bokashi, and progressive reveal of each registered block

concepts.form: a weekly magazine plate crowded with forty figures at a crush, every value in the scene made only from hatch density so the darkest passages are simply the most crossed, and the crowd dissolving to bare paper at the edges
concepts.lineage: weekly magazine pen-and-ink crowd illustration, crosshatch tonal drawing and engraved caption conventions, 1890 to 1910
system: Palette/material: one black ink on white rag paper, every value built from crossed line density alone, and no solid black anywhere in the plate
Type/composition: a fine old-style caption ruled beneath, forty figures crushed across the plate, and the crowd thinning to open paper at the margins
Topology/navigation: hatch density is the hierarchy, so navigation travels from the most crossed passages outward toward open paper
Controls/state: controls are figures, the active one gains a further crossing of hatch, and inactive ones thin toward outline
Responsive/motion: hatch rescales without ever becoming solid, and motion is a passage building density stroke by stroke
concepts.spark: forty people crushed into one plate, and the darkest part of the room is dark only because the pen went over it six times, with the crowd simply thinning into bare paper at the edges.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg crosshatch filter with density bound to interactive state, stroke-order build animation, and responsive hatch scaling

concepts.form: a classical album leaf mounted in a brocade border, a small painted scene held in enormous silk reserve, with collectors' seals accumulating in red along the mount and a colophon inscribed at one side
concepts.lineage: Song and Yuan album-leaf painting, silk mounting and brocade border craft, collectors' seal accumulation and colophon inscription
system: Palette/material: aged silk in oatmeal and pale celadon with ink and mineral pigment, cinnabar seals as the only saturated color anywhere
Type/composition: a small painted reserve set high inside a wide brocade mount, an inscribed colophon ranged at one side, seals clustered at the margins
Topology/navigation: the mount is mostly empty, so navigation moves between leaves and the seals record everyone who has looked
Controls/state: controls are seals, pressing one adds a cinnabar impression to the mount, and impressions accumulate permanently
Responsive/motion: the reserve holds its proportion while the mount absorbs the change, and motion is a seal pressing into the silk
concepts.spark: a painting the size of a postcard floating in an enormous silk mount, and around it in red, the seals of everyone who has owned it for eight hundred years, slowly crowding in.
concepts.webLeverage: a fixed-ratio reserve with responsive mount, accumulating seal state persisted local, and a press impression animation

concepts.form: an ink rubbing taken from a cast bronze vessel, the taotie mask and thunder-pattern ground lifted onto paper as white line on dense black, with a ruled scholar's annotation column set alongside
concepts.lineage: Chinese bronze vessel ink rubbing practice, Shang and Zhou taotie and leiwen ornament, antiquarian annotation and catalog printing
system: Palette/material: dense lampblack ink beaten into damp paper, forms reading as white line, with paper fiber breaking the black at every edge
Type/composition: a symmetrical mask centered on a vertical axis over a fine thunder-pattern ground, annotation ruled in a narrow side column
Topology/navigation: the ground is an all-over pattern and the mask is the landmark, so navigation moves between symmetrical registers
Controls/state: controls are register bands, the active one lifts to a cleaner white line, and inactive ones sink into the thunder ground
Responsive/motion: the thunder ground tiles at any size while the mask holds its axis, and motion is ink beaten gradually into paper
concepts.spark: a mask you cannot quite resolve into an animal, lifted off a bronze in white line against beaten black, floating on a ground of tiny squared spirals that goes on forever.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg pattern ground tiling responsive, a progressive ink-beat reveal animation, and register bands as navigation state

concepts.form: a machine-age journal plate, standardized objects photographed against white and ranged on a strict modular grid, with a numbered caption apparatus and a rigorous single-column argument running beside them
concepts.lineage: the L'Esprit Nouveau journal and its objet-type plates, machine-age purist publishing and modular page grids, 1920 to 1925
system: Palette/material: white ground with warm gray halftone and one ruled black, printed on smooth stock with generous unprinted margin
Type/composition: a single-column argument in a rational serif, objects ranged on a modular grid, and numbered captions ruled beneath each figure
Topology/navigation: the grid is the argument, so navigation moves figure by numbered figure and the text follows the same order
Controls/state: controls are figure numbers, the active one rules its caption open, and read figures drop to half-tone gray
Responsive/motion: the modular grid reflows in whole modules, and motion is a figure settling onto its module with no bounce
concepts.spark: a bottle, a pipe and a stack of plates, photographed against white and laid on a grid as if they were evidence, with numbered captions proving a point about civilization.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-module responsive grid, figure numbers as deep-linked state, and a settle animation with no easing overshoot

concepts.form: a bound book whose page edges hide a painted scene, invisible when the volume is closed and appearing only when the block is fanned to a precise angle, with gilding laid over the paint to conceal it completely
concepts.lineage: fore-edge painting, gilded page-block concealment and the fanned-angle reveal tradition
system: Palette/material: gold leaf over watercolor on the page block, so the closed edge reads as solid gilt and shows nothing at all
Type/composition: the hidden image spans the whole block and exists only across many edges at once, never on any single page
Topology/navigation: the image lives between states, so navigation is holding an angle rather than opening a page
Controls/state: controls are fan angles, the active angle resolves the picture, and any other angle returns solid gold
Responsive/motion: the reveal angle scales with block depth at any size, and motion is a continuous fan rather than a cut
concepts.spark: Closed it is a gold edge like any other book. Fan the pages to about thirty degrees and there is a harbor scene that was never on any page.
concepts.webLeverage: an angle-driven reveal bound to pointer state, canvas compositing across edge slices, and continuous fan motion

concepts.form: a painted narrative scroll unrolled one frame at a time while the painter sings the panel aloud, figures in flat saturated colour against bare paper with a hand-lettered caption band under each frame
concepts.lineage: Bengali patua scroll painting, Kalighat pat lineage, sung frame-by-frame narration and hand-lettered caption bands
system: Palette/material: earth red, indigo and turmeric yellow on joined paper backed with cloth, colours laid flat with a heavy dark contour and no shading
Type/composition: stacked frames of equal height read downward, each with a hand-lettered caption band beneath and figures filling the frame edge to edge
Topology/navigation: the scroll advances one frame at a time and cannot skip, so navigation is unrolling forward through a fixed narrative order
Controls/state: controls are frames, the active one unrolls into view with its caption, and passed frames roll away above
Responsive/motion: frames keep their height and crop their width, and motion is a continuous unroll paced like speech
concepts.spark: The painter unrolls one frame, sings what is in it, and only then lets you see the next one; the whole story is in her arms and it moves at the speed of her voice.
concepts.webLeverage: a scroll-driven frame sequence paced to audio, caption state per frame, and responsive cropping that preserves frame height

concepts.form: a printed ornament sheet issued for workshop copying, arabesque panels engraved at exact working size with a scale bar in the margin, sold so a goldsmith three cities away could cut the identical pattern
concepts.lineage: sixteenth-century Nuremberg printed ornament pattern sheets, engraved arabesque panels at working scale for workshop transfer
system: Palette/material: one engraving ink on laid paper with visible chain lines, every line a burin cut with no wash or tone anywhere
Type/composition: arabesque panels engraved at exact working size, ranged on the sheet with a scale bar and plate number in the margin
Topology/navigation: the sheet is a parts supply, so navigation selects a panel to copy rather than reading in an order
Controls/state: controls are panels, the active one shows its scale bar and dimensions, and copied panels take a small margin tick
Responsive/motion: panels reflow in whole units and the scale bar rescales truthfully, and motion is a burin line cutting itself
concepts.spark: Printed at exactly the size you were meant to cut it, with a scale bar in the margin, so that a workshop in another country could make the same thing without ever seeing the original.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg panel sheet with a truthful responsive scale bar, per-panel copy state, and burin-order line animation

concepts.form: a painted bookshelf screen where the shelves widen as they recede, objects rendered in reverse perspective so the far edge of every box is longer than the near one and the whole cabinet opens toward the viewer
concepts.lineage: Korean chaekgeori scholar's-possessions screen painting, reverse perspective construction and stacked shelf composition
system: Palette/material: mineral pigment on silk in muted malachite, cinnabar and bone white, with every object outlined and no cast shadow anywhere
Type/composition: a stacked grid of shelf boxes each drawn in reverse perspective, filled with books, brushes and vessels arranged as an inventory
Topology/navigation: the cabinet opens toward the viewer rather than receding, so navigation moves into a space that widens as it deepens
Controls/state: controls are shelf boxes, the active one widens further, and empty boxes show the painted back of the cabinet
Responsive/motion: the shelf grid reflows in whole boxes preserving the reverse construction, and motion is a box opening wider toward the viewer
concepts.spark: The back of every shelf is wider than the front, so the whole cabinet seems to be opening toward you rather than retreating, and it takes a while to work out why it feels wrong.
concepts.webLeverage: css 3d transforms building genuine reverse perspective, whole-box responsive shelf grid, and a widening open animation

concepts.form: a constructed script whose letters are built from a fixed set of strokes on a shared vertical spine, with a single composite emblem assembled from the same parts standing as the sign for a whole nation
concepts.lineage: the Soyombo constructed script and its composite national emblem, fixed stroke inventory and spine-hung letter construction
system: Palette/material: dense black ink on warm paper with one cinnabar red reserved for the emblem alone, and no other colour permitted
Type/composition: letters built from a closed stroke inventory hung on a common vertical spine, with the emblem assembled from the same parts at larger scale
Topology/navigation: everything is made from the same parts, so navigation recombines a fixed inventory rather than browsing new forms
Controls/state: controls are strokes, the active one joins the spine, and the assembled emblem takes the cinnabar
Responsive/motion: letterforms rebuild from the stroke set at any size, and motion is a letter assembling stroke by stroke on its spine
concepts.spark: Every letter is made from the same handful of strokes hung on one upright, and if you stack the right ones on top of each other you get the sign for the entire country.
concepts.webLeverage: svg letterforms composed from a shared stroke inventory, assembly animation on the spine, and a composite emblem built from the same parts

concepts.form: a newspaper set and printed on the ice by lamplight during a polar winter, hand-plates pulled from lithographic stones hauled south, with the compositor's errors left standing because there was no second chance
concepts.lineage: Antarctic expedition printing, hand-set type and lithographic plates produced in the field during polar winter
system: Palette/material: one black ink on damp-warped rag paper, plates pulled unevenly with visible pressure differences across each sheet
Type/composition: a small hand-set newspaper measure with a hand-drawn masthead and one lithographic plate tipped in per issue
Topology/navigation: issues appear at the pace conditions allow, so navigation moves by issue number through an irregular run
Controls/state: controls are issues, the active one shows its date and conditions, and uncorrected errors stay visible in the setting
Responsive/motion: the hand-set measure holds while margins crop, and motion is a plate pulling unevenly under hand pressure
concepts.spark: Set by hand in a hut in the dark, with the errors left in because there was no time and nowhere else to print it, three hundred miles from anyone.
concepts.webLeverage: a fixed hand-set measure with responsive margins, per-issue condition state, and an uneven hand-pull press animation

concepts.form: a hand-lettered birth record filled in by an itinerant schoolmaster, blackletter text ruled into a tulip and bird border, with the blanks for name and date left for a hand that arrives years later
concepts.lineage: Pennsylvania German fraktur illuminated records, itinerant schoolmaster lettering and tulip-and-bird border convention
system: Palette/material: iron gall ink on laid rag with watercolour in tulip red, indigo and yellow ochre, the colours pooling at the edges of each shape
Type/composition: a blackletter body block ruled inside a symmetrical border of tulips and facing birds, with blanks left for names and dates
Topology/navigation: the document is a fixed form with variable fields, so navigation moves between the same record filled differently
Controls/state: controls are fields, the active one accepts a later hand in a different ink, and unfilled fields keep their ruled line
Responsive/motion: the border reflows in whole motifs around a fixed body block, and motion is ink pooling as a field is filled
concepts.spark: Two different hands and two different inks on one sheet, thirty years apart, because the border was painted long before anyone knew whose birth it would record.
concepts.webLeverage: a fixed form with variable field state rendered in a distinct later hand, whole-motif responsive borders, and an ink-pool fill animation

concepts.form: an engraved owner plate pasted inside a cover, a personal device and a motto in Latin engraved at thumbnail size with detail no one will see without a glass, signed by an engraver nobody credits
concepts.lineage: ex libris bookplate engraving, personal device and motto convention and thumbnail-scale intaglio detail
system: Palette/material: one intaglio ink on a small pasted label, engraved with a density of line far beyond what the size can show unaided
Type/composition: a personal device centred with a motto on a ribbon beneath and the owner's name in engraved italic below that
Topology/navigation: the plate hides inside a cover, so navigation opens a book to find who owned it rather than browsing a shelf
Controls/state: controls are plates, the active one magnifies to reveal engraving detail, and later owners paste over earlier ones
Responsive/motion: the plate holds its true small size and magnifies on demand, and motion is a cover opening to reveal it
concepts.spark: Engraved at the size of a postage stamp with cross-hatching you physically cannot see without a magnifier, pasted where only the owner would ever look.
concepts.webLeverage: a true-scale plate with on-demand magnification revealing engraving density, layered ownership state, and a cover-open reveal

concepts.form: a stitched practice sheet working through alphabets and motif bands in order of difficulty, signed and dated at the foot by a child, the last band always looser than the first because she was learning as she went
concepts.lineage: needlework sampler practice, ordered alphabet and motif band progression and signed and dated completion
system: Palette/material: silk on loosely woven linen in madder, indigo and green, with the ground visible between stitches throughout
Type/composition: bands stacked in increasing difficulty, alphabets first, then motifs, then a scene, with a signature and date ruled at the foot
Topology/navigation: the sheet is chronological from top to bottom, so navigation descends through a skill developing in real time
Controls/state: controls are bands, the active one shows its technique, and later bands visibly loosen as the work goes on
Responsive/motion: bands reflow in whole rows while stitch scale holds, and motion is a band stitching in sequence
concepts.spark: The alphabet at the top is careful and even, and by the bottom of the cloth the stitches have gone loose and confident, and she signed it aged nine.
concepts.webLeverage: whole-row responsive bands with progressive looseness rendered per row, technique state per band, and sequential stitch animation

concepts.form: a printed software-manual page from a boxed product: a serif prose column banded off by nickel hairlines beside a redrawn figure cropped hard by the trim, the whole sheet ruled symmetrically about its binding spine and indexed by one colour tab that sticks out past the edge
concepts.lineage: the boxed-software printed manual at its peak, 1985 to 1993: Apple Macintosh manuals, Aldus and Adobe documentation in Sumner Stone's 1987 ITC Stone superfamily, and WordPerfect colour tabs
concepts.spark: A wire-bound manual open under a desk lamp, the vermilion tab of the section you are in sticking out past the trim, one keycap redrawn at eight times life size and running off the page edge, and nine lines of Stone Serif underneath explaining what the key does.
system: Palette/material: bone stock on signal-grey enamel, nickel hairlines. Nine index inks, one per surface as accent, the rest as fingernail tabs; accent fills, never type.
Type/composition: ITC Stone Serif 17/28 on a 62 to 70 measure, sole face under 24px; Stone Sans Semibold above, one element at 8x body cropped by trim. Ruled bands, one spine.
Topology/navigation: each surface belongs to one tab of the colour index. Only the tab rail breaks the trim; the current tab protrudes furthest and alone carries its ink.
Controls/state: one element per surface takes rank: hairline arm from the spine, display numeral, accent bar. Controls are struck plates: proud, flush pressed, engraved when off.
Responsive/motion: stepped registration onto detents, two or three frames of 90ms, nothing eased. Prose reflows to measure; figures crop, then drop to a numbered caption.
concepts.webLeverage: one --tab-ink property per section drives every accent; transitions run on steps(), no easing; the callout arm is an SVG path solved spine to element and re-solved on resize; figures crop with object-fit to a legibility floor

concepts.form: a reference-setting page drawn by a ruling engine, two short-measure text columns twinned around a fixed centre rail of keys, the whole block held small inside a wide annotation margin where the apparatus hangs and overlaps the block's edge
concepts.lineage: the centre-column reference setting perfected by the Oxford and Cambridge presses and by Bagster, 1810s to 1900s, and the same apparatus in wide-margin study editions and annotated statute books
concepts.spark: A wide-margin edition open under a lamp: two dense columns of small roman, a hairline channel of vermilion letter-keys running down between them, and four inches of bare paper all around where a previous reader has ruled one note and bracketed it back into the line it belongs to.
system: Palette/material: iron-black ink and one rubric vermilion on unbleached bone, three values only. A ruling engine draws every rule, bracket and detent at one device pixel.
Type/composition: Brevier body is Miller Text 17 to 19px on 1.5 leading, two columns of 34 to 40 characters round a 6 to 9 character rail. Pearl 11px small caps sets apparatus.
Topology/navigation: the centre rail is the one moving part, carrying keys and square detents cut wherever the flow changes footing. Global nav is a keyed list in the margin.
Controls/state: states are printed marks. A detent is hairline at rest, filled pressed, run through when disabled, bracketed on focus; spent is a struck bar. No radius anywhere.
Responsive/motion: the block holds its measure and the annotation margin absorbs width; under two columns the rail goes outboard. Motion is a damped single axis, no overshoot.
concepts.webLeverage: The ruling engine is real: a canvas or SVG layer reads live layout boxes and draws every hairline, detent and bracket at one device pixel, re-solving on resize and zoom. The lift relocates in-flow when the margin cannot hold it.

concepts.form: a literary quarterly's plain interior taken off the press and laid on a lit desk: cream laid leaves squared to the frame on a deep oltremare ground, one raking light throwing every shadow parallel, and a vermilion titling numeral forty times body size printed on the ground beneath them and running off the frame
concepts.lineage: Botteghe Oscure, Rome 1948 to 1960, Caetani's quarterly that set each contributor in their own language named in the margin, and Monotype's 1929 Bembo after Griffo's De Aetna roman
concepts.spark: an uncut signature of a quarterly lying on a blue-washed table under a low lamp, deckle showing along one edge, its shadow falling across a vermilion numeral printed on the table itself that runs off the table's edge
system: Palette/material: four colours only, deep oltremare ground, cream laid leaves, near-black ink, vermilion apparatus. The ground is procedural, chain and laid lines from a seed.
Type/composition: Bembo alone. Body 10.5/14 at 62 to 68 characters, justified; titling capitals from 8pt small caps to ground numerals at 40x. Examples set as verse, ranged left.
Topology/navigation: nothing touches the frame. Every element is a leaf on the ground, which shows on all four sides, and navigation lives in that margin in small caps.
Controls/state: a leaf turns in place to its verso; face down, blank back showing, means gone. Rank lifts a leaf: wider ground reserve, longer shadow, one vermilion rule beneath.
Responsive/motion: the measure is fixed, so width re-lays the leaves and the ground absorbs it. One drift: the wash migrates, the raking light swings every shadow off one angle.
concepts.webLeverage: One fragment shader draws the ground: laid mould, chain lines, deckle and pigment wash from a seed, on a clock publishing two custom properties, rake angle and shadow length, that every leaf's box-shadow reads.

concepts.form: a boxed-software reference manual lying open at a tabbed section, where the coloured divider board carries no mark at all and every paragraph, figure and keystroke sits on a punched acetate leaf hinged a millimetre above it, the whole book's extent drawn as a stepped tab rail down the fore edge
concepts.lineage: printed software reference manuals of the boxed era, 1984 to 1995: thumb-indexed ring-bound sets in the Adobe, Aldus and Lotus school, colour divider boards and bound-in acetate overlay plates
concepts.spark: A clear die-cut keyboard template lies across an open manual; its printed legends float above the chrome-yellow divider page beneath, two punch holes at its bound edge and one short hard shadow along its cut side.
system: Palette/material: milk acetate over a board of one section hue at full strength: oxide orange, chrome yellow, grass, teal, ultramarine, violet, sienna; vermilion held out.
Type/composition: one size does the work: Sabon 17/26 at a 62-character measure; Univers heads hang in the fifth margin column of a four-column grid, machine voice in mono.
Topology/navigation: a stepped tab rail down the fore edge, one tab per division, height proportional to extent, hue from the wheel; the current tab extends and is the board.
Controls/state: ply is the only rank, and only a top-ply leaf may be clear. Selected is a punched hole, disabled face-down, pending half-hinged, error a vermilion errata slip.
Responsive/motion: nothing eases or fades; every change is a 90ms two-frame step hinged at the punched edge. Width deals fewer leaves, four columns to two to one.
concepts.webLeverage: Solve leaf alpha at runtime: binary search sRGB source-over compositing against the board hue until the reading field lands in a fixed luminance band, then publish as a custom property. Hinges are steps(2) at 90ms; no easing curve anywhere.

concepts.form: a nineteenth-century lexicon page, black text set to a fixed measure with a shoulder margin down the outside, entries ranked by how much apparatus each one is granted rather than by size, guide words at the head naming the span you are inside, and every colour in the system quarantined inside a bordered plate
concepts.lineage: the scholarly nineteenth-century encyclopaedia: Meyers Konversations-Lexikon, Leipzig 1885 to 1890, and Britannica ninth, Edinburgh 1875 to 1889, chromolithographic plates among Scotch Roman text
concepts.spark: A lexicon lying open at a spread where a chromolithographed mineral plate in seven inks faces a column of black text set so tight that two entries touch, and two words at the top of the page name the first and the last thing you can reach without turning it.
system: Palette/material: engraving black on warm uncoated cream stock; colour only inside a bordered plate: vermilion, chrome yellow, emerald, ultramarine, madder rose, sepia, violet.
Type/composition: Miller Text at three sizes: body 16-17px on a 55-72 character measure, display 1.6 body, small 0.78. Twelve-unit module, two of shoulder, columns of five.
Topology/navigation: a head rule carries two guide words, the first and last item in view, recomputed as content passes; the shoulder a thumb index, current range struck through.
Controls/state: every control is a printed mark: a link closes in a solid arrow, pressed turns it down, visited takes a shoulder tick; rank is a hanging head plus a full rule.
Responsive/motion: columns are whole 55-72 character measures; extra width goes to the shoulder and the plates, never the line. Motion is a page passing, never a fade.
concepts.webLeverage: Guide words recomputed from the first and last entry in the viewport, column count derived from a character measure not breakpoints, plates as bordered figures for any foreign media, and a struck-and-replaced correction primitive.

concepts.form: a broadsheet's leader page as it stood on the paste-up flat, one type size from folio to standing head, waxed galleys overlapping on an endless press web while the reverse of the sheet ghosts through the stock under every one of them
concepts.lineage: the leader page of a Morison-era British broadsheet, The Times 1932 to 1966, set in the Linotype Legibility Group faces and composed on the wax paste-up flat
concepts.spark: A galley of the leading article lifted half off the flat under the bench lamp, wax still tacky along its edge, the reverse page reading backwards through the sheet in pale ink while a spot-blue rule runs on underneath it.
system: Palette/material: One press blue spot ink over a black key plate and warm newsprint; overlaps multiply and darken, a verso ghost runs beneath at five to eight percent ink
Type/composition: One size everywhere: Excelsior sets prose single column at 62 to 72, a tracked small-cap grotesque sets furniture, galleys overlap at small offsets
Topology/navigation: One endless press web, no page boundary, divided by rules; a standing rail at its leading edge carries the folio and small-cap marks, and moves are cuts
Controls/state: State is a proof mark, a small-cap slug in a hairline box that floods blue and reverses when set; emphasis widens the measure, floods, and tops the paste-up stack
Responsive/motion: Nothing scales, narrow viewports reflow and drop furniture columns; movement steps in whole baselines, a hard cut or a two-step stagger at 90ms, no easing
concepts.webLeverage: A verso layer renders the plane's reverse mirrored beneath every block at five to eight percent ink under mix-blend-mode multiply, masked to zero inside prose wells and foreign-media boxes, with scroll-snap set to the baseline unit.

families.label: Posters, Covers & Sleeves
families.description: Poster traditions, album and record sleeves, book jackets, and film title design: single-surface compositions engineered to seize attention and organize a whole through type, image, and grid.

concepts.form: an ecm records sleeve, a cold horizon photograph or near-empty field with a thin line of lowercase type floating in enormous quiet margin
concepts.lineage: ECM Records, Barbara Wojirsch and Dieter Rehm sleeve design, Manfred Eicher's Munich catalog
system: Palette/material: fog gray ground shading into sea slate, near-black ink for the single line of type, one cold horizon blue reserved for the active element
Type/composition: lowercase sans letterspaced wide, artist above title in two whispered lines, the margin ratio itself the compositional law
Topology/navigation: vast fields of emptiness with one small anchor per view; travel is a slow drift between horizons, never a jump
Controls/state: a single hairline of small type carries every state, present is dark, latent is fog gray, nothing ever grows louder than the field around it
Responsive/motion: margins compress before content ever does, preserving the emptiness ratio; motion is a long fade like weather
concepts.spark: A gray sea meets a grayer sky somewhere in the north, and a single line of small lowercase type hangs in the cold air like the last note of a piano left to decay.
concepts.webLeverage: IntersectionObserver paces the slow reveal of each horizon field as it enters the viewport.

concepts.form: a boxing fight poster, two names in slab caps colliding at a versus mark, faces mirrored in confrontation over a stacked undercard in shrinking type
concepts.lineage: Madison Square Garden fight bills, Ali-Frazier closed-circuit promotions, letterpress tune-up cards
system: Palette/material: newsprint cream ground, heavy black slab ink for the two names, one arena gold reserved for the versus mark and the live selection
Type/composition: condensed slab caps at collision scale, each name set to fill its half to the edge, date and venue in letterpress smalls beneath the mark
Topology/navigation: the sheet splits along a central versus axis, each half belongs to one opponent, everything else stacks beneath in ranked shrinking rows
Controls/state: any comparison becomes the two halves, the favored side's slab caps sit heavier, the undercard ranks the rest by type size alone
Responsive/motion: halves stack vertically on narrow frames with the versus mark as hinge; motion is a title-card punch-in
concepts.spark: Outside the arena in the rain, two heavyweight profiles glare across a gold VS while the undercard shrinks line by line into names only their mothers came to see.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS grid mirrors the two halves for any compare, with a draggable versus divider rebalancing them.

concepts.form: a fillmore psychedelic handbill, lettering melted into liquid ornament that fills every contour, vibrating complementary inks at maximum interference
concepts.lineage: Wes Wilson and Victor Moscoso, Fillmore and Avalon Ballroom handbills, Family Dog concerts
system: Palette/material: electric blue ground under hot orange lettering, the vibrating complementary pair reserved for what is active, calmer wine and moss at rest
Type/composition: one hand-drawn face per sheet, strokes swelling until counters nearly close, no straight baseline anywhere, the title the largest liquid mass
Topology/navigation: words become shapes that interlock like smoke filling a bottle, you read by tracing contours, and slow reading is designed in
Controls/state: the active element vibrates in complementary inks that fight at the boundary, resting elements settle into one calmer pair
Responsive/motion: the lettering mass re-melts to fill each new contour rather than reflowing lines; motion is a slow liquid breathe
concepts.spark: Outside the ballroom a kid tilts the handbill under a streetlamp, and the orange letters against electric blue seem to hum and crawl until the band name swims into focus.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG turbulence filters melt the lettering live, and prefers-reduced-motion freezes the liquid state.

concepts.form: a hatch show print letterpress gig poster, wood-type stacked in full-width bands where every line fills the measure and each ink pass lands a hair off-register
concepts.lineage: Hatch Show Print Nashville, 19th-century wood-type broadsides, country and rockabilly show bills
system: Palette/material: poster-stock cream ground, black wood-type ink beside one barn red and one deep blue run, the red pass reserved for the headline act
Type/composition: carved wood type stacked edge to edge, gothic condensed against slab and ornamented faces, every band forced to fill the full measure
Topology/navigation: one tall broadside of stacked horizontal bands, each line a full-width slab; the eye travels top to bottom through ranked type sizes
Controls/state: states are ink treatments, active is a solid overprint pass, disabled is a dry ghost impression, emphasis is a second color run slightly off-register
Responsive/motion: bands rewrap by swapping to condensed wood type at narrow widths; motion is a single press-pull, one clean stamp per change
concepts.spark: In a print shop that smells of kerosene and ink, a century of carved wood letters slams onto poster stock one color at a time, each pass a heartbeat off-register from the last.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS mix-blend-mode multiplies overprinted ink layers, and container queries swap each band to condensed wood type.

concepts.form: an ospaaal solidarity silkscreen, flat fearless color fields around one emblematic figure, the slogan repeated in four languages as a typographic border
concepts.lineage: OSPAAAL Havana, Cuban silkscreen posters, Tricontinental magazine inserts, Alfredo Rostgaard
system: Palette/material: flat silkscreen fields, hot red and sun yellow over a cream sheet, one saturated ink pass reserved for the emblem in focus
Type/composition: bold geometric sans set solid, the slogan repeated in spanish, english, french, and arabic, letterforms cut as flat shapes like the figure
Topology/navigation: a centered emblem commands the sheet while a running multilingual frame carries the message around all four edges
Controls/state: state is a screen pull, each change adds or removes one flat color layer, urgency stacks hot layers, calm strips back to two inks
Responsive/motion: the emblem holds center at any ratio and the language border rewraps its four texts; motion is a squeegee wipe per layer
concepts.spark: In a Havana workshop a folded poster slips inside a magazine and unfurls across three continents, one raised fist printed in colors bold enough to survive any wall.
concepts.webLeverage: Canvas compositing simulates screen-pull layers, adding one flat ink at a time in real-time.

concepts.form: a pelican paperback jacket on the marber grid, color-coded band up top and a witty conceptual image locked into the lower two-thirds
concepts.lineage: Romek Marber's Penguin Crime grid, Penguin and Pelican Books, Germano Facetti art direction
system: Palette/material: off-white stock and black text ink under penguin crime green and pelican blue bands, the ground stays paper while color lives in the band
Type/composition: quiet grotesk locked to the marber grid, horizontal rules dividing publisher, title, and image fields, type never trespassing into the image
Topology/navigation: every jacket shares one grid, horizontal rules divide publisher band, title band, and image field, so a shelf of many reads as one system
Controls/state: series membership is a color band, states recolor the band while type and rules never move; only the image field is allowed to surprise
Responsive/motion: the grid is proportional, bands keep their ratios from thumbnail to full spread; motion is a shelf slide between jackets
concepts.spark: On a spinning wire rack, forty crime paperbacks in the same green livery each hide one sly visual joke below the rule line, a whole library disguised as a pattern.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS custom properties swap the series band color per category while the grid template stays computed and fixed.

concepts.form: a polish film poster, one painted surreal metaphor swallowing the whole sheet, hand-lettered title bent to fit the image's anatomy
concepts.lineage: Polish School of Posters, Jan Lenica, Franciszek Starowieyski, Wiktor Górka, CYRK prints
system: Palette/material: feverish gouache on cheap poster stock, bruise violet and blood crimson over muddy ochre, the hottest red reserved for the element in focus
Type/composition: hand-lettered strokes sharing the brush of the painting, the title bent to the figure's anatomy, no grid and no typeface anywhere
Topology/navigation: one metaphorical image per sheet is the entire territory, secondary matter rides inside the image's own contours rather than beside it
Controls/state: moods change by repainting the metaphor, a warning is a wound in the image, success blooms out of it; lettering flexes to follow the new anatomy
Responsive/motion: the image composes around one dominant axis that survives any crop; motion is paint bleeding into paper
concepts.spark: Behind the Iron Curtain a cabaret dancer's face dissolves into a wolf's, painted in feverish gouache, because the censor read words but never learned to read pictures.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG clip-paths let hand-lettered titles flow along the painted figure's contours at any size.

concepts.form: a pulp paperback rack, lurid painted covers jostling spine-out and face-out, each promising doom in three tiers of breathless cover lines
concepts.lineage: 1940s-50s pulp paperbacks, Popular Library and Dell mapbacks, Robert McGinnis cover painting
system: Palette/material: night-blue painted scenes under taxi yellow and lipstick red cover lines, cheap ivory pulp stock as ground, red reserved for the chosen cover
Type/composition: brush script over condensed gothic caps, cover lines breaking into italics for the promise of doom, the painting always owning the center
Topology/navigation: a wire rack of pockets, most items show spines and chosen ones turn face-out, browsing is spinning tiers rather than scanning lists
Controls/state: attention promotes a spine to a full painted cover, the three-tier cover-line stack ranks hook, title, and dread in fixed positions
Responsive/motion: narrow widths show one face-out and a fan of spines, wide shows the whole carousel; motion is the rack's squeaky spin
concepts.spark: In a drugstore corner the wire rack creaks around, and every turn faces out another painted blonde, another smoking gun, another promise that this one ends badly.
concepts.webLeverage: 3D CSS transforms spin the rack's tiers, with scroll-snap landing each pocket face-out.

concepts.form: a saul bass title sequence, cut-paper shapes and a single jittering line building meaning across timed cards on a flat color field
concepts.lineage: Saul Bass, The Man with the Golden Arm, Anatomy of a Murder, Vertigo title work
system: Palette/material: one flat saturated field per card, burnt orange, ink black, and bone white, the field color swapping per act while silhouettes stay black
Type/composition: skinny hand-set caps sitting slightly off baseline, one idea per card in hard asymmetry, credits ranked as timed cards rather than columns
Topology/navigation: a timed sequence of full-bleed cards, one idea per card; jumping ahead scrubs the sequence rather than abandoning it
Controls/state: everything is a cut-paper symbol, states change by swapping the silhouette rather than decorating it; a jittery hand-drawn line marks the live element
Responsive/motion: shapes are flat and scale-free so cards recompose at any width; motion is staccato paper-cut jumps
concepts.spark: A black cut-paper arm reaches across a burnt-orange field while brass stabs, and in ninety seconds of jittering silhouettes an entire story is told without showing a single face.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG shape morphs animate the paper-cut swaps, with scroll-driven animation timelines advancing each card.

concepts.form: a stenberg brothers film poster, photomontage figures at impossible diagonals, perspective faked by scale jumps and type racing along the tilt
concepts.lineage: Vladimir and Georgii Stenberg, Soviet constructivist cinema posters, Sovkino advertising sheets
system: Palette/material: sovkino red and coal black over unprinted cream, gray halftone photomontage flesh at rest, flat red serving as both alarm and accent ink
Type/composition: constructivist sans caps racing along the tilt, letters wedged into the composition as if built from it, the diagonal is the baseline
Topology/navigation: one violent diagonal organizes the sheet, elements gain importance by scale jump rather than position, the tilt is the reading order
Controls/state: a state change re-tilts the axis, alarm steepens the diagonal and jumps the key figure two scales up, calm settles toward the horizontal
Responsive/motion: the diagonal re-angles to each frame's proportions while scale ratios hold; motion is a lurching montage cut
concepts.spark: A cameraman's giant face looms over a sprinting figure a tenth his size while red letterforms tumble down the tilt, the whole cinema screaming from a single silent sheet.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS transforms drive the diagonal composition, with view transitions cutting between montage states.

concepts.form: a wpa national-park travel poster, a landscape flattened into stacked silkscreen planes with a ranger-voiced imperative set in blocky caps below
concepts.lineage: WPA Federal Art Project posters, See America series, Ranger Naturalist Service silkscreens
system: Palette/material: four flat silkscreen inks, one unbroken teal sky swath over pine green and canyon ochre planes, cream stock showing through as the light
Type/composition: blocky geometric caps in a caption bar beneath the scene, one imperative per sheet, the landscape composed above it and never interrupted
Topology/navigation: the scene layers into foreground, midground, and sky planes; deeper subjects live on deeper planes and travel is walking into them
Controls/state: each state is a season of the same scene, inks reshuffle from summer to snow while plane edges never move, the caption bar states one imperative
Responsive/motion: planes crop from the outside in so the summit always survives; motion is gentle plane parallax
concepts.spark: From a canvas tent at dawn you see the geyser rendered in four flat inks, the sky one unbroken swath of teal, and beneath it two words in block caps: SEE AMERICA.
concepts.webLeverage: Layered SVG planes parallax under pointer and scroll, each plane a separate flat-ink shape.

concepts.form: a silent-era intertitle card, hand-lettered dialogue on soft black inside an ornamented frame, the whole print tinted amber for lamplight and blue for night, iris circles opening and closing every scene of the picture
concepts.lineage: 1920s silent film intertitles, Weimar and Hollywood art title departments, nitrate tinting conventions
system: Palette/material: soft black card grounds with cream lettering, scene tints washing the whole frame, amber for interiors, blue for night, rose for romance, grain over everything
Type/composition: hand-lettered dialogue centered with generous margins, corner flourishes matched to the picture's mood, quotation dashes for speech and spaced caps for narration
Topology/navigation: cards alternate with scenes; narration cards set the chapters, dialogue cards carry the voices, and an iris opens each new place from one point of interest
Controls/state: the current mood tints every element at once, emphasis earns a larger lettered card of its own, and a held card lingers exactly as long as it takes to read twice
Responsive/motion: cards were made for small frames and simply scale; motion is iris in, iris out, and the faint dance of grain
concepts.spark: the piano vamps, the frame irises down to her hand on the doorknob, and the card cuts in on black, fancy letters trembling slightly, telling you what he never had the courage to say aloud
concepts.webLeverage: css clip-path irises drive the scene transitions while tint states recolor the whole page through blend modes

concepts.form: a sonidero dance poster, fluorescent inks stacked line on line over black, every sound system billed in a different color and size, dates and barrio venues shouting in condensed caps, stapled to the light pole in multiples
concepts.lineage: Mexico City sonidero and baile posters, fluorescent-stock offset printing, cumbia sound-system billing culture
system: Palette/material: matte black ground with fluorescent pink, acid green, and blaze orange inks alternating line by line, white held for the small print and fine rules
Type/composition: ultra-condensed caps stacked edge to edge, each act sized by billing, the headline name arched or slanted, date and venue locked in a boxed bottom band
Topology/navigation: the sheet reads top to bottom as a bill; headliners first, then the stack, then the venue block, and repeat posting turns one message into a wall
Controls/state: the featured line burns brightest with a blacklight flicker, past dates take a diagonal overprint strip, and picking any line pulls its full listing forward
Responsive/motion: the stack condenses its letterforms to fit before it ever breaks a line; motion is a blacklight pulse on the headline only
concepts.spark: On a concrete pole at dusk the same poster repeats five times, fluorescent pink and green stacked to the edges, and the headline name arcs across all five in letters you can read from the moving bus.
concepts.webLeverage: variable font width axes condense each line to exact measure while css blend modes make fluorescent inks glow on black

concepts.form: an Ikko Tanaka poster, where a face or figure is rebuilt from a few flat geometric planes of color and the grid quietly does the rest
concepts.lineage: Ikko Tanaka's Nihon Buyo posters and Japanese graphic modernism
concepts.spark: Five colored shapes on a quiet grid suddenly become a dancer's face; the eye is one red semicircle, and removing any single plane collapses the whole person.
system: Palette/material: calm paper ground carrying a small set of confident flat planes in vermilion, indigo, gold, and black; no outlines anywhere
Type/composition: minimal grotesk locked to the same grid that places the planes; monumental figure, whisper-quiet caption
Topology/navigation: Move by figure, by plane, and by series.
Controls/state: Compose, remove, and swap planes; focus names what each plane is doing for the figure.
Responsive/motion: Planes glide to recompose the figure per aspect ratio; the figure never scales below recognizability.
concepts.webLeverage: Layered CSS and SVG planes recomposing responsively while remaining one semantic figure

concepts.form: a Designers Republic sleeve, where pseudo-corporate roundels, hazard sans, faux-kanji, and registration marks compose hostile-brand information noise that is itself immaculate branding
concepts.lineage: The Designers Republic's Sheffield studio work for Warp and the WipEout era of anti-corporate corporate design
concepts.spark: A magenta target grid locks over black; warning glyphs, barcode fragments, and a fake product code crowd the edge while one enormous condensed word shouts through the noise.
system: Palette/material: magenta, safety orange, and white on absolute black, flat print surfaces with no gradients; density itself is the material
Type/composition: condensed hazard grotesk in stacked lockups, faux-kanji and registration marks as ornament, everything gridded tight to the edge
Topology/navigation: Move by product code, by roundel family, and by warning class.
Controls/state: Stamp, register, and certify; active states add another layer of official-looking marks.
Responsive/motion: Density reflows by dropping ornament layers in declared steps; the one shouting word never shrinks.
concepts.webLeverage: Layered SVG mark systems with density tiers driven by container queries

concepts.form: a hand-lettered record sleeve, where a beaming bandleader portrait floats in tropical color under an exuberant painted band name
concepts.lineage: West African highlife and Afro-funk album sleeves, Ghanaian and Nigerian pressings, 1960s to 1970s
concepts.spark: A bandleader grins from a cut-out portrait against a wall of mango orange and palm green. The band name arcs overhead in fat hand-brushed letters, each one outlined twice, drop-shadowed once, and packed cheek to cheek.
system: Palette/material: Saturated tropical color, mango, palm green, sky, and hibiscus red, on warm cream board
Type/composition: Exuberant hand-brushed display lettering, double-outlined and shadowed, arcing across the top; a smaller sans for track lists below
Topology/navigation: Move by release title, by bandleader portrait, and by side and track.
Controls/state: Flip, cue, and credit; selecting a track brightens its row and lifts the sleeve portrait forward over its color field.
Responsive/motion: The arced title reflows to a straight stacked banner on narrow screens; reduced-motion swaps sleeves with a plain cross-fade.
concepts.webLeverage: Set the arced band name on an SVG textPath and layer double outlines with paint-order stroke, so the hand-lettered headline stays crisp at any size.

concepts.form: a berlin poster house's trade-mark wall, the same product redrawn as a flat emblem across a dozen sheets, each sheet a different saturated ground with the brand word cut from one custom alphabet
concepts.lineage: Lucian Bernhard's Berlin object-poster program, its custom cut alphabet and color-coded trade-mark series, Hollerbaum und Schmidt, 1906 to 1920
system: Palette/material: each sheet one saturated ground from a fixed house set of ox-blood, mustard, moss and slate, the object cut from a single contrasting solid
Type/composition: a custom alphabet with fat slab terminals, the brand word locked beneath a heroic flat object, and the ground carrying no ornament at all
Topology/navigation: the wall is the map, so navigation moves between grounds and each ground is a different product in the same house voice
Controls/state: controls are object emblems, the active one swaps its ground to the house accent, and inactive ones hold their assigned color
Responsive/motion: sheets retile in whole units and objects never scale below legibility, and motion is a hard ground swap with no fade
concepts.spark: a wall of a dozen sheets, each one a different saturated ground, each carrying one object drawn flat and huge, and every brand word cut from the same alphabet nobody else was allowed to use.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-unit responsive sheet wall, ground color swapped as a css custom property, and hard cuts between poster states

concepts.form: a penny-press broadside where relief-engraved skeletons act out the day's news, the image band across the top and dense verse set in two hard columns beneath it
concepts.lineage: Jose Guadalupe Posada's calaveras for Antonio Vanegas Arroyo's Mexico City penny press, 1890 to 1913
system: Palette/material: coarse newsprint in a single black relief ink, with one alarm color flooded behind the image band on holiday sheets only
Type/composition: a shouting headline in mixed wood-type sizes tops the sheet, the engraving band sits below it, and verse fills two justified columns
Topology/navigation: the sheet is one continuous cry, so navigation is by broadside rather than by section, each new sheet replacing the last
Controls/state: controls are wood-type words with rule underlines, pressed states ink heavier, and read sheets fade toward the paper tone
Responsive/motion: the two columns collapse to one and the image band goes full width, while motion is the judder of a hand-fed press
concepts.spark: skeletons in feathered hats parade across the top of a cheap sheet, grinning at a scandal, and underneath them the verse is rammed into two columns so tight the press left ink on your thumb.
concepts.webLeverage: css multi-column verse that collapses responsive, svg relief line art, and a print-judder motion on state change

concepts.form: a double-feature exploitation one-sheet, two titles shouting at different scales over a collage of clipped scenes, hand-lettered shock lines wedged into every gap and a dense billing block anchoring the foot
concepts.lineage: 1970s grindhouse and drive-in one-sheets, combo bills, hand-lettered ballyhoo and rating-strip conventions
system: Palette/material: blaring process yellow and blood red over black, cheap misregistered offset on thin stock, halftone dots left visible
Type/composition: a huge distressed display title, a second title half its size, hand-lettered promises angled into the gaps, agate billing at the foot
Topology/navigation: the sheet is a shouting hierarchy, so navigation is by billing rank and every new view rebills the same cast
Controls/state: controls are angled ballyhoo tags, pressing one flares its outline, and spent items drop into the agate block below
