Responsive/motion: the second title stacks under the first as frames narrow, and motion is a hard misregistered jolt in two inks
concepts.spark: two titles fighting for the same sheet, a woman screaming in a clipped oval, four hand-lettered promises jammed into the corners, and at the bottom a wall of agate nobody was ever meant to read.
concepts.webLeverage: css blend modes for misregistration, a live billing-rank sort of the agate block, and angled tag reveal on pointer state

concepts.form: a workshop linocut broadside cut for a strike or a literacy campaign, monumental figures gouged from black with white chisel strokes, a slab of demand lettering carved into the same block
concepts.lineage: Taller de Grafica Popular linocut broadsides, Mexico City workshop printing, Leopoldo Mendez, 1937 onward
system: Palette/material: one black relief ink on cheap manila or newsprint, all modeling made by the width and direction of the gouge
Type/composition: demand lettering carved into the block itself in heavy irregular caps, the figure filling three quarters of the sheet from below
Topology/navigation: each sheet is one demand, so navigation moves between demands rather than through them, always at the same low angle
Controls/state: controls are carved lettering blocks, pressing one floods it solid black, and inactive ones stay as outline gouges
Responsive/motion: the figure crops from the edges inward and never scales down, and motion is a single heavy press impression
concepts.spark: a fist and a forearm gouged out of black lino, seen from below so they fill the sheet, and the words underneath were cut with the same knife into the same block by somebody in a hurry.
concepts.webLeverage: svg gouge-textured artwork, a press-impression animation on control state, and edge-crop responsive behavior

concepts.form: a peruvian dance poster screenprinted in fluorescent inks on black, bulging outlined lettering swelling to fill every centimeter, band names ranked by size and a fringe of dates crammed along the foot
concepts.lineage: Peruvian chicha concert posters, Lima screenprint workshops, fluorescent ink on black stock, 1980s onward
system: Palette/material: fluorescent magenta, orange and green screened flat on black stock, colors chosen to vibrate against each other rather than harmonize
Type/composition: bulging outlined display letters swelling into the space they are given, billing ranked strictly by size, dates crammed as a foot fringe
Topology/navigation: the sheet fills completely, so navigation is by billing rank and a new event simply re-ranks the same crowded field
Controls/state: controls are outlined name blocks, the active one gains a second fluorescent outline, and past dates drop to a flat green
Responsive/motion: letters swell or contract to keep the field full at any width, and motion is a fluorescent pulse across the ranking
concepts.spark: magenta and green screaming at each other off pure black, letters swollen until there is not one millimeter of spare paper, and the headliner is simply the biggest thing on the sheet by a factor of four.
concepts.webLeverage: svg text that swells responsive to fill its box, a css fluorescent pulse animation, and live billing-rank state

concepts.form: a southern rap cd cover built in a photo editor with every filter on, the artist composited onto a mansion lawn with beveled chrome lettering, lens flares, and diamonds dropped onto every available surface
concepts.lineage: the Houston studio that made Southern rap CD covers, beveled chrome type and composited excess, 1992 to 2003
system: Palette/material: high-gloss chrome and gold bevels over saturated composited photography, purple and green flares laid on top of everything
Type/composition: an enormous beveled chrome title arced across the top, a subtitle in matching gold, and small composited elements filling every gap
Topology/navigation: nothing is subtracted, so navigation adds another element to the composite rather than replacing the current one
Controls/state: controls are chrome plates, the active one throws a lens flare, and inactive ones sit at lower bevel depth
Responsive/motion: elements re-composite to fill any frame, and motion is a slow flare travel across the chrome
concepts.spark: a mansion, a tiger, a helicopter, and the artist standing in front of all three, with the title bevelled in chrome so heavy it has its own weather. nothing was ever removed from this image.
concepts.webLeverage: css gradient bevels with a shader flare pass, responsive composite layering, and pointer-driven highlight travel

concepts.form: a hand-drawn cassette j-card for a bedroom project, a small ink keep or forest crosshatched onto photocopied stock, the project name inked in a cramped blackletter and the tracklist hand-numbered down the spine
concepts.lineage: the hand-drawn dungeon synth cassette j-card tradition, photocopied sleeve craft and bedroom tape labels, 1993 onward
system: Palette/material: photocopy gray on off-white card, one ink weight only, contrast lost and regained through generations of copying
Type/composition: a cramped hand-inked blackletter title over a small crosshatched scene, tracklist hand-numbered vertically down the narrow spine
Topology/navigation: the object folds, so navigation is unfolding the j-card panel by panel rather than moving through a page
Controls/state: controls are numbered tracks, the active one gains a hand-inked bracket, and played ones fade a photocopy generation
Responsive/motion: panels unfold in order at any width, and motion is a paper fold with a slight copy-machine jitter
concepts.spark: a tower on a hill, crosshatched by hand at about two centimeters across, photocopied four times until the ink went soft, and a tracklist numbered down the spine in handwriting that gets smaller near the end.
concepts.webLeverage: css fold transitions per panel, an svg crosshatch filter with generational degradation state, and vertical spine reflow

concepts.form: a painted martial-arts film hoarding, a swordsman frozen mid-leap against a wash of cloud and mountain, brush-drawn title characters stacked vertically and the cast billed in a hand-lettered lower band
concepts.lineage: Hong Kong wuxia film poster painting, Shaw Brothers and King Hu publicity art, painted hoarding studios, 1966 to 1980
system: Palette/material: painted cinnabar and ink-wash mountain over a bleached sky, with gold reserved for the title strokes and blade highlights
Type/composition: a stacked vertical title on the right, the figure leaping across the upper two thirds, and a hand-lettered billing band at the foot
Topology/navigation: the frame is a single held moment, so moving means cutting to the next held moment rather than panning within one
Controls/state: controls are billing lines, the active one takes a gold stroke, and the rest stay in flat cinnabar
Responsive/motion: the cloud wash crops and the figure holds scale, and motion is a hard cut with a brief blade highlight
concepts.spark: a swordsman caught at the top of a leap he will never finish, cloud washed in behind him, and the title painted down the right edge in strokes that clearly came off a real brush.
concepts.webLeverage: css writing-mode vertical titles, an svg blade highlight animation on state, and responsive crop of the wash background

concepts.form: a record sleeve dressed as an old educational paperback, a small collaged occult woodcut inside a fixed series frame, catalogue number and series band printed exactly where a public library edition would put them
concepts.lineage: the hauntology label sleeve program, mid-century educational paperback series framing, collaged woodcut and library catalogue furniture
system: Palette/material: faded institutional green and oxblood on aged paperback stock, one collaged halftone woodcut, and no photograph anywhere
Type/composition: a fixed series frame with a rule at head and foot, the title in a modest transitional serif, catalogue number set small at one corner
Topology/navigation: the world is a numbered series, so navigation moves along catalogue numbers rather than through categories
Controls/state: controls are catalogue entries, the active one takes the series band color, and unreleased numbers print as a blank frame
Responsive/motion: the series frame holds its proportion at any width, and motion is a slow tape-speed drift as a title settles
concepts.spark: it looks exactly like a paperback about British birds from 1968, until you notice the woodcut in the middle is of something that is not a bird, and the catalogue number is impossible.
concepts.webLeverage: a fixed-ratio responsive series frame, catalogue number as url state, and a tape-drift settle animation between titles

concepts.form: an underground theatre poster silkscreened in clashing flat color, a rising-sun ray burst behind collaged photographic heads, hand-drawn troupe lettering crammed into a border of dates and prices
concepts.lineage: Japanese angura underground theatre poster art, Tadanori Yokoo silkscreen work, 1960s to 70s troupe billing sheets
system: Palette/material: flat screened vermilion, jade and cadmium yellow on white, printed dense enough that the inks sit slightly proud of the sheet
Type/composition: hand-drawn troupe lettering at the head, a ray burst radiating from one off-center point, dates and prices packed into a ruled border
Topology/navigation: rays fan from a single origin, so navigation follows a ray outward to its billing rather than descending a list
Controls/state: controls are border cells, the active one floods vermilion, and past dates print as a struck rule inside the cell
Responsive/motion: the burst re-radiates from its origin at any aspect, and motion is a ray sweeping around the origin point
concepts.spark: rays firing out from a point somewhere off to the left, three photographic heads pasted into the middle of them, and every last centimeter of the border packed with dates in lettering somebody drew by hand at two in the morning.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg ray burst that re-radiates responsive, border cells as navigation state, and a sweeping ray animation on transition

concepts.form: a jamaican dance poster screened on fluorescent card, sound names ranked in outlined block caps with the venue struck across the middle and a hand-ruled grid of dates filling the lower third
concepts.lineage: Jamaican soundsystem dance posters, Kingston screenprint shops, sound clash billing and fluorescent card stock
system: Palette/material: fluorescent yellow and pink card with black and one screened spot, ink laid heavy so edges bleed slightly into the stock
Type/composition: outlined block caps ranked by sound rather than by act, the venue struck across the center, dates hand-ruled into a lower grid
Topology/navigation: the bill is a ranking, so navigation moves between sounds by billing weight rather than by category
Controls/state: controls are sound names, the active one gains a second outline and drop, and past dances rule through
Responsive/motion: block caps rescale to hold the ranking at any width, and motion is a heavy screened drop landing under the type
concepts.spark: four sound names stacked by who is bigger, outlined twice each, the venue struck right across the middle of them, and a hand-ruled grid of dates underneath on card the color of a warning sign.
concepts.webLeverage: responsive svg block lettering that holds billing rank, a screened drop animation on state, and live date-grid filtering

concepts.form: a postwar crime film one-sheet worked in two inks, a figure thrown as a long hard shadow across a painted street, the title set in condensed caps and the billing block ruled tight beneath
concepts.lineage: American crime film one-sheets and lobby card sets of 1944 to 1955, duotone poster printing and studio billing conventions
system: Palette/material: a hard duotone of ink black and one sour amber on cream stock, all modeling done by shadow shape rather than by tone
Type/composition: condensed caps for the title, a figure placed small against a large shadow, and a ruled billing block locked to the foot
Topology/navigation: the shadow points, so navigation follows the direction a cast shadow throws rather than a menu order
Controls/state: controls are billing lines, the active one takes the amber, and spent ones recede into the black
Responsive/motion: the shadow re-casts to any aspect and the figure holds scale, and motion is a light source swinging the shadow across
concepts.spark: the man is small and the shadow he throws is four times his size and going the wrong way up a wall, and the title sits in condensed caps like a charge being read out.
concepts.webLeverage: css and svg cast shadows recomputed responsive, a light-source animation swinging the shadow, and billing state in amber

concepts.form: a madrid scene magazine cover after the dictatorship, a flash-lit portrait cropped hard under a hand-inked masthead, cover lines scattered at angles in three fluorescent inks with no grid holding them
concepts.lineage: the Movida Madrileña scene press and its poster art, Madrid magazine and comic illustration, 1977 to 1985
system: Palette/material: fluorescent pink, acid green and black over white, printed cheap so the inks misregister at every edge
Type/composition: a hand-inked masthead, a flash-lit portrait cropped past the frame, and cover lines set at four different angles with no shared baseline
Topology/navigation: the cover is a scatter, so navigation is picking a cover line out of the noise rather than reading in order
Controls/state: controls are cover lines, the active one flips to acid green, and read ones drop to black
Responsive/motion: cover lines re-scatter without ever aligning, and motion is a misregistered ink shift on selection
concepts.spark: a face cropped so hard it loses the chin, a masthead somebody inked by hand that afternoon, and six cover lines thrown across it at angles chosen by nobody in particular.
concepts.webLeverage: css transforms scattering cover lines responsive, a misregistration shift animation on state, and read state in local storage

concepts.form: a french house label sleeve, a direct-flash party photograph defaced with a fat marker scrawl, the label logo redrawn by hand over the image and a fluorescent sticker slapped across one corner
concepts.lineage: the Paris electro label sleeve and flyer program of 2005 to 2010, flash photography defaced with marker logo vandalism
system: Palette/material: blown flash photography with crushed shadows, one fluorescent marker color scrawled over it, and a white sticker stock corner
Type/composition: a hand-scrawled logo sitting directly on the photograph, small pressed-type credits at the foot, and a sticker breaking one corner
Topology/navigation: the sleeve is a defaced surface, so navigation adds another mark rather than opening a clean new view
Controls/state: controls are scrawl marks, the active one is redrawn heavier, and used ones stay on the surface as history
Responsive/motion: scrawls redraw to fit any crop, and motion is a marker stroke laid down at speed
concepts.spark: somebody took a flash photo of a room at four in the morning and then drew the label logo straight over the top of it in marker, badly, on purpose, and slapped a sticker in the corner.
concepts.webLeverage: svg marker paths drawn with stroke animation, persistent defacement state, and responsive scrawl repositioning

concepts.form: a barcelona cafe poster where the figures are cut as flat silhouettes and the unprinted paper between them does the drawing, a swelling hand-lettered name arcing over the negative shape they leave
concepts.lineage: Ramon Casas and the Barcelona modernista poster, Quatre Gats sheets and Catalan lithographic printing, 1890 to 1910
system: Palette/material: three lithographic inks in olive, oxblood and cream, with unprinted paper carrying as much of the image as any printed area
Type/composition: hand-lettered organic caps arcing over the composition, figures cut as flat silhouettes, and the shape between them treated as a form in its own right
Topology/navigation: negative shapes are the paths, so navigation moves through the gaps between figures rather than around them
Controls/state: controls are silhouette shapes, the active one fills oxblood, and inactive ones read only as the paper they exclude
Responsive/motion: silhouettes re-cut and the negative shape between them is preserved, and motion is a flat area filling from one edge
concepts.spark: two figures cut flat in olive and oxblood, and the shape of the bare paper trapped between them is better drawn than either of them, with the cafe name arcing over the top of the gap.
concepts.webLeverage: svg silhouette shapes re-cut responsive with preserved negative space, directional fill animation, and gap-aware layout

concepts.form: a shelf of crime novel jackets from one imprint, every spine and band identical across forty numbered titles, with only the single flat clue object in the center changing from a candlestick to a timetable to a torn glove
concepts.lineage: British between-the-wars detective fiction jackets and crime club series imprints, two-color jacket printing and numbered series conventions
system: Palette/material: two flat inks in bottle green and vermilion on cream jacket stock, every title printed identically so only the clue object differs
Type/composition: a ruled imprint band at the head, a numbered spine, and one flat clue object centered in an otherwise empty field
Topology/navigation: the series is a shelf of near-identical objects, so navigation is spotting the one clue that changed between numbers
Controls/state: controls are clue objects, the active one takes vermilion, and eliminated ones drop to the green and stay eliminated
Responsive/motion: the shelf reflows in whole jackets, and motion is a jacket sliding out and its clue rotating into view
concepts.spark: forty jackets on a shelf, every one identical in green and red, and the only difference between number twelve and number thirteen is that one has a candlestick on it and the other has a railway timetable.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-jacket responsive shelf, elimination state persisted per clue, and a slide-and-rotate reveal animation

concepts.form: a berlin cabaret bill printed in two harsh inks, an angular figure in stark lighting cut against a black field, the programme ranked in expressionist lettering that leans hard against the vertical
concepts.lineage: Weimar Berlin cabaret and revue bills, expressionist poster lettering and two-ink printing, 1919 to 1933
system: Palette/material: acid yellow and black on cheap stock, no midtone permitted, everything resolved to lit or unlit with a hard edge
Type/composition: expressionist lettering leaning off the vertical, an angular figure cut from the black, and the programme ranked in a stepped column
Topology/navigation: the programme is an ordered evening, so navigation advances an act rather than browsing a menu
Controls/state: controls are programme lines, the active one reverses to acid yellow, and finished acts are struck through
Responsive/motion: the stepped column restacks without straightening, and motion is a hard lighting cut from black to yellow
concepts.spark: acid yellow on black, no gray anywhere, a figure with its cheekbones cut out of the darkness, and the programme leaning off the vertical as if the room is already unsteady.
concepts.webLeverage: a hard two-state lighting cut on interaction, responsive stepped column restacking, and struck-through act state

concepts.form: a french pop record sleeve, a cropped studio portrait on a flat saturated ground with a rounded logotype above and four track titles ranked in a small tidy block at one corner
concepts.lineage: French yé-yé pop record sleeve design of the 1960s, extended-play sleeve conventions and rounded pop logotypes
system: Palette/material: one saturated flat ground per release in tangerine or turquoise, portrait printed warm, and white as the only relief color
Type/composition: a rounded pop logotype at the head, a portrait cropped square at the chin, and four track titles ranked small in one corner
Topology/navigation: the release is four tracks, so navigation moves within a small closed set rather than an open catalog
Controls/state: controls are track lines, the active one takes white on the ground, and played ones drop to a tint
Responsive/motion: the flat ground floods any frame and the portrait crops square, and motion is a ground color cross-fade between releases
concepts.spark: one flat tangerine ground, a face cropped square at the chin, a logotype with rounded corners, and four song titles tucked politely into the bottom corner.
concepts.webLeverage: a css custom-property ground with cross-fade animation, square responsive portrait cropping, and played state per track

concepts.form: a tokyo boutique-pop sleeve wrapped in a printed paper obi band, the band crowded with dense vertical credits and catalog numbers while the sleeve face behind it holds one geometric mark and nothing else
concepts.lineage: Japanese record obi band printing and Shibuya-kei boutique-pop art direction quoting mid-century European modernism, 1993 onward
system: Palette/material: a saturated obi band in one strong hue against a pale sleeve face, the band printed dense and the face left almost bare
Type/composition: crowded vertical credits packed onto the obi band, a single geometric mark on the face behind, and a deliberate density collision between the two
Topology/navigation: the band overlays the face, so navigation slides the band to reveal what it was covering
Controls/state: controls are band segments, the active one slides clear of the face, and inactive ones stay wrapped across it
Responsive/motion: the band holds its proportion of the face at any width, and motion is the band sliding off and back on
concepts.spark: a nearly empty sleeve with one small mark on it, and wrapped around the bottom third a paper band so crowded with credits that the collision between the two is the whole design.
concepts.webLeverage: a proportional overlay band that slides on pointer state, responsive density on the band, and reveal state for the face beneath

concepts.form: a london pirate radio flyer photocopied and folded small, mc names ranked in a heavy outlined face over a low-resolution city photograph, phone numbers and pager codes packed into the lower band
concepts.lineage: UK pirate radio and grime flyer print, photocopied rave and dubplate promotion, MC billing and pager code conventions, 1998 onward
system: Palette/material: photocopier black on colored office stock, halftones collapsing to hard dots, folds wearing white through the ink
Type/composition: a heavy outlined display face ranking MC names, a degraded city photograph beneath, and codes packed into a ruled lower band
Topology/navigation: the bill is a ranked crew, so navigation moves through billing order rather than through categories
Controls/state: controls are MC names, the active one gains a second outline, and dropped names are simply overprinted
Responsive/motion: the billing restacks in whole names at any width, and motion is a photocopy generation jump
concepts.spark: a flyer folded into eighths in somebody's pocket, twenty MC names ranked by size, a city photo copied so many times it is mostly dots, and a pager number along the bottom.
concepts.webLeverage: responsive billing that restacks in whole names, a generational degradation filter on state, and live rank ordering

concepts.form: a southern rap tape cover dubbed at home, a low-resolution portrait pushed to hard contrast over a purple field, the artist name set in a heavy chrome-free outline face with the tape number hand-marked
concepts.lineage: Memphis rap home-dubbed tape covers of the 1990s, photocopied and low-resolution portrait treatment, hand-marked tape numbering
system: Palette/material: deep purple and black with a bleached portrait pushed past midtone, printed on cheap stock and dubbed onto a plain shell
Type/composition: a heavy outlined name across the head, a hard-contrast portrait beneath, and a tape number written by hand at one corner
Topology/navigation: the tape is a numbered run, so navigation moves between hand-numbered dubs of the same short catalog
Controls/state: controls are track marks, the active one is circled by hand, and played ones are struck with a pen line
Responsive/motion: the portrait crops to hold its contrast, and motion is a slowed tape drag on transition
concepts.spark: a portrait photocopied until it is only black and white with nothing in between, on a purple field, with the tape number written on the corner in biro by whoever dubbed it.
concepts.webLeverage: a css contrast filter driven by state, hand-marked track state persisted local, and a slowed tape-drag transition

concepts.form: a slowed-tempo lounge tape cover, a mid-century hotel photograph tinted a single dusty hue and set behind a soft-edged rounded logotype, the runtime printed unusually long in a small corner block
concepts.lineage: the barber beats and slowed-lounge cover tradition, single-hue tinted mid-century photography and soft rounded logotypes
system: Palette/material: one dusty tint applied over the whole photograph, contrast lifted and flattened, no true black and no true white anywhere
Type/composition: a soft-edged rounded logotype centered low, the photograph tinted behind it, and a runtime figure set small at one corner
Topology/navigation: the tape runs unusually long, so navigation moves slowly along a single continuous duration
Controls/state: controls are time marks, the active one warms its tint, and passed ones cool toward gray
Responsive/motion: the photograph crops while the logotype holds center, and motion is a slow tint drift across the field
concepts.spark: a hotel lobby from 1974 tinted the color of weak tea, a soft rounded logotype sitting low over it, and a runtime in the corner that turns out to be four hours long.
concepts.webLeverage: a css tint filter drifting on a timeline, responsive photograph cropping with a held logotype, and time-mark state

concepts.form: a brazilian album sleeve collaging studio portraits into a painted tropical tableau, cut-out figures pasted at mismatched scales among leaves and plastic fruit, concrete-poetry lettering scattered across the whole field
concepts.lineage: Tropicalia album art direction, Rogerio Duarte's sleeve design, Brazilian concrete poetry and cut-paper tableau collage
system: Palette/material: hot tropical greens and mango over a saturated painted backdrop, cut-out photographs printed warm with visible scissor edges
Type/composition: concrete-poetry lettering scattered at several angles and scales, figures pasted at deliberately wrong sizes among painted foliage
Topology/navigation: the tableau is one crowded scene, so navigation moves between pasted figures rather than through sections
Controls/state: controls are cut-outs, the active one lifts with a paper shadow, and inactive ones sit flat in the paste-up
Responsive/motion: figures repack among the foliage at any width, and motion is a cut-out lifting and settling back
concepts.spark: a man twice the size of the man next to him, both cut out with scissors and pasted into a painted jungle full of plastic fruit, with the word tropicalia broken into syllables and thrown across the whole thing.
concepts.webLeverage: a responsive collage that repacks cut-outs, paper-shadow lift transforms on state, and scattered svg lettering

concepts.form: a hardcore rave record sleeve built around one airbrushed mascot, a horned figure rendered in high-contrast airbrush against a black field with the event name in a chrome-free chiseled logotype locked above it
concepts.lineage: Dutch hardcore rave label artwork, airbrushed mascot illustration and chiseled event logotypes, 1992 onward
system: Palette/material: airbrushed crimson and bone against unrelieved black, high-contrast rendering with hard specular edges and no midtone drift
Type/composition: a chiseled logotype locked above the mascot, the figure centered and cropped at the shoulders, and event details ruled small at the foot
Topology/navigation: the mascot is the constant and the event changes around it, so navigation moves between editions of one recurring figure
Controls/state: controls are edition marks, the active one lights the mascot's eyes, and past editions drop to a bone outline
Responsive/motion: the mascot holds center and the black field absorbs the reflow, and motion is a hard strobe cut between editions
concepts.spark: the same horned figure on every record for fifteen years, airbrushed within an inch of its life against pure black, with the event name chiselled above it like something carved into a door.
concepts.webLeverage: a centered mascot with black-field responsive absorption, strobe-cut transitions, and edition state lighting the figure

concepts.form: a recife album sleeve fusing mangrove mud with circuitry, a crab drawn as a printed circuit board over a silt-brown ground, hand-inked lettering crowding the margins like graffiti on a river wall
concepts.lineage: the Manguebeat movement's record and poster art in Recife, mangrove-and-antenna iconography, hand-inked Brazilian sleeve design, 1991 onward
system: Palette/material: silt brown and mangrove green with one signal orange, printed on coarse stock so the ink sits rough and slightly blotted
Type/composition: a central creature drawn as circuitry, hand-inked lettering crowding all four margins, and a small antenna motif repeating as a rule
Topology/navigation: margins carry the noise and the center carries the subject, so navigation moves inward from crowded edge to clear middle
Controls/state: controls are antenna marks, the active one signals with the orange, and inactive ones stay in mangrove green
Responsive/motion: margin lettering recrowds at any width, and motion is a signal pulse travelling the circuit
concepts.spark: a crab whose shell is a circuit board, sitting in river mud, with hand-inked words crammed into every margin like somebody ran out of room and kept writing anyway.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg circuit path with a travelling signal pulse, responsive margin recrowding, and antenna controls bound to state

concepts.form: a record sleeve titled entirely in unicode glyphs, triangles and crosses substituted for letters until the name is unpronounceable, set over a smeared photograph slowed to the point of blur with heavy vignetting
concepts.lineage: the occult-glyph sleeve tradition of late-2000s underground electronic labels, unicode substitution titling and smeared photography
system: Palette/material: bruised violet and black over a smeared photograph, heavy vignetting closing the corners, with one bone white for the glyph row
Type/composition: a title row built from geometric unicode glyphs rather than letters, centered small, over an image dragged into motion blur
Topology/navigation: names are unreadable so navigation is by shape recognition, moving between glyph rows rather than titles
Controls/state: controls are glyphs, the active one brightens to bone white, and inactive ones sink into the vignette
Responsive/motion: the vignette closes further as frames narrow, and motion is a directional smear on transition
concepts.spark: the band name is a triangle, a cross and a shape you do not have a word for, floating over a photograph that has been dragged sideways until it stopped being a photograph.
concepts.webLeverage: a css directional smear filter on transition, responsive vignette closing, and glyph controls with brightened state

concepts.form: a dance hall handbill from the zoot era, an exaggerated long-line silhouette drawn in flat ink over a two-color ground, the orchestra billed in stacked display caps with a scalloped border closing the sheet
concepts.lineage: 1940s American dance hall handbills and zoot-era orchestra billing, flat silhouette illustration and scalloped letterpress borders
system: Palette/material: two letterpress inks in plum and ochre on cream stock, ink laid heavy enough to emboss the sheet, with no halftone anywhere
Type/composition: an exaggerated long silhouette drawn flat, orchestra names stacked in display caps by billing, and a scalloped border closing all four edges
Topology/navigation: billing order is the hierarchy, so navigation moves down the stack from headline orchestra to support
Controls/state: controls are billing lines, the active one takes the plum, and past dates emboss without ink
Responsive/motion: the scalloped border repeats in whole scallops, and motion is a letterpress impression pressing in
concepts.spark: a silhouette with shoulders a foot too wide and trousers down to the shoe, printed in plum and ochre, with the orchestra names stacked by importance inside a scalloped border.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg scalloped border repeating in whole units, a press-impression animation on state, and billing-rank ordering

concepts.form: a club wall where flyers are stapled over flyers, the top layer torn back in strips to expose four earlier nights at once, staple holes perforating every generation and one fresh sheet pasted crooked over all of it
concepts.lineage: club and venue flyer walls, stapled photocopy accretion, torn-back layering and paste-over practice
system: Palette/material: photocopy black on saturated fluorescent stock, older layers sun-bleached to pastel, staple holes punched through every generation
Type/composition: heavy display caps at four different scales fighting across torn edges, with only the newest sheet fully legible
Topology/navigation: depth is calendar, so navigation tears a strip back to reach a night that already happened
Controls/state: controls are torn strips, pulling one exposes the sheet beneath, and exposed layers stay open as a record
Responsive/motion: strips retear to fit any width, and motion is a paper rip that catches on a staple
concepts.spark: Somebody tore a strip off the wall to see what was playing last month and found three more nights underneath, each one stapled through the last.
concepts.webLeverage: layered svg tear masks generated responsive, pointer-driven strip reveal, and persistent exposed state

concepts.form: a small-press zine cover pulled on a duplicator in two spot inks, the layers deliberately misregistered so a third color appears where they overlap, paper showing through the halftone as visible open dots
concepts.lineage: risograph and mimeograph small-press printing, two-drum spot color overlap, deliberate misregistration and open halftone
system: Palette/material: fluorescent pink and medium blue on newsprint-weight stock, overlapping into a muddy third color, ink sitting visibly on the surface
Type/composition: display type set in one ink and imagery in the other, offset by a few millimeters so the overlap zone becomes its own shape
Topology/navigation: two layers move semi-independently, so navigation shifts one layer against the other to change what the overlap says
Controls/state: controls are layer offsets, the active one slides its ink out of register, and aligned states collapse the third color entirely
Responsive/motion: halftone dots hold their size while the image scales, and motion is one drum layer sliding against the other
concepts.spark: Pink over blue, printed a hair out of line on purpose, and where they cross there is a third color the machine cannot actually make.
concepts.webLeverage: css blend modes producing the overlap color, layer offset bound to interactive state, and a fixed-size halftone pattern

concepts.form: a jazz session sleeve where a duotone photograph is cropped hard to one corner, the artist name set in tight sans caps at an unexpected angle, and a wide band of flat color carrying the rest of the field
concepts.lineage: 1950s and 60s jazz session sleeve design, duotone session photography and angled sans-caps titling
system: Palette/material: a duotone photograph in ink black and one warm spot color, set against a wide flat field of the same spot at full strength
Type/composition: tight sans caps set at a deliberate angle, a session photograph cropped hard to one corner, and generous flat color elsewhere
Topology/navigation: the flat band is the constant and the photograph moves within it, so navigation recrops rather than repaginating
Controls/state: controls are title lines, the active one reverses out of the band, and inactive ones sit in the photograph's shadow
Responsive/motion: the flat band absorbs reflow while the crop holds its tension, and motion is a band color change between sessions
concepts.spark: A photograph of a man at a piano, cropped so hard he is almost out of frame, and the rest of the sleeve is one flat orange with his name across it at eleven degrees.
concepts.webLeverage: responsive crop that preserves compositional tension, a flat band as a css custom property, and per-session color transitions

concepts.form: a mobile cinema banner painted on a flour sack, a film scene reinvented at speed in thick enamel with invented monsters the film never contained, the title hand-lettered across the top in dripping outlined caps
concepts.lineage: West African mobile cinema banner painting on flour sacks, invented-scene enamel painting and dripping outlined titling
system: Palette/material: thick enamel on a rough flour sack whose weave and printed markings show through, colors mixed on site and applied fast
Type/composition: dripping outlined caps arced across the top, one invented scene filling the field, and a painted border closing the ragged edge
Topology/navigation: each banner is one promised scene, so navigation moves between banners rather than within one
Controls/state: controls are painted elements, the active one gains a heavier outline, and past screenings crack and flake
Responsive/motion: the sack weave shows at any scale, and motion is enamel dripping and catching at the edge of a letter
concepts.spark: The film did not have a giant hand in it, or that monster, but the man painting the sack in an afternoon decided it should, and he was right.
concepts.webLeverage: a woven texture layer under responsive artwork, a drip animation on letter edges, and wear state accumulating per screening

concepts.form: a small-press poetry broadside run off on a stencil duplicator, purple ink bleeding into absorbent paper, the poem typed directly onto the stencil with visible strikeovers and a hand-cut linocut mark in the corner
concepts.lineage: mimeograph small-press poetry publishing, typed stencil production with visible corrections and hand-cut relief marks
system: Palette/material: aniline purple bleeding into cheap absorbent paper, edges of every letterform feathering, with one black relief mark struck in the corner
Type/composition: a typewriter face set directly on the stencil with visible strikeovers, ranged left with a hand-cut mark at one corner
Topology/navigation: each sheet holds one poem, so navigation moves sheet to sheet rather than scrolling a continuous text
Controls/state: controls are lines, the active one deepens its purple bleed, and corrected ones keep their strikeover visible
Responsive/motion: the typed measure holds and the sheet crops around it, and motion is ink feathering outward into the paper
concepts.spark: Purple ink feathering into cheap paper, a word typed over twice because there was no way to take it back, and a linocut bird stamped in the corner.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg feathering filter bound to state, a fixed typed measure with responsive cropping, and visible correction state

concepts.form: a music festival lineup sheet where every act is set in the same face and the entire hierarchy is carried by size and line breaks alone, headliners spanning the width and the smallest names packed into a justified block at the foot
concepts.lineage: contemporary music festival lineup poster typography, size-only hierarchy and justified name blocks
system: Palette/material: one saturated ground with a single contrasting ink, no imagery whatsoever, and the type doing every job on the sheet
Type/composition: one condensed face at eight sizes, headliners spanning full width, and the long tail justified into a dense block at the foot
Topology/navigation: billing is the only structure, so navigation moves down through decreasing importance
Controls/state: controls are names, the active one inverts out of the ground, and sold-out days take a struck rule across their block
Responsive/motion: names rebreak to keep the block justified at any width, and motion is a size step as billing changes
concepts.spark: No pictures at all, just names, and you can tell exactly who matters most from across the room purely by how big they are.
concepts.webLeverage: responsive justified type blocks that rebreak at any width, billing-rank state, and size-step transitions

concepts.form: a museum exhibition identity where one oversized cropped detail from a single work carries every surface, the title set small against it in a fixed corner, and dates and venue ruled into a consistent band at the foot of everything
concepts.lineage: contemporary museum exhibition identity design, single-detail cropping with fixed corner titling and consistent information bands
system: Palette/material: the palette is taken entirely from the cropped artwork, with one neutral for the band and no color invented outside the work
Type/composition: a large cropped detail dominating, the title set small and locked to one corner, and a ruled band carrying dates and venue
Topology/navigation: the same crop recurs across every surface, so navigation moves between applications rather than between images
Controls/state: controls are band items, the active one takes the artwork's dominant hue, and past dates strike within the band
Responsive/motion: the crop reframes to any aspect while keeping its focal detail, and motion is a slow push into the detail
concepts.spark: One corner of one painting, blown up until it stops being recognizable, with the exhibition title set politely small in the corner.
concepts.webLeverage: art-directed responsive cropping around a declared focal point, palette extracted from the artwork, and a slow push-in

concepts.form: a publisher series seen on the shelf, spines designed to be read together so the series mark aligns across every volume, numbers running in sequence and one continuous color field crossing the whole run when shelved in order
concepts.lineage: publisher series spine design, aligned series marks with sequential numbering and shelf-continuous color fields
system: Palette/material: a graded color field distributed across the run so each spine holds one step, with a consistent stock and one foil-free ink
Type/composition: a series mark at a fixed height on every spine, the number set in a consistent position, and titles set to a common baseline
Topology/navigation: the shelf is the index and order is the structure, so navigation moves along a sequence rather than through categories
Controls/state: controls are spines, the active one pulls forward from the run, and unowned volumes render as a gap in the color field
Responsive/motion: the run reflows in whole spines preserving order, and motion is a volume pulling out and turning to show its cover
concepts.spark: Shelve all forty in order and the spines make one continuous gradient, so a missing volume is a visible notch in the color.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-spine responsive run with computed color steps, ownership gaps in the field, and a pull-and-turn transition

concepts.form: a hand-coloured woodcut broadside sold at a fair, a crowded scene cut in thick outline and washed with four transparent colours, a caption block of dense lettering filling the strip beneath
concepts.lineage: Russian lubok folk woodcut broadsides, fairground print sellers, hand-colouring workshops and caption-block setting
system: Palette/material: rough grey paper with a heavy black woodcut line washed by four transparent colours applied past the outline by hand
Type/composition: a crowded scene filling the upper field with a dense hand-lettered caption strip beneath, the two divided by a single cut rule
Topology/navigation: each sheet is one complete tale, so navigation moves between sheets rather than through them
Controls/state: controls are figures in the scene, the active one takes a second colour wash, and told sheets fade toward the paper
Responsive/motion: the caption strip stays full width while the scene crops, and motion is a colour wash flooding past its outline
concepts.spark: The colour does not stay inside the lines because it was washed on by hand at speed for a penny a sheet, and somehow that is why it is alive.
concepts.webLeverage: svg woodcut linework with wash layers that deliberately overflow, per-figure state, and a full-width responsive caption strip

concepts.form: a pamphlet hung by a string across a market stall, its cover a single woodcut over a rhymed title in wood type, sold from a line where the whole stock is readable at once as a wall of covers
concepts.lineage: Brazilian and Portuguese cordel chapbook publishing, string-hung market display and woodcut cover practice
system: Palette/material: coarse newsprint covers in one ink, occasionally on a coloured stock, with the woodcut re-used across many unrelated titles
Type/composition: a single woodcut above a rhymed title in wood type, with the poet's name set small at the foot and no other cover matter
Topology/navigation: the stock hangs on a line so the whole catalogue is visible at once, and navigation scans a wall rather than a list
Controls/state: controls are pamphlets on the line, the active one is lifted from the string, and sold slots hang empty
Responsive/motion: the line reflows in whole pamphlets and adds rows as needed, and motion is a pamphlet lifting off its string
concepts.spark: The entire bookshop is a piece of string with forty covers pegged to it, and the same woodcut of a horseman is on nine unrelated stories.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-pamphlet responsive hanging line, lift-from-string interaction, and sold-state gaps in the display

concepts.form: a folk woodblock print pulled onto paper coated with crushed shell, each colour cut as its own block and printed separately over a ground that glitters faintly under the flat pigment
concepts.lineage: Vietnamese Đông Hồ folk woodblock printing, crushed scallop-shell ground paper and one-block-per-colour registration
system: Palette/material: crushed shell ground paper that catches light beneath flat mineral pigments in red, yellow, green and indigo, with a final black keyblock
Type/composition: a single subject centred with a short block of characters at one side, colours printed as separate flat areas under a black outline
Topology/navigation: the print builds colour by colour, so navigation adds a block rather than moving to a new view
Controls/state: controls are colour blocks, the active one prints its layer, and the keyblock always prints last
Responsive/motion: the composition crops around its centred subject, and motion is each block registering in printing order
concepts.spark: The paper itself glitters because it is painted with crushed shell, so the flat colours printed on top of it never sit quite still.
concepts.webLeverage: layered svg colour blocks over a shimmering ground texture, print-order reveal animation, and centred responsive cropping

concepts.form: a street ballad sheet printed with no music at all, the tune given only as the name of another song everyone already knows, above a woodcut reused from whatever the printer had in the drawer
concepts.lineage: street ballad sheet printing, tune-name-instead-of-notation convention and reused stock woodcut practice
system: Palette/material: one worn black ink on cheap unsized paper, the woodcut visibly more battered than the type it sits above
Type/composition: a title, then the line naming the tune to sing it to, then dense verse in a narrow double column beneath a stock woodcut
Topology/navigation: the tune is a pointer to another sheet, so navigation follows references between ballads rather than reading one
Controls/state: controls are tune names, the active one links to the ballad it borrows from, and orphaned tunes have no target
Responsive/motion: the double column collapses to one while the woodcut holds, and motion is a worn impression pressing unevenly
concepts.spark: There is no music printed anywhere on it. Instead it just says which other song to sing it to, and assumes you already know that one.
concepts.webLeverage: a reference graph between ballads via tune names, orphan detection, and a responsive double column with a held woodcut

families.label: Notation & Diagram Systems
families.description: Systems that encode meaning as marks and diagrams: musical and choreographic notation, pictograms, technical and scientific drawings, and charts whose legends become interface grammar.

concepts.form: an experimental graphic score, cardew's treatise pages where line weight, cluster density, and drift replace notes, interpretation left to the performer
concepts.lineage: Cornelius Cardew's Treatise, Ligeti's Artikulation listening score, Cage's indeterminate notations
system: Palette/material: absolute black geometry on white stock, silence kept as true white ground, the performer's pencil gray marking the passage in play
Type/composition: type nearly absent, small grotesk folios at the corners; the central lifeline rules the page and stroke weight does the ranking type would do
Topology/navigation: a long unbroken scroll where thickening lines, swarming dots, and empty stretches pace the journey, no numbered anchors, only visual weather
Controls/state: intensity is stroke weight and cluster density, an idea's importance literally thickens its line, silence is honored as empty space
Responsive/motion: the scroll compresses like a squeezed accordion with density ratios preserved; motion drifts with reading pace
concepts.spark: One hundred ninety-three pages of black geometry unfurl across the music stands, and the ensemble stares at a swelling line, deciding together what a thickening means tonight.
concepts.webLeverage: Scroll-driven animation ties playback density to reading position along one continuous canvas scroll.

concepts.form: a labanotation dance score, a vertical center staff read upward where symbol shape is direction, shading is level, and length is exact duration
concepts.lineage: Rudolf Laban's Kinetographie, Dance Notation Bureau scores, Albrecht Knust's kinetography
system: Palette/material: white score paper and black symbol blocks, level encoded as solid, hatched, or dotted fill, the beat in progress banded pale gray across the staff
Type/composition: type stays marginal, small count numerals beside the staff; the vertical center staff rules the page and bilateral symmetry is the layout law
Topology/navigation: columns flank a center line, left column for left limb and right for right, time flows bottom to top so the future is always above
Controls/state: each action is a shaped block whose length is its duration, shading sets level, simultaneous acts sit side by side across the columns
Responsive/motion: columns thin but never merge, symmetry across the centerline is the invariant; motion rises like a slow elevator
concepts.spark: In a mirrored studio a notator watches the leap twice, then draws a shaded rectangle whose exact height is the half-second the dancer hung in the air.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS grid columns mirror the body's bilateral layout, and scroll timelines run time upward through the score.

concepts.form: an orienteering map and legend, iso-standard colors where white means runnable forest, contours rule the truth, and the course rides in purple over everything
concepts.lineage: ISOM mapping standard, Scandinavian orienteering federations, control-description sheets
system: Palette/material: isom inks, white runnable forest, olive thicket, yellow open land, brown contours, blue marsh, course purple reserved for the active leg
Type/composition: condensed sans control numerals in purple beside their circles, the legend a ranked symbol table, contour line texture is the page's ground
Topology/navigation: terrain is a fixed color language beneath and the numbered purple course rides above, you travel control to control choosing your own route
Controls/state: each control pairs a circle on the map with a coded description row, punched controls check off, the course layer never edits the terrain
Responsive/motion: the map keeps metric scale and clips to a window around your current leg; panning follows the compass bearing
concepts.spark: Thumb on the map and breath ragged, a runner in wet birch forest gambles on the marsh crossing because two contour lines pinch, and the purple line does not care how.
concepts.webLeverage: Geolocation tracks your position over the fixed-scale map with the course as an SVG overlay layer.

concepts.form: a celestial star atlas chart, magnitudes as ranked dot sizes on a coordinate sphere, constellation lines and mythic figures faint beneath the data
concepts.lineage: Norton's Star Atlas, Uranometria, Tirion's Sky Atlas 2000.0 conventions
system: Palette/material: deep navy chart ground with chalk-white stars, red-flashlight amber for annotations, the object under the eye ringed in that same night-vision red
Type/composition: light serif italic names the constellations, small tabular figures label coordinates, dot diameter carries the hierarchy the type declines to
Topology/navigation: the sky splits into overlapping charts with matched edges, coordinates gridline the field and an index of named objects points into each plate
Controls/state: importance is dot diameter on a fixed magnitude ramp, variable objects wear distinct rings, the mythic figure layer fades up only on request
Responsive/motion: each plate crops around its brightest anchors at small sizes; panning drifts like slow sidereal motion
concepts.spark: Under a red flashlight at two in the morning, a cold thumb traces from the chart's inked dots up to the actual sky, and Orion's belt agrees with the paper exactly.
concepts.webLeverage: Canvas plots thousands of magnitude-scaled points with smooth zoom between chart plates.

concepts.form: a synoptic weather chart of station models, each observation a compact glyph cluster around a circle, isobars threading the stations into weather
concepts.lineage: WMO station-model code, NOAA surface analysis charts, shipping forecast synoptics
system: Palette/material: pale chart-gray coastlines under jet station ink, cold-front blue and warm-front red toothed lines, the watched low circled in grease-pencil red
Type/composition: tabular figures at fixed seats around each station circle, isobar labels set into their gaps, highs and lows named in large sans capitals
Topology/navigation: stations pin to true geography, each a dense glyph rosette; isobar contours are the connective tissue you read between them
Controls/state: every value has a fixed seat around the station circle, wind barbs add feathers per ten knots, fronts declare themselves in toothed lines
Responsive/motion: zooming sheds outer glyphs before ever moving one from its seat; successive charts animate as an advancing system
concepts.spark: In the forecast office at dawn a hundred inked rosettes bloom across the map of the ocean, and where the isobars squeeze closest together the forecaster circles tomorrow's gale.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG glyph rosettes stay legible at fixed seats while canvas interpolates animated isobar fields.

concepts.form: an illuminated roll of arms, ranked shields on vellum built by blazon grammar under the tincture law that metal never sits on metal nor colour on colour, each bearer named in gothic script
concepts.lineage: medieval English rolls of arms, the Zurich armorial, heralds' blazon grammar
system: Palette/material: the seven tinctures, or and argent metals against gules, azure, sable, vert, purpure, vellum cream as ground, sable as ink, gold leaf on the arms in focus
Type/composition: gothic textura minuscule names each bearer beneath his shield, shields ranked in even rows down the roll, blazon captions held to one ruled line
Topology/navigation: one continuous vellum roll read downward, shields ranked by precedence in even rows, kinship traced through quartered and differenced arms
Controls/state: every mark is blazonable, variants add cadency labels and differenced charges, the tincture law forbids color on color so every state keeps contrast
Responsive/motion: the roll narrows to a single shield column with names below, motion is the slow unrolling of the vellum
concepts.spark: In a candlelit chancery a herald lays gold leaf onto a shield's field, recites the blazon aloud, azure a bend or, and inks the bearer's name in gothic minuscule beneath the drying arms.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG paths and patterns generate ordinaries and charges from blazon parameters, tincture contrast enforced in code.

concepts.form: a tibetan mandala cosmogram, nested rings and four gates mapping a cosmology onto one square, each quadrant color-coded, every position meaningful, read inward toward the center
concepts.lineage: Tibetan thangka painting, sand mandala construction, Vajrayana cosmological diagrams, Kalachakra mandala tradition
system: Palette/material: mineral pigment quadrants of white, yellow, red, and green on indigo ground, gold line work for structure, the center reserved for the present focus
Type/composition: labels ride the rings on radial baselines, counts and names sized by ring depth, strict fourfold symmetry with one square palace inside the circles
Topology/navigation: concentric rings run from outer fire to inner palace; you enter by a cardinal gate and each ring inward is a narrower, more important scope
Controls/state: the active ring brightens to full pigment while outer rings dim toward indigo, quadrant color declares category, the center holds the chosen thing
Responsive/motion: rings collapse to stacked arcs on narrow screens with the center always visible; motion is slow rotation of the outer ring
concepts.spark: You kneel at the edge of a sand mandala as monks tap colored grains through brass funnels, the four gates aligned to the doors of the room, and the whole cosmos tightens ring by ring toward a center you cannot yet enter.
concepts.webLeverage: svg concentric geometry with radial text paths, and css transforms rotate ring groups without rebuilding the layout

concepts.form: the kamon family crest grammar, thousands of identities generated from circles, plants, and geometry, each one a single monochrome mark that survives any size, cloth, or lantern
concepts.lineage: Japanese kamon heraldry, Edo-era crest catalogs and pattern books, mon-kiri paper cutting
system: Palette/material: sumi ink black on undyed linen white, one indigo field for the active identity, no gradients; every mark reads in positive or reversed-out form
Type/composition: marks sit centered in a circle module on a strict grid of same-size cells, names in small quiet gothic caps below, the mark always outranks the label
Topology/navigation: a catalog grid of equal circular cells grouped by motif family, plants with plants, tools with tools; drilling in enlarges one mark to full frame
Controls/state: selection reverses the mark, white on indigo instead of ink on white; disabled marks thin to outline, and every state survives at 16 pixels
Responsive/motion: the grid drops columns but never scales marks below legibility; motion is a paper-cut reveal of the mark's construction lines
concepts.spark: You flip through an Edo crest catalog, hundreds of circles in rows, a crane folded into pure geometry beside three ginger leaves, and you find your own family's mark stamped small and sharp on the corner of a lantern.
concepts.webLeverage: inline svg marks stay crisp from favicon to hero size, and css custom properties flip positive and reversed states in one rule

concepts.form: an andean quipu, a primary cord hung with knotted pendant strings where position, knot type, and cord color encode quantity and category, a ledger read by hand along threads
concepts.lineage: Inka khipu administration, khipukamayuq record keepers, Andean cord and fiber accounting
system: Palette/material: undyed camelid fiber in cream and brown as ground, madder red and indigo cords for categories, a twisted two-color cord marking the active record
Type/composition: numerals rendered as knot clusters ranked by height on each cord, decimal position read top to bottom, labels small and horizontal at the primary cord
Topology/navigation: one horizontal primary cord with pendant cords hanging in groups; you move laterally across categories and downward into a single cord's digits
Controls/state: touching a cord lifts it forward and unspins its value into plain digits, edits tie a new knot rather than erasing, totals live on summary cords
Responsive/motion: pendant groups wrap into rows while cords keep their hang; motion is a slight sway settling after touch
concepts.spark: You run a knotted cord through your fingers in cold highland light, counting a long knot of seven near the tip, red threads for llamas and blue for cloth, an entire province's tribute hanging across your knees.
concepts.webLeverage: svg cords with drag interaction, pointer events lift a cord while css transforms animate its settling sway

concepts.form: adinkra symbol cloth, a stamped lexicon of proverbs printed in gridded fields, each geometric mark carrying a named meaning, comb-drawn lines dividing the cloth into panels
concepts.lineage: Akan adinkra printing of Ghana, Ntonso stamp carvers, calabash stamps and badie ink, Asante proverb iconography
system: Palette/material: badie ink black stamped on russet, brick, or indigo cloth grounds, comb-drawn dividing lines in the same ink, one pale panel for the item in focus
Type/composition: symbols repeat in ranked rows inside comb-ruled panels, each panel one meaning family, names set small beneath in wide-tracked caps like woven labels
Topology/navigation: the cloth divides into a grid of ruled panels, one proverb family per panel; you read panel by panel and zoom to one stamp for its meaning
Controls/state: pressing an action stamps it, slightly rotated with inked edges, never twice identical; the chosen symbol prints darker while neighbors sit half-inked
Responsive/motion: panels reflow to a single column with rules intact; motion is the press and lift of a stamp landing
concepts.spark: You hold a carved calabash stamp over stretched cloth in a Ntonso courtyard, press it into thick black badie ink, and rock it onto the russet field, one more sankofa bird joining the ranked rows drying in the sun.
concepts.webLeverage: svg stamp marks tiled with css grid, and a filter roughens edges so each printed instance lands slightly different

concepts.form: a kunstformen der natur lithographic plate, radiolarians and medusae arrayed in mirror-symmetric constellations on a dark ground, each specimen numbered to a legend page, drawn past the limit of the microscope
concepts.lineage: Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur, Adolf Giltsch lithography, Leipzig chromolithograph plates, 1899 to 1904
system: Palette/material: near-black ground with specimens in pearl, amber, and sea-glass green, lithographic crayon grain in every shade, one accent hue per plate binding its figures
Type/composition: italic latin binomials in a ruled legend block beneath the plate, small index numerals beside each specimen, the plate title in spaced serif caps
Topology/navigation: each section is a plate composed in bilateral symmetry around a dominant central figure; the legend maps numerals to entries and zoom dives into one specimen
Controls/state: choosing a numeral lifts its specimen brighter while siblings sink into the ground, comparison sets two figures on one plate at matched scale
Responsive/motion: plates reflow to a centered single column keeping symmetry pairs together; motion is a slow brightening, as if the ground were deep water
concepts.spark: Under the lamp fifty glass skeletons hang in perfect mirror order on a ground like deep water, and numeral seven leads your eye down to a legend line naming a creature no one has ever seen alive.
concepts.webLeverage: svg filters lay lithographic grain over vector specimens and a magnifier zooms one numbered figure without leaving the plate

concepts.form: a utility patent drawing sheet, an invention exploded into numbered figures in ruled ink line, reference numerals tied to parts by curved leader lines, hatching standing in for every material, witnessed and dated in the margin
concepts.lineage: USPTO utility patent drawings, nineteenth and early twentieth century draftsman conventions, Official Gazette engravings
system: Palette/material: india ink line on white bond inside a single ruled border, section hatching as the only fill, one carmine annotation ink reserved for what is under examination
Type/composition: Fig. numerals in open serif caps head each view, reference numerals hang at leader-line ends, the invention title runs along the sheet head in spaced caps
Topology/navigation: figures are views of one invention; you move between elevation, section, and detail, and every part numeral links to its line in the specification
Controls/state: selecting a numeral pulls its leader taut and thickens that part's outline, assembled and exploded are two states of one figure, granted sheets carry the dated seal
Responsive/motion: sheets stack figure by figure on small screens with leaders redrawn to fit; motion is the explode and reassemble along dashed axis lines
concepts.spark: You unroll the sheet and Fig. 2 blooms into an exploded view, forty parts hanging on invisible threads, numeral 23 arcing on a curved leader to the one washer the whole claim depends on.
concepts.webLeverage: svg leader lines and hatch patterns redraw responsively while an animated transform explodes assemblies along their axes

concepts.form: an Isotype statistical atlas, where quantities are rows of repeated flat pictograms and every comparison is countable at a glance
concepts.lineage: Otto Neurath and Gerd Arntz's Isotype movement and its printed statistical atlases
concepts.spark: Ranks of identical black figures march across the page, one per million; the strike year is a sudden red row twice as long, and no axis is needed to feel it.
system: Palette/material: warm off-white page, flat black pictograms, one insistent red reserved for the figure that matters; no gradients anywhere
Type/composition: quiet grotesk captions under bold row labels; charts are ranked rows of repeated units aligned to one common left edge
Topology/navigation: Move by question, by decade, and by population row.
Controls/state: Count, compare, isolate, and re-unit quantities; selection turns a row red.
Responsive/motion: Rows grow by adding whole units one at a time; narrow screens change the unit value and say so plainly.
concepts.webLeverage: Unit-count charts as real DOM lists, one element per unit, so quantities stay countable by screen readers

concepts.form: the 1900 Du Bois data portraits, where hand-inked bars, spirals, and color fields turn hard statistics into unapologetically bold graphic argument
concepts.lineage: W. E. B. Du Bois's American Negro Exhibit charts from the 1900 Paris Exposition
concepts.spark: A crimson spiral coils tighter than the page should allow, gold and black bars slam against hand-lettered captions, and one wandering line carries a population across fifty years.
system: Palette/material: aged cream board with saturated crimson, gold, emerald, and ink black laid down flat by hand
Type/composition: hand-lettered small-caps captions; each chart invents the form its question needs: coiled spirals, wrapped bars, stepped squares
Topology/navigation: Move by question, by chart form, and by year.
Controls/state: Trace, unroll, and compare; a spiral unrolls into a bar to prove the same quantity.
Responsive/motion: Charts redraw as if inked in one continuous stroke; small screens show one chart at a time at full bleed.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG chart forms with an unroll transition between spiral and bar encodings of the same data

concepts.form: a kolam pattern book, where looping lines travel around dot lattices in unbroken paths and every morning's design is both geometry and welcome
concepts.lineage: Tamil kolam threshold drawing, its printed pattern books, and dot-lattice loop grammar
concepts.spark: A grid of dots waits like sheet music; one white line sets out, bends around every dot without lifting, and closes exactly where it began as the doorway brightens.
system: Palette/material: deep threshold ground with rice-white line work; celebration variants add bordered bands of saturated pigment
Type/composition: pattern-book numbering and modest labels beside dominant lattice drawings; symmetry classes organize the page
Topology/navigation: Move by lattice size, symmetry family, and occasion.
Controls/state: Trace, continue, and complete loops; an unfinished path is a visible, honest state.
Responsive/motion: Loops draw as one continuous stroke; small screens reduce the lattice count, never the line weight.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG single-path loop drawing with pathLength animation and lattice sizes derived from the viewport

concepts.form: a service diagram where lines run only at fixed angles, interchanges drawn as linked markers and every station tick spaced evenly regardless of true distance, so the network reads as connections rather than geography
concepts.lineage: diagrammatic transit mapping, fixed-angle line geometry with evenly spaced station ticks and linked interchange markers
system: Palette/material: a pale ground with one saturated color per line, white-cored interchange markers, and no terrain or geography beneath
Type/composition: station names set at consistent angles beside their ticks, line colors carrying identity, and a legend ruled into one corner
Topology/navigation: connection matters and distance does not, so navigation follows lines and changes at interchanges
Controls/state: controls are lines and stations, the active line saturates while others drop to a tint, and closures strike their segment
Responsive/motion: the diagram simplifies by dropping minor ticks rather than scaling text down, and motion is a route tracing along its line
concepts.spark: Nothing on it is where it really is, every line runs at forty-five degrees, and it is the most useful map anybody has ever made of that city.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg fixed-angle network with route tracing animation, line-focus state dimming others, and tick-dropping responsive simplification

concepts.form: a painted almanac reading several week-cycles at once, concurrent cycles of five, six and seven days interlocking into a single ruled table where every cell carries the symbols of all cycles that fall on it
concepts.lineage: Balinese tika calendar painting, concurrent pawukon week-cycle reckoning, symbol-stacked almanac cells
system: Palette/material: soot black and iron red on cloth-backed board, symbols drawn small and dense with no colour used decoratively
Type/composition: a ruled table where each cell stacks the symbols of every cycle falling on that day, cycles distinguished by symbol shape rather than colour
Topology/navigation: several cycles run at once so navigation follows one cycle across the table while the others cross it
Controls/state: controls are cycles, the active one lights every cell it touches, and coincidences of two cycles mark heavier
Responsive/motion: the table reflows in whole cells and never drops a cycle, and motion is one cycle sweeping its cells in order
concepts.spark: Three different weeks running at the same time across one grid, and the days that matter are simply the squares where all three happen to land together.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-cell responsive table with per-cycle highlighting, coincidence detection across cycles, and a sweeping cycle animation

concepts.form: a weaving draft written as four linked diagrams, threading across the top, tie-up in the corner, treadling down the side and drawdown filling the field, where changing any one of them rewrites the cloth in the fourth
concepts.lineage: handweaving draft notation, threading and tie-up and treadling diagrams and the computed drawdown
system: Palette/material: filled and empty cells on graph paper in a single ink, with no colour used until the drawdown shows the cloth
Type/composition: threading along the top edge, tie-up boxed in the corner, treadling down the side, and the drawdown computed into the remaining field
Topology/navigation: the three inputs surround the one output, so navigation edits a margin and reads the centre
Controls/state: controls are cells in threading, tie-up and treadling, and any change recomputes the entire drawdown immediately
Responsive/motion: the four diagrams keep their corner relationship at any size, and motion is a drawdown recomputing cell by cell
concepts.spark: Three little grids around the edges, and the big one in the middle is not drawn at all, it is what those three make happen when the loom runs.
concepts.webLeverage: a live drawdown computed from threading, tie-up and treadling state, with cell-by-cell recompute animation and a fixed corner layout

concepts.form: a pocket airline timetable read as a raked rack of tinted glass slides lying on a lit goldenrod bed, where every column, code strip, heading and paragraph is set at one single type size so rank has to be carried by weight, case, reversal and rule instead
concepts.lineage: the interior pages of airline pocket timetables and the Official Airline Guide, 1958 to 1978, including the general information pages where that tradition set its running paragraphs
concepts.spark: A 1971 pocket timetable lying open flat on a light table, a scratched acetate ruler laid across the departure columns at a slight lean, the rules printed on the reverse of the sheet glowing up through the goldenrod stock.
system: Palette/material: Lit goldenrod bed under slate tinted glass, in carbon, bible ivory, vermilion and bottle green, accent set per block id, prose panes opaque ivory
Type/composition: One size only: Bell Gothic prose at 58 to 66, Trade Gothic Condensed No. 18 labels; rank is weight and case, containers rake 11 degrees, baselines flat
Topology/navigation: One continuous rack of slides along the rake, each restating its own heading; travel is lateral, a tick rail shows position and extent at every width
Controls/state: State is a mark in a fixed cell, filled holds, hollow does not, vermilion strikes, green confirms; one element per screen goes to an opaque reversed plate
Responsive/motion: One light travels the bed along the rake, never crossing a prose pane; slides move on that axis only, reduced motion parks it, width never scales type
concepts.webLeverage: CSS parallelogram containers driven by one --rake property with counter sheared inner blocks, the single type size as a token no component may override, code strips computed at build time, and the light as one composited gradient layer.

concepts.form: a knitting pattern leaflet's instruction page, where every term the page defines appears forever after as a small-cap token from the key at the head, every block closes with the count you should be holding in parentheses, and the whole thing is set on the flat wrong side of a fabric that is knitted everywhere the text is not
concepts.lineage: British and American knitting pattern publishing, Weldon's Practical Needlework from 1886 through the Patons and Baldwins leaflet era, and the Craft Yarn Council abbreviations fixed in 1997
concepts.spark: A folded leaflet held open under one thumb, the row line running k1, ssk, yo, k1, yo, k2tog, rep from star to last st, and ending in a number in brackets, with a soft pencil tick in the margin against every row already worked.
system: Palette/material: Two yarns, a saturated ground and a contrast, knitted procedurally across the field; foreign media enters untinted, fenced by a one stitch contrast selvedge
Type/composition: Monotype Plantin sets prose small with true small caps at a 48 to 60 measure, Monotype Grotesque Condensed for labels; prose sets on wrong side plates
Topology/navigation: One continuous cloth that never re-grounds; each text block carries a margin coordinate and closes on its count in parentheses, tokens expand in place
Controls/state: Marks printed on the cloth, a contrast yarn notch in a block's selvedge, worked blocks retiring toward the ground; rank is one struck swatch, yarns swapped
Responsive/motion: Nothing animates, every change is an instant restrike, an expanding token holds its top edge; a stitch is fixed in device pixels, so width buys more cloth
concepts.webLeverage: A WebGL knit field in two yarn colours with stitch size fixed in device pixels rather than uv, text on wrong-side plates punched by a stencil mask, tokens expanding inline with no transition, and one struck swatch in view at a time.

concepts.form: A watch-material interchangeability sheet where a giant calibre number and a tipped-in exploded plate sit under pasted supplement slips, all of it packed into tables of five-point figures between hairlines and held clear of every edge by a buff rail.
concepts.lineage: Swiss and American watch-material catalogues: Bestfit Encyclopedia of Watch Material (1936-1960s) and Flume Werksucher calibre sheets (1950s)
concepts.spark: A buff catalogue leaf on a bench mat under a loupe: a cinnabar-numbered supplement slip pasted over half a movement plate, the superseded part numbers struck through in black, forty screw-slot circles marching down a hairline-ruled column.
system: Palette/material: buff catalogue stock, dense black, one cinnabar overprint, steel-grey halftone; foreign photos tip in as cornered slips with hairline keylines, never bleeding.
Type/composition: tight tabular grotesque, tiny figures between hairlines; prose only on reserved buff panels; one item per surface enlarged tenfold as a double-ruled loupe plate.
Topology/navigation: nothing touches an edge; an unbroken buff rail two slot-widths wide frames every surface and carries numbered stub tabs that overlap the block they open.
Controls/state: state is a printed screw-slot circle: slot upright means set, canted means pending, unslotted means absent, struck through means superseded. Colour adds nothing.
Responsive/motion: everything snaps: slots detent in forty-five degree steps, slips advance one row-height, panels restack against the rail. No fades, no easing, no bleed.
concepts.webLeverage: One SVG slot-mark whose rotation in 45 degree detents is the only state channel, plus a tipped-in slip component with printed corner mounts and a keyline, and a persistent buff rail no element may cross.
avoid: No dead instrument greys or brushed-brass chrome: the ground is printed buff stock, and the second ink must actually print.
No luxury watch marketing: no wristshots, no gold serif logotype, no polished case renders, no crown-and-shield crests.
No decorative gear or cog ornament, and no exploded plate used as wallpaper behind running copy.

families.label: Maps & Journeys
families.description: Maps, routes, signs, transit, trails, landmarks, orientation, and the visual drama of finding a way through a world.
