concepts.form: an emergency light braid, photoluminescent floor strips, handrail light pulses, iso green exit pictograms, and door-frame edge glow braided into redundant visual paths to safety
concepts.lineage: Photoluminescent egress marking, ISO 7010 safety signage, aircraft floor-path lighting, high-rise evacuation systems
system: Palette/material: phosphor green glow on matte black ground, iso safety green panels with white pictogram figures, amber pulse reserved for the live direction
Type/composition: white iso pictograms and arrows inside solid green panels, almost no prose, hierarchy spoken by glow intensity and panel size
Topology/navigation: floor strip, handrail pulse, and door glyph braid as redundant paths to each exit, agreeing at every junction so losing one never strands you
Controls/state: a closed passage's floor strip goes dark and the braid rethreads around it, the live route pulses toward safety, refuges hold a steady green frame
Responsive/motion: small screens show one glowing next instruction with the braid as a thin strip above; pulses travel exit-ward at safe rates
concepts.spark: Smoke swallows the ceiling signs, but a cool green line wakes along the floor edge, a pulse of light runs the handrail toward the stair, and a white running figure glows in its green door frame.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS keyframe pulses travel exit-ward along SVG path strips, and prefers-reduced-motion swaps travel for steady glow.

concepts.form: a metropolitan rail map fired as a midnight-blue enamel mural, where scarlet, cobalt, amber, and green lines bend at disciplined angles, interchange circles bloom at crossings, and the entire city becomes a legible promise of movement
concepts.lineage: Harry Beck's diagrammatic Underground map, Tokyo Metro wayfinding, Mexico City Metro iconography, and international transit information design
system: Palette/material: midnight-blue enamel ground with porcelain white station ticks, scarlet, cobalt, amber, and green line inks, the chosen line burning brightest
Type/composition: humanist transit sans in fixed-size station labels, lines bending only at 45 and 90 degrees, the diagram's discipline is the composition
Topology/navigation: Organize movement by line, station order, branch, interchange, fare boundary, and destination rather than literal geographic distance.
Controls/state: Trace, transfer, reverse, reroute, and compare journeys with open, arriving, delayed, suspended, crowded, and accessible states.
Responsive/motion: Focus the chosen corridor while preserving transfer context; never shrink the whole network into an unreadable miniature.
concepts.spark: Under the station's white light, four colored lines meet in one porcelain interchange; a fingertip follows the scarlet route outward until the dense center opens toward the river.
concepts.webLeverage: Live service state can recompute only affected routes and transfer promises, while deep-linked itineraries, native search, and offline caching preserve a usable journey beyond the mural.

concepts.form: a night-market sign river, where lantern color, stall awnings, steam, handwritten boards, and sound lead visitors through a temporary street
concepts.lineage: Night-market lantern codes, hand-painted shop signs, and temporary street wayfinding.
system: Palette/material: saffron lantern glow over wet asphalt black, blue awning and red banner inks, steam white as soft divider, lantern gold marking the open stall
Type/composition: hand-painted brush characters beside marker-on-cardboard prices, each stall's sign its own voice, the river of lanterns the only shared order
Topology/navigation: Follow temporary sign families through food, craft, performance, rest, and exit districts.
Controls/state: Choose interests, reveal crowd-friendly alternatives, and save a stall by its visual landmark.
Responsive/motion: Keep the nearest sign and district edge dominant on phones while retaining a simple escape route.
concepts.spark: A river of saffron lanterns bends past blue fish awnings, disappears in dumpling steam, and resurfaces as hand-painted arrows toward a midnight music court.
concepts.webLeverage: Live vendor openings, short-range location, and offline visual landmark cards adapt to a market that changes nightly.

concepts.form: an old treasure map on salt-stiffened vellum, where a compass rose, missing corner, tide marks, coded marginalia, false trails, and a hand-drawn coastline turn navigation into inference
concepts.lineage: Portolan charts, manuscript cartography, maritime wayfinding, engraved adventure maps, material archives, and puzzle-box clue design
system: Palette/material: salt-stiffened vellum tan with iron-gall sepia ink, tide-stain gray blooms, one faded red route rising under oblique light as the active trail
Type/composition: cramped manuscript hand with a flourished compass rose, coded marginalia crowding the edges, the coastline drawn first and words fit after
Topology/navigation: Move from map edge to landmark, bearing, marginal clue, damaged gap, candidate route, hidden harbor, and final cache hypothesis.
Controls/state: Rotate, measure, reveal, annotate, combine clues, and compare sealed, weathered, suspected, disproved, aligned, and solved states.
Responsive/motion: Center one clue chain on phones while preserving the whole parchment as context
concepts.spark: Oblique light raises a nearly erased red route beneath the ink; the torn corner aligns with a crescent island, and a tide stain suddenly becomes the boundary of a hidden harbor.
concepts.webLeverage: Deep image zoom, oblique-light layers, URL-addressable annotations, collaborative hypothesis history, and accessible transcription let groups solve the artifact while every inference retains provenance.

concepts.form: an international airport sign system, saturated yellow panels hung as framed overhead bands, black humanist sans beside white pictograms, arrows placed by strict edge rules, gate numbers at monumental scale down the concourse
concepts.lineage: Paul Mijksenaar's Schiphol signage, Adrian Frutiger at Roissy, AIGA DOT pictograms
system: Palette/material: saturated schiphol yellow panel ground with black type, white pictograms on black inset squares, yellow reserved for wayfinding and nothing else
Type/composition: frutiger-cut humanist sans in sentence case, one message per band line, arrows locked to the panel edge they point past, gate numbers monumental
Topology/navigation: a chain of decision points, each junction shows only the choices ahead with distances in minutes, and every path re-signs itself after each turn
Controls/state: the followed destination stays highlighted band to band, a gate change repaints the arrow instantly, closed routes drop off the panel entirely
Responsive/motion: small screens collapse to the single next decision with the gate number monumental; motion is a split-flap band update
concepts.spark: Off the jet bridge with nine minutes to make the connection, one yellow band hangs at the corridor junction, black letters and a running-figure pictogram agreeing: gates D1-D57, left, twelve minutes' walk.
concepts.webLeverage: Sticky positioned sign bands persist while corridors scroll past, and view transitions swap panel messages at each decision point.

concepts.form: a sanborn fire insurance plat, city blocks footprinted in construction-coded color, pink for brick and yellow for frame, street names in spaced caps along their rights of way, numbered sheets keyed to an index, corrections pasted over the past
concepts.lineage: Sanborn Map Company fire insurance atlases, 1880s to 1950s survey drafting and paste-slip revision practice
system: Palette/material: rose-pink brick, straw-yellow frame, and slate-blue stone footprints on plat cream, olive detail inks, carmine circled numerals as the working accent
Type/composition: street names in spaced caps run along their streets, sheet and block numerals sit in circles, tiny upright gothic notes annotate each footprint
Topology/navigation: an index sheet keys the territory; each numbered sheet holds a few blocks, edge arrows hand off to adjacent sheets, and footprints open into their records
Controls/state: a revised parcel wears a pasted correction slip one shade brighter than its sheet, hazard codes letter the risky, and the chosen footprint saturates alone
Responsive/motion: small screens serve one block per view with the index a tap away; motion is the paste slip settling over the old footprint
concepts.spark: In the atlas the whole burned district survives as pink and yellow footprints, and where the opera house came down someone has pasted a fresh slip, one shade brighter, over the building the fire took.
concepts.webLeverage: svg footprint layers color by data attribute and a searchparams-addressed index deep-links any sheet and block

concepts.form: a survey plate of enormous ground figures readable only from above, each line recorded as a measured stake alignment with its bearing and length tabulated beside a plan that no one standing on it could ever perceive
concepts.lineage: desert geoglyph survey recording, stake-alignment measurement and aerial plan tabulation
system: Palette/material: pale desert ground with a darker surface removed to draw the line, recorded as fine survey ink on drafting film
Type/composition: an aerial plan of continuous single-stroke figures with a bearing and length table ranged alongside
Topology/navigation: the figure is invisible at ground level, so navigation alternates between a walked line and the plan that explains it
Controls/state: controls are line segments, the active one reports its bearing and length, and walked segments dim on the plan
Responsive/motion: the plan scales while the bearing table reflows beneath, and motion is a rise from ground level to plan view
concepts.spark: A single line walked across the desert for four kilometres that turns out, from high enough up, to be one wing of a bird nobody on the ground has ever seen.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg aerial plan with segment bearing readouts, a ground-to-plan camera transition, and a responsive reflowing measurement table

concepts.form: a fair-pavilion interior threaded by one unbroken mitred band of ink silkscreened along the wall at hand height, where every bay of content exists only because the band doubles back and pens it in, and each place the band crosses itself prints one step darker
concepts.lineage: postwar world's-fair pavilion circulation graphics, Brussels 1958 to Osaka 1970: silkscreened route bands and their folded companion guides; read against mindmarket.com, Awwwards Site of the Day 2026
concepts.spark: Ten at night in a half-lit fair pavilion, cleaners gone, a four-inch orange band running the wall at hand height, doubling back to pen in a bay of pinned photographs, the crossing printed a shade darker where the squeegee passed twice.
system: Palette/material: seven zone inks screened on grey-tan uncoated board, tooth showing. Live zone floods 30-60%. Foreign media takes a butted band of that ink, never a tint over it.
Type/composition: one condensed grotesque, two sizes, flush to a band edge. Prose sits only on bare board at 7:1; rank is the band swelling to a solid plate around one element.
Topology/navigation: one unbroken band enters at one edge and leaves by another; regions exist only where it doubles back and encloses them. Stations are notches in its outer edge.
Controls/state: state is ink passes, not hue. Off knocks out to bare board, available is one pass, active overprints two a step darker, disabled leaves the outline alone.
Responsive/motion: the band prints once, entrance to exit, at a constant rate no scroll can scrub or reverse. Narrow, it folds to a vertical spine. Reduced motion arrives printed.
concepts.webLeverage: one SVG polyline whose vertices are computed from the content, drawn once by stroke-dashoffset at a constant rate independent of scroll; its self-intersections solve to clipPaths that become the bays, and state is multiply overprint
avoid: Not a curved ribbon: every turn is a mitre and every corner square, or this collapses into the flowing-blob brand site the mechanic was extracted from.
Seven inks are not confetti: one zone ink dominates a surface and the other six appear only at notches, crossings and the far edge.
The grain is press tooth, not a noise overlay; no drop shadows, no soft gradients, nothing implying the band is lit or floating.

concepts.form: a zoo and gardens guide map, where every area is a swelling lobe of flat colour and the coastline between lobes does all the dividing, and where a lobe can open in its middle so the page ground shows through it as water
concepts.lineage: American pictorial map illustration, 1930s-1970s: the folded zoo, park and campus guide maps handed out by the thousand at the gate
concepts.spark: A summer opening-morning guide map creased into eight panels: an apple-green headland swelling across the fold, a coral flamingo standing right on its edge with one foot out over the cream, and a yellow capsule pinned to the coastline reading GATE.
system: Palette/material: Flat unmodulated colour, no grain: green #8ED462 land on cream #F5F1E4 water, ink #2C2E2A. Photographs keep their own colour, cropped to a lobe, never tinted.
Type/composition: One grotesk at one weight; display at 0.95 leading, -0.06em. Prose is ink on cream, white, green or yellow; coral and blue carry labels only.
Topology/navigation: One lobe dominates each screen, swelling until its coast leaves the frame on two sides; a lobe may open in its middle and let the ground through as water.
Controls/state: Controls are capsules in yellow #F5E211, coral #FF705D, blue #2BA0FF, lilac #EBC1FF; a round chip rides its trailing edge and crosses to the leading edge when live.
Responsive/motion: Everything that moves takes 0.4s and overshoots before settling. Scroll redraws the coastline continuously; at narrow widths the coast runs down the frame.
concepts.webLeverage: Every area is one SVG path; scroll advances a single timeline that morphs the coastline, and the same path clips the illustration and the type, so one geometry drives layout, art and state together.
avoid: Do not let the lobes settle into equal sizes at even spacing; a coastline that never pinches or swells is wallpaper, not a map.
Keep the drawn cast few and specific. A character posted on every lobe turns a guide map into a sticker sheet.
No paper grain, fold shadows or halftone. The colour is flat and unmodulated, and a printed texture drags this world grey.

families.label: The Graphic Canon
families.description: Design movements inhabited as worlds: métro entrances, workshops, showrooms, and lobbies that carry a movement's geometry, ornament logic, palette, and conviction.

concepts.form: a cast-iron Art Nouveau métro entrance at dusk, where whiplash tendrils, amber glass, and organic lettering grow a threshold out of the street
concepts.lineage: Hector Guimard's Paris Métro édicules, Horta interiors, and the 1900 Art Nouveau movement's botanical structural ornament
system: Palette/material: guimard-green cast iron on wet asphalt gray ground, cream enamel plaques carrying body ink, amber opaline glass as the active glow
Type/composition: hand-drawn whiplash letterforms whose strokes bud into tendrils, headlines arched over each threshold, body copy held in narrow botanical frames
Topology/navigation: descend through a single ornamented threshold into branching stem-and-tendril routes.
Controls/state: controls bud from structural stems; hover swells a tendril, selection blooms it into an amber lamp.
Responsive/motion: tendrils simplify to a single stem on phones; growth eases organically and settles without looping.
concepts.spark: Iron stems rise from the pavement, curl into amber lamps, and spell the entrance name in letters that grew rather than were set.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG path-drawn tendrils animate growth along vectors while remaining crisp, addressable DOM at every zoom.

concepts.form: a Bauhaus foundation-course workshop, where primary circles, squares, and triangles in red, yellow, and blue are tested as material exercises on white tables
concepts.lineage: Weimar and Dessau Bauhaus Vorkurs pedagogy, Itten and Moholy-Nagy material studies, Kandinsky's point-line-plane
system: Palette/material: worktable-white ground with near-black ink, primaries rationed by role, red circle for the active state, blue square for structure, yellow triangle for alerts
Type/composition: bayer-style single-case geometric sans, lowercase headlines, composition ruled by point, line, and plane against a visible baseline grid
Topology/navigation: navigate by exercise; each section is one compositional problem solved with primary forms.
Controls/state: drag geometric elements against a visible baseline grid; state reads as balance, tension, or rest.
Responsive/motion: compositions rebalance rather than shrink; motion is a straight-line translation with honest easing.
concepts.spark: On a white worktable, a red circle, yellow triangle, and blue square wait like instruments; every arrangement is an argument about balance.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS grid and transforms make the composition itself the interactive canvas, with drag-and-drop arrangement.

concepts.form: an ulm school test bench for braun radios, where the sk4's clear acrylic hood, ordered dials, and gray-white housing are checked against ruled tolerances
concepts.lineage: Hochschule für Gestaltung Ulm, Dieter Rams and Hans Gugelot's Braun SK4, Otl Aicher's grid systems
system: Palette/material: sk4 gray-white housing as ground, graphite dial markings as body ink, the single green control lamp reserved for the live setting
Type/composition: small lowercase akzidenz-grotesk labels set flush to hairline rules, spacing stepped in millimeter increments, numerals the only emphasis allowed
Topology/navigation: every function sits in one ruled fascia row; nothing hides, and hierarchy comes from spacing intervals measured in millimeters
Controls/state: dials and sliders show their value by physical position alone; the single permitted accent color marks only the live setting
Responsive/motion: the fascia re-spaces on a strict modular scale per viewport; motion is damped mechanical settling
concepts.spark: Under a clear acrylic hood a pale gray radio waits on the ruled bench while a hand in a cotton glove nudges one green dial exactly the width of a hair.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS custom properties drive a millimeter-true spacing scale while pointer events give every dial damped direct manipulation

concepts.form: a brutalist conservatory terrace, where raw board-marked concrete holds tropical greenery, ribbed towers, and lake light in one massive calm
concepts.lineage: The Barbican Estate and conservatory, Chamberlin Powell and Bon, béton brut and megastructure planning
system: Palette/material: board-marked concrete gray as ground, lake-light off-white as body ink, fern and monstera green reserved for live and growing content
Type/composition: heavy cast-in sans capitals like formwork signage, letters inset flush into the mass, layout in wide structural bays divided by rib-thick rules
Topology/navigation: heavy fixed masses frame the routes; wayfinding is cast into the structure as inset signage.
Controls/state: controls are recessed into surfaces like switch plates; states change light within the recess, never float.
Responsive/motion: masses never animate; only light, plants, and people move, and small screens get deeper single columns.
concepts.spark: Concrete ribs vault overhead, ferns spill through the grid, and the weight of the place makes the quiet feel earned.
concepts.webLeverage: Texture-true concrete surfaces from generative noise, with layout masses that resist scroll like real weight.

concepts.form: a Constructivist agit-train stopped at a village platform, where diagonal red wedges, stencil type, and photomontage turn railcars into moving broadsides
concepts.lineage: Soviet agit-prop trains, El Lissitzky wedge posters, Rodchenko photomontage and diagonal composition
system: Palette/material: unbleached newsprint cream ground, soot-black stencil ink for body, revolutionary red rationed to the wedge that drives the action
Type/composition: stenciled wood-type caps and heavy numerals angled with the line of travel, photomontage fragments locked into the wedge's thrust, slogans banding each car
Topology/navigation: content advances car by car along one strong diagonal axis of travel.
Controls/state: calls to action are wedges that physically enter the composition; pressed states drive deeper.
Responsive/motion: diagonals steepen on tall screens and relax on wide; scroll advances the train
concepts.spark: A red wedge drives across a railcar; stenciled slogans and pasted photographs angle forward as if the train were still moving.
concepts.webLeverage: Scroll-driven horizontal travel with clip-path wedges keeps the diagonal grammar live in the browser.

concepts.form: an Art Deco cinema lobby at premiere hour, where stepped brass zigzags, sunburst marquees, and lacquered geometry frame velvet-roped anticipation
concepts.lineage: 1920s-30s picture palaces, Chrysler Building metalwork, streamline moderne signage and fan motifs
system: Palette/material: lacquered ebony ground, champagne and brass gold for frames and body accents, velvet-rope crimson marking the primary action
Type/composition: high-waisted deco capitals with inline strokes climbing stepped marquee tiers, layouts mirrored about a center axis, sunburst rules fanning the headings
Topology/navigation: arrival is staged as marquee, lobby, corridor, house; each threshold steps the geometry tighter.
Controls/state: primary actions get the sunburst frame; secondary actions recede into fluted panels.
Responsive/motion: stepped forms collapse tier by tier on small screens; light sweeps travel metal only on capable devices.
concepts.spark: Brass sunbursts fan over the doors, letters climb in stepped tiers, and every surface promises the feature has not started yet.
concepts.webLeverage: Gradient-mapped metallic surfaces and staged route transitions give each threshold a real arrival state.

concepts.form: a silver-foiled loft where celebrity portraits are silkscreened in off-register repeats, drying racks turning one image into thirty deliberate variations
concepts.lineage: Andy Warhol's 47th Street Factory, Billy Name's silver foil, silkscreen editioning, Interview magazine
system: Palette/material: silver-foil ground, one dense black halftone pass as body ink, fluorescent pink and marigold pulled per edition to mark the active print
Type/composition: headline caps silkscreened slightly off register, halftone dots visible at reading distance, the layout a drying rack of equal repeated frames
Topology/navigation: content presents as editioned repeats on a rack grid; you browse variations of one subject rather than single views of many
Controls/state: each action pulls a fresh print; states appear as ink shifts, misregistration, and color swaps across otherwise identical frames
Responsive/motion: the edition grid reflows from thirty-up sheets to single pulls on small screens; motion is the squeegee wipe
concepts.spark: Under tinfoil ceilings and one bare red bulb, the same famous face dries thirty times on a rope line, each copy wrong in a slightly more beautiful way.
concepts.webLeverage: canvas filters and CSS blend modes generate off-register color separations procedurally, so every repeat is a genuine variant

concepts.form: a machine-bound futurist book fastened with two aluminum bolts, its pages of diagonal wood type and onomatopoeic blasts meant to be read at engine speed
concepts.lineage: Fortunato Depero's Depero Futurista 1927, Marinetti's parole in libertà, Casa d'Arte Futurista Rovereto
system: Palette/material: unvarnished cream stock as ground, machine-black wood-type ink for body, one mechanical red for the word under pressure, aluminum bolt heads always visible
Type/composition: mixed wood-type sizes in one shout, words set 15 to 45 degrees off horizontal, onomatopoeia scaled by loudness, no two spreads composed alike
Topology/navigation: pages hinge on two visible bolts; every spread is a fresh typographic collision angled 15 to 45 degrees off horizontal
Controls/state: words themselves are the levers, set in wood-type weights; a pressed word slams larger inside a printed shockwave ring
Responsive/motion: narrow viewports rotate compositions toward vertical thrust; motion is percussive page-slams
concepts.spark: A book fastened with industrial bolts refuses to lie quietly on the table, every page shouting ZANG TUMB in wood type that leans into the turn like a racing chassis.
concepts.webLeverage: variable-font weight animation and CSS transforms let letterforms accelerate, tilt, and slam with true kinetic timing

concepts.form: a Googie roadside diner under a starburst sign, where boomerang counters, cantilevered roofs, and atomic orbits sell coffee as the space age
concepts.lineage: Southern California Googie architecture, Armet & Davis coffee shops, atomic-age signage and boomerang laminate
system: Palette/material: turquoise and coral counter laminate over chrome trim, charcoal boomerang speckle as texture, neon starburst white saved for the active state
Type/composition: exclamatory script for feature names over slab caps for the menu board, baselines allowed to tilt with the cantilever, prices set inside atomic starbursts
Topology/navigation: one swooping cantilever line carries the eye from sign to counter to booth; sections hang off it.
Controls/state: interactive elements orbit on atomic paths; active states snap into the starburst.
Responsive/motion: the swoop becomes a vertical spine on phones; orbits become static constellations under
concepts.spark: The roofline launches upward, the sign spins a neon starburst, and even the laminate counter orbits with boomerangs: the future, served all night.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS offset-path orbits and animated neon SVG strokes run the sign's physics natively in the browser.

concepts.form: a wiener werkstätte metalwork showroom, where hammered silver baskets punched with perfect square holes stack luxury into strict black-and-white lattices
concepts.lineage: Josef Hoffmann's Quadratlstil, Wiener Werkstätte metal shop, Ver Sacrum page borders, Palais Stoclet detailing
system: Palette/material: gallery-white ground ruled in lacquer black, hammered-silver sheen on frames and edges, the active cell filled solid black within its pierced row
Type/composition: ver sacrum roman capitals letterspaced inside ruled cartouches, square-unit borders framing every text block, symmetry held strictly to the lattice
Topology/navigation: content sits inside square-punched lattice frames; sections are nested caskets that open along strict orthogonal seams
Controls/state: every control is one square cell in a hammered border; active fills the cell solid black, idle leaves it pierced open
Responsive/motion: the lattice re-counts its squares per viewport but never stretches one; motion is a slow silver glint
concepts.spark: In a showroom off the Ringstrasse, silver baskets pierced with rows of perfect square holes catch the gaslight, and the walls themselves look drawn with a ruler dipped in black lacquer.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS grid with aspect-ratio-locked square cells and SVG lattice masks keep the punched geometry exact at every viewport

concepts.form: a psychedelic liquid-light show in a ballroom, where oil-and-dye projections breathe behind hand-lettered posters that melt legibility to its edge
concepts.lineage: 1966-69 Fillmore and Avalon poster art, Wes Wilson lettering, overhead liquid-light projection collectives
system: Palette/material: magenta, oil-orange, and acid-green dye blooms on a black ballroom ground, the brightest bloom backing the current section's cream-white text
Type/composition: wilson-style melted lettering filling every gap of its frame, lines swelling to the poster's edge, hierarchy read as heat rather than size
Topology/navigation: content floats on a breathing projection field; the current section holds the brightest bloom.
Controls/state: type warps toward the edge of legibility on idle and straightens instantly under pointer or focus.
Responsive/motion: blooms slow and shrink on small screens
concepts.spark: Colored oil blooms and collapses across the wall in rhythm; the headline bends like heat but you can still read the night's bill.
concepts.webLeverage: WebGL fluid simulation drives the projection while real HTML text stays selectable and accessible above it.

concepts.form: a Memphis Milano showroom morning, where terrazzo speckle, squiggle laminate, and clashing candy geometry make the furniture argue cheerfully
concepts.lineage: Ettore Sottsass and the 1981 Memphis group, Bacterio print laminates, postmodern Italian furniture
system: Palette/material: pink arguing with mint over bacterio-speckled cream laminate ground, black squiggle print as texture, one candy yellow reserved for the pressed control
Type/composition: chunky geometric display faces set at play angles, each block its own shape and pattern fill, alignment loose but every clash choreographed
Topology/navigation: sections are objects in a showroom, each with its own playful geometry inside one shared floor.
Controls/state: every control is a distinct toy-like shape; states change pattern fill, never just tint.
Responsive/motion: objects reflow like rearranged furniture; motion is springy but short, and pattern stays legible at density.
concepts.spark: A shelf leans like a question, the laminate crawls with black squiggles, and pink argues with mint until the argument becomes the room.
concepts.webLeverage: Procedural pattern fills generated per element keep speckle and squiggle unique at every viewport.

concepts.form: a William Morris pattern drawing room, where willow boughs and pomegranates repeat across wallpaper, textile, and binding as one hand-drawn ecosystem
concepts.lineage: Morris & Co. wallpapers and chintzes, the Arts and Crafts movement, Kelmscott Press ornament
system: Palette/material: indigo and willow-green pattern grounds with madder-red fruit accents, unbleached linen cream panels carrying dark sepia body ink
Type/composition: kelmscott-weight blackletter-toned type with drawn initials, text in cleared panels bordered by the repeat, ornament and column cut from one cloth
Topology/navigation: one master repeat unit generates borders, dividers, and frames; sections are cuts of the same cloth.
Controls/state: interactive elements sit in cleared medallions inside the pattern; hover lets the surrounding vines lean in.
Responsive/motion: the repeat rescales by density tier; growth animation traces stems once on entry and rests.
concepts.spark: The same willow stem returns on wall, curtain, and book edge, each repeat hand-drawn enough that the room feels grown, not printed.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG pattern tiles recolor and rescale from computed theme values, keeping ornament crisp and themable in the DOM.

concepts.form: a postmodern piazza staged as stacked classical orders, stainless-steel columns and scarlet stucco arcs traced at night in blue and red neon
concepts.lineage: Charles Moore's Piazza d'Italia New Orleans 1978, Venturi's decorated shed, postmodern classicism
system: Palette/material: night-sky black ground, scarlet stucco and stainless-steel panels as surfaces, blue and red neon tube light tracing whichever order is active
Type/composition: inscribed roman capitals running the entablature with neon-outline serifs, text arcs following the colonnade's curve, classical proportion quoted with a wink
Topology/navigation: concentric colonnade arcs frame one central destination; each ring quotes a different classical order at a different pitch of seriousness
Controls/state: capitals and arches are the controls; an active element lights its neon outline, quotation marks drawn around every action
Responsive/motion: the arcs flatten into a proscenium strip on small screens; motion is theatrical reveal ring by ring
concepts.spark: A roman colonnade rises out of a parking lot in stainless steel and scarlet stucco, and when night falls the cornices switch on in blue neon like ruins that learned to wink.
concepts.webLeverage: layered CSS 3d transforms give the stage-set arcs real parallax depth as the visitor moves through the rings

concepts.form: a photocopied punk zine spread pinned above the paste-up table, ransom-note headlines torn from three newspapers, halftone scraps and biro scrawl columns gone gritty through xerox generations
concepts.lineage: Jamie Reid's ransom lettering, Sniffin' Glue and Mark Perry's photocopy runs, 1977 DIY punk press
system: Palette/material: xerox toner black on cheap white copy paper ground, roller streaks and gray banding as texture, one day-glo flyer pink reserved for the action
Type/composition: ransom capitals cut letter by letter from mismatched papers for headlines, typewriter body columns glued down crooked, biro corrections in the margins
Topology/navigation: sections are stapled sheets in reading order; hierarchy is whatever got cut out biggest and glued down most crooked
Controls/state: controls are torn paper scraps; pressing one re-photocopies it a generation darker, grittier, and more smeared
Responsive/motion: columns re-paste at torn-edge breakpoints, never smooth reflow; motion is an abrupt slap-down placement
concepts.spark: You pull tonight's flyer off the stack still warm from the copier, the headline cut from three different papers, the band photo two generations past legible, the gig details scrawled in biro down a crooked column.
concepts.webLeverage: clip-path torn edges and SVG filter grain reproduce photocopier degradation live in the DOM, one generation per interaction

concepts.form: the layout desk of a surf-culture music magazine, columns colliding mid-sentence, an interview set entirely in dingbats, page numbers lost on purpose
concepts.lineage: David Carson's Ray Gun 1992-96, Beach Culture, The End of Print, surf-punk photography
system: Palette/material: surf-photo bleach tones on uncoated stock ground, dense overprinted black type as body ink, one clashing spot color per spread's loudest fragment
Type/composition: template gothic and battered grotesks at colliding sizes, columns crashing mid-sentence, type printed straight through the photograph when it earns it
Topology/navigation: reading order is earned, not given; the eye enters through the loudest fragment and assembles the page the way you hear a song
Controls/state: emphasis overprints, masks, and shears the type itself; the more urgent the content, the further the grid is allowed to break
Responsive/motion: fragments recompose per viewport into fresh collisions, never a tidy fallback; motion is print-registration slippage
concepts.spark: Somewhere beneath three overlapping headlines and a photograph printed straight through the text is an article that swears you will feel it before you can read it.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS mix-blend-mode overprints and layered grid areas let type collide while staying selectable, real text under the wreckage

concepts.form: the Rietveld Schröder house at midday, where sliding primary-color planes reconfigure one small room into many, and every joint stays visibly honest
concepts.lineage: Gerrit Rietveld's 1924 Schröder House, De Stijl planes and primaries, Mondrian's asymmetric balance
system: Palette/material: white and gray planes as ground, black frame lines as structural ink, red, yellow, and blue rationed to the sliding edges that actually move
Type/composition: lowercase geometric sans set flush to plane edges, text blocks treated as rectangles in the composition, asymmetric balance ruled by primary-color joints
Topology/navigation: one continuous space partitioned by sliding planes; routes are plane positions, not pages.
Controls/state: panels physically slide to reveal or combine sections; color marks the moving edge, gray holds the frame.
Responsive/motion: planes become stacked sliding sheets on phones; every slide is reversible and announced.
concepts.spark: A red plane slides, a yellow edge appears, and the living room becomes two bedrooms: the house is a composition you operate.
concepts.webLeverage: The View Transitions API and CSS plane slides make layout reconfiguration itself the navigation model.

concepts.form: a white gallery hung with black-and-white wave canvases, flat paint that flexes and strobes as visitors change their viewing distance
concepts.lineage: Bridget Riley's Movement in Squares and Current, The Responsive Eye at MoMA 1965
system: Palette/material: flat matte black and gallery white only, no mixed grays, contrast generated optically by line frequency, the tightest interval acting as the accent
Type/composition: a sparse neutral grotesk held clear of the waves in white margins, one caption per canvas, the composition itself a ruled monochrome field
Topology/navigation: the room is a sequence of vantage distances; each canvas holds a near, mid, and far reading and rewards deliberate approach
Controls/state: state rides the pattern itself; line frequency tightens toward points that want attention and relaxes wherever nothing is asked
Responsive/motion: wave frequency recalculates against device pixel density so the shimmer survives every screen
concepts.spark: The paintings hold perfectly still and yet the floor seems to tip, black lines swelling like a sea you can hear somewhere behind your own eyes.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG patterns modulated by scroll position and IntersectionObserver let a flat page flex as if the retina were being played

concepts.form: the observation lounge of a 1930s streamlined ocean liner, chrome speed lines wrapping lacquered cork walls, portholes in rhythm, furniture bolted against the swell
concepts.lineage: SS Normandie first-class interiors, Raymond Loewy and Norman Bel Geddes streamlining, the Burlington Zephyr observation car
system: Palette/material: lacquered cork tan and chrome speed lines over deep-hull navy ground, ivory body ink, engine-telegraph amber glowing behind the engaged control
Type/composition: streamline sans caps with speed-line extenders, letterspaced headings banding bow to stern, three parallel rules carrying every title forward
Topology/navigation: space flows bow to stern along three parallel chrome lines that never break; sections round their corners into each other, no hard stops
Controls/state: fittings are bolted and recessed against weather; engaged states glow behind frosted glass like an engine-room telegraph
Responsive/motion: the horizontal band compresses but its three speed lines persist at every width; motion is a long ocean ease
concepts.spark: Beyond the curved glass the atlantic slides past at thirty knots, and every rail, lamp, and letter in the room leans forward as if the furniture itself were making the crossing.
concepts.webLeverage: scroll-driven animation carries the chrome speed lines and horizon through the page on one continuous motion timeline

concepts.form: a late-1960s sunken conversation pit, where teak, wool, and low amber light pull a whole room's attention into one upholstered horizon
concepts.lineage: Mid-century modern interiors, Eero Saarinen's Miller House pit, Danish teak furniture and Panton-era color
system: Palette/material: burnt-orange wool and teak brown against off-white plaster ground, espresso body ink, low amber lamplight as the glow on the active center
Type/composition: warm mid-century serif headlines over a relaxed sans body, wide horizontal measures held at eye level, generous leading keeping the room low and calm
Topology/navigation: the primary task sits in the sunken center; peripheral content stays on the surrounding terrace level.
Controls/state: descending into a section is a level change with a visible step; focus literally lowers and warms.
Responsive/motion: on phones the pit becomes a full-bleed room; level changes ease like sitting down, never bounce.
concepts.spark: Three steps down, the room becomes a nest: burnt-orange cushions, a teak rail at eye level, and everything important within arm's reach.
concepts.webLeverage: Depth staged with scroll-driven scale and shadow, plus a focus model that keyboard users traverse level by level.

concepts.form: the 0.10 exhibition corner in petrograd, a black square hung high where the icon belongs while tilted painted planes swarm the white walls below it
concepts.lineage: Kazimir Malevich's 0.10 exhibition 1915, Suprematist canvases, the Russian icon-corner tradition
system: Palette/material: gallery-white field as ground, the black square as absolute anchor and ink, suprematist red and yellow bars rationed to planes in an active state
Type/composition: bare geometric sans fragments tilted with their planes, no ruled grid at all, mass and angle ranking the reading order across the white field
Topology/navigation: one element earns the high corner as absolute anchor; everything else drifts on a white field ranked by tilt and mass, never by rows
Controls/state: controls are bare geometric planes; selecting one squares its tilt to true, dismissing it lets the plane drift off the field's edge
Responsive/motion: the white field extends past every viewport and re-clusters planes by mass; motion is slow orbital drift
concepts.spark: In a cold Petrograd room a black square hangs where the icon of Christ should be, and beneath it painted planes float free of gravity on walls crowded to the ceiling.
concepts.webLeverage: absolute positioning on a pannable oversize canvas with CSS transforms keeps every plane's tilt and drift mathematically exact

concepts.form: a Swiss International Style concert-poster wall, where one modular grid disciplines objective headlines, geometric rhythm, and photographic fragments across a series
concepts.lineage: Josef Müller-Brockmann's Zürich Tonhalle posters, Basel school grid systems, 1950s Swiss typography
system: Palette/material: unprinted poster white ground, objective black akzidenz ink for body, one saturated signal red or blue per piece marking the current selection
Type/composition: akzidenz-grotesk set flush left ragged right on the module, sizes stepped in grid units, geometric arcs and bars serving as the only imagery
Topology/navigation: one master grid governs every page; sections differ by geometric motif, never by layout anarchy.
Controls/state: controls are typographic; active states shift weight and bar position on the grid, not color noise.
Responsive/motion: the module count adapts per breakpoint while column rhythm stays; motion is grid-snapped.
concepts.spark: Twelve posters, one grid: each concert gets its own geometry of arcs and bars, yet the wall reads as a single calm intelligence.
concepts.webLeverage: A CSS grid exposed as a visible design surface; filters re-sort the series in real time without breaking the module.

concepts.form: a dead shopping mall atrium at closing time, marble fountain still running, plastic palms and teal-pink neon reflected in escalators that go nowhere
concepts.lineage: Gruen-era mall architecture, Floral Shoppe cover language, muzak tape loops, early web gradients
system: Palette/material: teal-to-pink dusk gradient ground, fountain-marble white for panels, faded palm green as texture, dead-brand neon magenta humming on the active sign
Type/composition: chrome-extruded serif display with full-width letterspacing, times italic and katakana glosses in captions, layout mirrored around the fountain axis
Topology/navigation: space is concentric rings around a fountain court; you drift by escalator between levels that repeat with small decays
Controls/state: signage is dead-brand neon; hover hums a tube up to full glow while idle states flicker with the wiring of a closed store
Responsive/motion: the atrium compresses to one reflective corridor on narrow screens; all motion runs thirty percent slow
concepts.spark: Somewhere below, a fountain still runs for nobody, pink dusk pours through the skylight grid, and the muzak is a love song slowed down until it aches.
concepts.webLeverage: Web Audio time-stretching and CSS gradient animation keep the atrium's dusk loop and slowed soundtrack in one shared tempo

concepts.form: a Y2K translucent-tech lounge, where candy-colored polycarbonate shells, chrome blobs, and aqua gloss promise a friendly frictionless millennium
concepts.lineage: Late-90s iMac G3 translucency, Aqua-era interface gloss, blobject product design and inflatable furniture
system: Palette/material: aqua-gloss white ground, bondi blue, tangerine, and lime polycarbonate shells as panels, graphite body ink, internal cyan glow filling the live control
Type/composition: a rounded techno sans with wide apertures set in pill lozenges, labels centered under the gloss, stacking ruled by each shell's shallow curve
Topology/navigation: panels are translucent shells stacked in shallow depth; what sits behind a surface stays faintly visible.
Controls/state: controls are glossy capsules with internal glow states; progress shows as liquid filling the shell.
Responsive/motion: shells flatten to frosted layers on low power; gloss highlights track pointer only on fine pointers.
concepts.spark: Everything glows from inside its candy shell: the hardware shows its organs, the buttons look wet, and the future feels friendly.
concepts.webLeverage: Backdrop-filter translucency and pointer-tracked specular highlights render the material honestly in CSS.

concepts.form: an alhambra courtyard lined in hand-cut zellige, cobalt, ochre, green, and white tesserae locking into girih symmetry beneath carved muqarnas and calligraphic friezes, a still pool doubling the ornament
concepts.lineage: Nasrid dynasty craft at the Alhambra, girih and zellige traditions, cursive thuluth friezes, Owen Jones's Grammar of Ornament plates
system: Palette/material: glazed zellige cobalt, ochre, copper green, and bone white over warm stucco cream ground, deep sepia body ink, the cobalt star cell marking the active state
Type/composition: cursive calligraphic friezes banding the section heads with geometric kufic accents, content panels framed in tiled borders, layout mirrored on the pool's axis
Topology/navigation: rooms open off a central reflecting court; every route is symmetric about the water axis and each threshold is a framed arch
Controls/state: controls are single tesserae in the pattern; hover raises the glaze's gleam, selection rotates the star's fill while the girih lattice holds
Responsive/motion: the pattern re-tessellates at smaller symmetry orders per viewport, never cropping mid-star; motion is water shimmer over glaze
concepts.spark: Water holds perfectly still in the courtyard's center, doubling ten thousand hand-cut tiles; cobalt stars lock into white eight-folds up the wall until the geometry dissolves overhead into carved stucco honeycomb.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG pattern tiles built from one girih rule set repeat losslessly at every scale, with CSS transforms rotating star cells in place

concepts.form: a creator-hardware desk instrument, bone and putty keycaps with dye-sublimated mono legends gridded into a gunmetal chassis, one safety-orange action key, knurled aluminum knobs, and a small amber status screen
concepts.lineage: Teenage Engineering OP-1 and TX-6, Work Louder creator boards, Panic Playdate, mechanical-keycap colorway culture, Braun functionalism inherited
system: Palette/material: bone and putty keycap grays on gunmetal, charcoal legends as body ink, safety orange reserved for the action that matters, amber screen glow as live state
Type/composition: small dye-sub mono legends centered on every key with silkscreened corner icons, the layout a strict keycap grid broken by one satisfying asymmetry
Topology/navigation: functions live as physical keys in a grid, families group by row and accent color, and the knob owns anything continuous
Controls/state: every control clicks with tactile certainty, active modes light their key, the amber screen reports one value at a time, orange keys commit
Responsive/motion: the grid reflows by whole key units, never fractional; motion is key-travel snap and knob detents
concepts.spark: Your thumb finds the knurled knob without looking; a quarter-detent turn, the amber screen ticks from 9:00 to 9:15, and the one orange key under your index finger is obviously, satisfyingly, the point.
concepts.webLeverage: css grid and layered shadows model keycap physics, :active states give real key travel, and a drag-driven knob scrubs values with full keyboard parity

concepts.form: korean dancheong bracket work, structural timber wrapped in a codified five-color system, lotus and cloud bands repeating along beams, pigment ranking the building it protects
concepts.lineage: Korean dancheong painting guilds, obangsaek five-color cosmology, Joseon temple and palace polychromy
system: Palette/material: the obangsaek set, blue, red, yellow, white, black, laid over deep green beam ground; red heads the hierarchy, white outlines every band edge
Type/composition: content bands wrap linear members end to end, headers as bracket-end medallions, repeating lotus and cloud units metered evenly along each beam
Topology/navigation: structure is the map; primary beams carry primary sections, brackets branch to sub-items, and rank is read from how ornate the wrap is
Controls/state: state shows as ornament grade, plain timber for disabled, single-band for resting, full five-color wrap for active, white edging sharpens on focus
Responsive/motion: bands shorten their repeat count but never their unit size on narrow screens; motion is a slow ripple along a band's repeats
concepts.spark: You stand under temple eaves at dusk looking up into stacked brackets, five colors stepping through lotus bands along every beam, white outlines holding each shape apart, the timber underneath hidden and ranked.
concepts.webLeverage: css border-image and repeating gradients meter the band units, keeping repeats intact instead of stretching them

concepts.form: an eighties shopping mall after close, terrazzo floors and brass rails under disciplined neon script, glass elevators rising through fountain light, retail modernism taken straight
concepts.lineage: Gruen-era mall architecture, eighties retail signage craft, neon bending shops, terrazzo and brass interior systems
system: Palette/material: warm terrazzo gray ground flecked with brass, deep evening teal shadows, one rose neon tube as the accent, its glow pooled only on the active storefront
Type/composition: one restrained neon script for names over a quiet geometric sans for everything else, storefronts ranked on a strict level grid, no stacked novelty faces
Topology/navigation: the atrium organizes everything; levels ring the fountain, the glass elevator is the vertical axis and the directory map is a lit cross-section
Controls/state: the open storefront hums with its neon lit, closed ones sit behind drawn grilles at half light, hover raises the grille a hand's width
Responsive/motion: levels stack into one scrolling promenade on phones; motion is the elevator's slow rise and fountain shimmer
concepts.spark: you ride the glass elevator alone after close, the fountain below throwing slow light on the brass rails, and one rose neon script hums over a dark storefront while your steps echo off terrazzo
concepts.webLeverage: css text-shadow layers do the neon tube glow, scroll-driven animation rides the elevator between levels, blend modes pool light on terrazzo

concepts.form: an upscale galleria at midnight, brass rails and terrazzo floors lit only by each shop's hand-bent neon signature, every logotype reflected once in glass and once in polished stone
concepts.lineage: Postwar shopping arcades, Milan and Osaka galleria interiors, neon sign craft, department-store wayfinding
system: Palette/material: espresso-dark ground, terrazzo gray and brushed brass structure, each section owning a single jewel neon hue, ruby, emerald or sapphire, never mixed in one view
Type/composition: every destination gets a hand-bent neon logotype in script or thin caps, while body copy sits in a quiet grotesque on dark directory boards with brass rules
Topology/navigation: the illuminated floor directory is the map, storefronts are sections along a corridor, and the escalator between floors is the level change
Controls/state: idle signs rest at half glow, hover hums the tube to full brightness, the open section spills warm light on the terrazzo, closed ones read CLOSED in small brass
Responsive/motion: the galleria compresses to one storefront corridor on phones, and motion is only the neon warm-up and a slow escalator glide
concepts.spark: Your footsteps echo on terrazzo as one emerald script hums awake over the milliner's glass, its reflection pooling at your feet, the rest of the corridor waiting in half-lit brass.
concepts.webLeverage: svg filters render tube glow and its doubled reflection, and view transitions carry the escalator glide between floors.

concepts.form: a Wim Crouwel gridded type specimen, where letterforms are built cell by cell on a visible construction grid and the poster is the proof
concepts.lineage: Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet, Total Design, and the Stedelijk exhibition catalogs
concepts.spark: Faint blue gridlines cover the sheet like graph paper; enormous letterforms assemble themselves from its cells, and one diagonal is the only rebellion the system permits.
system: Palette/material: white or one stark saturated ground, faint construction-grid hairlines, one accent plane earned by the headline
Type/composition: monumental grid-constructed letterforms over small neutral grotesk; the layout grid stays visible as part of the design
Topology/navigation: Move by cell, by letter, and by catalog entry.
Controls/state: Reveal construction, snap to cells, and toggle grid visibility as a real state.
Responsive/motion: The page reflows by whole cells; letterforms rebuild cell by cell when content changes.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS grid as the literal visible armature with display letterforms drawn from the same grid tokens

concepts.form: a 1914 manifesto magazine page set entirely in wood type, words blasted and blessed in stacked slabs running at right angles, black rules cutting the field into hard diagonal wedges
concepts.lineage: Wyndham Lewis's BLAST and the London Vorticist group, wood-type manifesto setting, 1914 to 1915
system: Palette/material: puce paper stock with one heavy black ink, no image and no halftone, the type mass itself carrying every value
Type/composition: enormous condensed wood-type caps stacked in unequal slabs, rotated ninety degrees, split by thick rules into diagonal wedges
Topology/navigation: the page is a list of blasts and blesses, so navigation is a stacked manifesto where each item is its own typographic slab
Controls/state: controls are type slabs, the active one takes full black weight, and the rest reverse out of the puce ground
Responsive/motion: slabs restack rather than shrink as frames narrow, and motion is a hard ninety-degree rotation of one wedge at a time
concepts.spark: the whole page is shouting in wood type, half of it turned sideways, thick rules slicing the puce paper into wedges, and there is not one picture anywhere because the letters are doing the hitting.
concepts.webLeverage: css writing-mode for rotated slabs, clip-path wedge rules, and a responsive restack that never scales the type down

concepts.form: a dada assemblage page built from tram tickets, torn newsprint, and mixed type cases, rules and printers' fists dragged in at angles so the composition reads as a found object rather than a layout
concepts.lineage: Kurt Schwitters's Merz, Cabaret Voltaire and Berlin dada typography, printers' case improvisation, 1916 to 1923
system: Palette/material: aged ticket stock, newsprint gray, and one dull red, everything sitting at slightly different paper ages and thicknesses
Type/composition: every size and face at once from a raided case, printers' fists and rules pointing across the field, no dominant axis
Topology/navigation: the field is a pinboard of scraps, and navigation means pulling one scrap forward while the rest keep their positions
Controls/state: controls are pasted scraps, pressing one lifts it with a small shadow, and used ones settle back into the collage
Responsive/motion: scraps repack rather than scale as the frame changes, and motion is a paste-and-lift with no smooth easing
concepts.spark: a tram ticket, half a headline, a printer's fist pointing at nothing in particular, and eleven sizes of type from the same raided case, all glued down at angles that should not work and completely do.
concepts.webLeverage: a responsive collage that repacks scraps, css transforms for lift and paste states, and pointer-driven z-order reordering

concepts.form: a prague crystalline interior where every plane is faceted into prisms, the facade folded into repeating diamond bays and the printed matter carrying the same crystal grammar in rules and initials
concepts.lineage: Pavel Janak and Josef Gocar's Czech cubist architecture and furniture, Umelecky mesicnik pages, Prague 1911 to 1914
system: Palette/material: raked white plaster and dark oak against smoked glass, values created by facet angle rather than by pigment
Type/composition: sharp angular caps with faceted terminals, rules broken into chevrons, and initials cut like gems into the text block
Topology/navigation: space is a run of faceted bays, and moving means turning a facet toward you so a new plane catches the light
Controls/state: controls are prism plates, the active one turns its bright face forward, and inactive ones sit in raked shadow
Responsive/motion: facets subdivide or merge with the frame width, and motion is an angular fold rather than a slide or a fade
concepts.spark: even the doorframe is folded into diamonds, the plaster catches the light on one facet and drops the next into shadow, and the book on the table has initials cut like gemstones out of the same idea.
concepts.webLeverage: css 3d transforms folding facet planes, clip-path prism controls, and light response driven by pointer motion

concepts.form: a depthless field where one grinning motif repeats at five different scales at once, some filling the frame and some barely a speck, all at identical saturation with no shadow to say which is nearer
concepts.lineage: the Superflat exhibition program and studio graphic system, published flatness manifesto and multi-scale motif fields, 2000 onward
system: Palette/material: candy saturation at full strength, every color sealed inside a clean black contour, and a flat ground that never recedes
Type/composition: rounded display caps sitting on the same plane as the artwork, one motif repeated at five scales simultaneously with no perspective cue
Topology/navigation: scale is the only depth cue and it is a lie, so navigation zooms between scales and never actually arrives anywhere
Controls/state: controls are motif instances, the active one jumps a whole scale step, and inactive ones hold their place in the swarm
Responsive/motion: the swarm redistributes across any frame, and motion is a flat scale jump with no perspective and no shadow
concepts.spark: the same grinning flower filling half the frame and also appearing eleven times the size of a full stop, both at exactly the same saturation, with nothing anywhere to tell you which one is closer.
concepts.webLeverage: generative svg motif placement across scale steps, flat scale-jump transforms on state, and a responsive redistributing swarm

concepts.form: a balkan avant-garde review page assembling latin and cyrillic wood type on one asymmetric field, heavy bars driving diagonally under stacked manifesto lines and a numbered issue mark in the corner
concepts.lineage: Ljubomir Micic's Zenit review, Zagreb and Belgrade avant-garde typography, 1921 to 1926
system: Palette/material: rough gray stock with black and one alarm red, ink sitting unevenly so the bars show press texture at their edges
Type/composition: mixed wood-type weights stacked at hard left, heavy bars running diagonally beneath, and a numbered issue mark boxed in one corner
Topology/navigation: the review is a numbered run, and moving means advancing the issue mark while the bar angle shifts to a new degree
Controls/state: controls are bar-anchored words, the active bar takes the alarm red, and spent ones drop to a hairline
Responsive/motion: bars re-angle rather than shorten as the frame narrows, and motion is a bar sweeping in from the sheet edge
concepts.spark: stacked lines hard against the left edge, a red bar cutting under them at an angle nobody would choose today, and a small boxed number in the corner insisting this is issue eleven of a revolution.
concepts.webLeverage: css transforms re-angling bars responsive, a numbered issue state in the url, and bar sweep animation on transition

concepts.form: a krakow secession review page where a stylized folk-flower border grows in from the margins toward hand-drawn display lettering, the text block sitting inside the growth like a clearing
concepts.lineage: Stanislaw Wyspianski's Chimera and Zycie pages, Krakow secession print, Polish folk motif stylization, 1897 to 1918
system: Palette/material: warm ivory stock with sap green, dusty rose and a deep slate, ornament printed in flat areas with a fine outline
Type/composition: hand-drawn display lettering with organic terminals, a symmetrical border growing inward, and body text ranged in one calm column
Topology/navigation: sections open as clearings inside the ornament, and moving grows a new border in while the previous one recedes
Controls/state: controls are ornament nodes, the active one flowers open, and inactive ones stay as closed buds along the stem
Responsive/motion: the border thins to a single stem on narrow frames, and motion is a slow growth along the stem rather than a fade
concepts.spark: the flowers come in from all four margins, stylized until they are almost geometry, and they leave exactly enough room in the middle for a poem that clearly thinks it is important.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg border that animates its stroke as growth, responsive stem simplification, and node controls bound to focus state

concepts.form: a glasgow tearoom interior stretched vertically into thin black uprights, a stencilled rose repeating at eye height and elongated lettering standing as tall and narrow as the chairbacks
concepts.lineage: Charles Rennie Mackintosh and the Glasgow Four, the stencilled Glasgow rose, tearoom and Scottish Musical Review work, 1896 onward
system: Palette/material: chalk white and lamp black with rose pink and leaf green used only inside the stencil, oak stained almost to black
Type/composition: extremely elongated caps with squared terminals, everything hung from a tall vertical grid, the rose repeating on one horizontal band
Topology/navigation: the world is read vertically, and moving means rising or dropping through bands rather than moving sideways
Controls/state: controls are tall uprights, the active one carries the stencilled rose, and the rest hold plain black
Responsive/motion: uprights narrow but never shorten as frames change, and motion is a vertical rise with the rose fading in last
concepts.spark: everything in the room is taller than it needs to be, black uprights running floor to ceiling, and at exactly eye height a small pink stencilled rose repeating like a held note.
concepts.webLeverage: a css vertical grid that preserves height responsive, an svg stencil rose reveal, and motion tied to scroll state

concepts.form: a paris hoarding stripped back by hand, layers of pasted posters torn through to expose four earlier campaigns at once, the ragged tear edges becoming the only composition anybody planned
concepts.lineage: Jacques Villegle and Raymond Hains's decollage of Paris billboards, affiches lacerees, 1949 to 1962
system: Palette/material: aged poster inks bleached to chalk, paste-gray backing board, and the pale fibrous edge every tear exposes
Type/composition: fragments of four type systems at four scales coexisting, no fragment complete, reading order set by tear depth alone
Topology/navigation: depth is history, so navigation is tearing further down into older layers rather than moving across the surface
Controls/state: controls are torn flaps, pulling one exposes the layer beneath, and exposed layers stay exposed as a record
Responsive/motion: tears regenerate to fit any frame, and motion is a paper rip that accelerates and then catches
concepts.spark: somebody tore a strip off a wall of posters and found a concert from four years ago underneath, then another, then another, and the accidental edges are better than anything on any of the sheets.
concepts.webLeverage: layered svg tear masks generated responsive, pointer-driven reveal of lower strata, and persistent exposed state

concepts.form: a civic plate for a rebuilt green city, art-nouveau whiplash line drawn around photovoltaic hexagon geometry, a tiled roofline of panels and climbing plants sharing the same repeating unit
concepts.lineage: the published solarpunk illustration and manifesto anthology program, art-nouveau line over photovoltaic geometry, 2014 onward
system: Palette/material: warm brass-free ochre and leaf green over cream, with panel blue as the only cool note and a fine dark outline holding all forms
Type/composition: an art-nouveau display face with vegetal terminals, a hexagon tiling as the underlying grid, and captions ranged along the tile edges
Topology/navigation: the city is a tiling, so navigation is moving to an adjacent hexagon rather than descending a menu
Controls/state: controls are hex tiles, the active one puts out a climbing vine to its neighbor, and dormant ones hold plain panel blue
Responsive/motion: the hex tiling reflows in whole units, and motion is a vine growing along the tile boundary
concepts.spark: the roofline and the ivy turn out to be built on the same hexagon, and the lettering has leaves on it, and nobody involved has apologized for the optimism.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg hex tiling that reflows responsive, animated vine growth along tile paths, and adjacency navigation state

concepts.form: a canvas that quotes a state poster style back at itself, heroic diagonal figures and slogan banners rendered exactly to the official manner but carrying an invented emblem, gallery labels ruled beside it
concepts.lineage: the Sots Art appropriation of Soviet agitprop by Komar and Melamid and their circle, 1972 onward
system: Palette/material: state red and ochre over primed canvas, painted in an official finish, with gallery-white as the only surrounding material
Type/composition: slogan banners in heavy official caps set at a rising diagonal, the invented emblem centered, and a small ruled label set beside
Topology/navigation: every view is a quotation with a caption, so navigation moves between quoted works and the labels that undercut them
Controls/state: controls are banner slogans, the active one takes full state red, and the rest hold at label gray
Responsive/motion: banners re-angle their diagonal to the frame, and motion is a banner rising into place and stopping hard
concepts.spark: it is painted exactly the way the real ones were painted, same red, same rising diagonal, same certainty, and the emblem in the middle stands for absolutely nothing at all.
concepts.webLeverage: css transforms re-angling banner diagonals, label state paired to each work, and a rising banner animation

concepts.form: a nineteen-twenties commercial revival plate, lotus and scarab motifs stacked into a stepped cartouche frame, gold-line ornament ruling a cinema front and its packaging in the same borrowed grammar
concepts.lineage: 1920s Egyptian revival commercial print and cinema front design following the 1922 tomb opening, packaging and poster ornament
system: Palette/material: lapis blue and carnelian over cream board with a fine gold rule, all ornament printed flat with no rendered relief
Type/composition: stacked geometric caps inside a stepped cartouche, a lotus band ruling the head and foot, symmetry enforced on the vertical axis
Topology/navigation: the cartouche is the container, so navigation opens a new cartouche while the banding stays constant
Controls/state: controls are cartouche cells, the active one takes the gold rule, and inactive ones sit in flat lapis
Responsive/motion: the lotus band repeats in whole motifs, and motion is a cartouche stepping open along its axis
concepts.spark: a cinema front, a biscuit tin and a cigarette packet all suddenly covered in lotus and scarab in 1923, printed flat in lapis and carnelian with a gold rule, because a tomb got opened.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg motif band repeating in whole units responsive, a stepped cartouche open animation, and gold-rule accent state

concepts.form: a regional design movement's pattern program, an interlaced geometric alphabet and furniture ornament derived from local stone and embroidery, published as a plate book of repeatable units and letterforms
concepts.lineage: the Seiz Breur Breton design movement, its published ornament and alphabet program derived from regional craft, 1923 to 1947
system: Palette/material: slate gray and oatmeal with one madder red, printed flat on plate stock with a fine keyline defining every unit
Type/composition: a geometric constructed alphabet with squared terminals, ornament units ranged on a numbered plate, captions ruled at the foot
Topology/navigation: the plate book is a parts catalog, so navigation assembles units into a border rather than browsing pages
Controls/state: controls are ornament units, the active one snaps into the assembled border, and unused units stay ranged on the plate
Responsive/motion: assembled borders repeat in whole units, and motion is a unit sliding into the border and locking
concepts.spark: a whole alphabet and a whole ornament grammar, worked out from carved stone and embroidery, printed as a numbered plate book so anyone in the region could build with it.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg unit assembly with drag placement, whole-unit responsive borders, and a lock-in animation on placement

concepts.form: a catalan civic programme of measured classicism, a mediterranean figure held inside a ruled arcade with proportion marks visible, its printed matter set in a calm humanist face on a strict two-part page
concepts.lineage: the Noucentisme civic and publishing programme in Catalonia, measured classicism and its printed order, 1906 to 1923
system: Palette/material: lime white and terracotta with mediterranean blue, matte plaster and unglazed tile, no gloss on any surface
Type/composition: a calm humanist serif on a two-part page, arcade bays ruled at even intervals, and small proportion marks left visible in the margin
Topology/navigation: bays repeat at a fixed interval, so navigation steps one bay at a time along a measured arcade
Controls/state: controls are bays, the active one is marked by a terracotta impost, and inactive ones hold plain lime
Responsive/motion: bays add or drop in whole intervals, and motion is a measured step with no acceleration
concepts.spark: everything measured, everything calm, an arcade of even bays in lime and terracotta with the proportion marks left showing in the margin because somebody was proud of the arithmetic.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-interval responsive bay grid, stepped navigation state, and a measured linear motion curve

concepts.form: a collective's painted plate built from a shared symbol set, hard-edged figures and hovering objects in a fixed palette, each work signed with a member's invented pseudonym mark in one corner
concepts.lineage: the Toyism art collective's shared symbol program and pseudonym signing convention, hard-edge collective painting, 1992 onward
system: Palette/material: a fixed collective palette of cobalt, magenta and lemon on a flat ground, hard edges with no blending permitted anywhere
Type/composition: a compact geometric sans for titles, hard-edged figures with hovering objects, and a small pseudonym mark locked to one corner
Topology/navigation: the symbol set is shared, so navigation moves between members' works that reuse the same vocabulary differently
Controls/state: controls are symbols, the active one hovers clear of the ground, and inactive ones sit flat against it
Responsive/motion: symbols reposition without ever overlapping the pseudonym mark, and motion is a slow hover drift
concepts.spark: the same handful of symbols turning up in twelve different painters' work, each one signed with an invented name in the corner, and none of them will tell you which is which.
concepts.webLeverage: responsive svg symbol placement, a hover-drift animation on state, and per-member attribution state

concepts.form: a monumental state mural panel, idealized workers arranged on a rising diagonal with a banner slogan ruled across the base, painted in a fixed official palette with the horizon line always low
concepts.lineage: the socialist realist mural and poster program, official idealized figure painting and slogan banner convention, 1932 onward
system: Palette/material: earth ochre, wheat and state red on plaster, painted matte with a single warm light source and no cast ambiguity
Type/composition: figures on a rising diagonal seen from below, a slogan banner ruled across the base, and the horizon kept low in every panel
Topology/navigation: panels sequence as a program, so navigation advances along a wall from panel to panel at a fixed height
Controls/state: controls are banner segments, the active one takes state red, and inactive ones stay in wheat
Responsive/motion: panels crop from the edges and the low horizon never moves, and motion is a lateral pan along the wall
concepts.spark: everyone painted from slightly below so they look taller than you, arranged on a diagonal going up and to the right, with the slogan ruled along the bottom in case you missed it.
concepts.webLeverage: responsive panel cropping with a fixed horizon, lateral pan motion, and banner segment accent state

concepts.form: a nineties domestic interior program of ironic gothic curves, wrought scrollwork and crescent-moon motifs set against sponged jewel walls, its printed matter carrying the same curling arch and star furniture
concepts.lineage: the 1990s whimsigothic interior and print program, wrought scroll and crescent motif decorating, sponged wall finishes
system: Palette/material: sponged aubergine and teal walls with wrought black scrollwork, gauze and beaded texture, and no flat painted surface
Type/composition: a curling display face with pointed terminals, arch-topped panels, and crescent and star motifs scattered as furniture
Topology/navigation: arches are doorways, so navigation passes through an arch-topped panel into the next room
Controls/state: controls are scroll ends, the active one curls open, and inactive ones stay coiled against the arch
Responsive/motion: arch panels reflow in whole openings, and motion is a scroll uncurling along its own spiral
concepts.spark: sponged aubergine walls, wrought iron curling around a mirror, a crescent moon somewhere it has no business being, and every doorway topped with a point.
concepts.webLeverage: svg scroll paths uncurling along a spiral, whole-opening responsive arch panels, and sponged css texture layers

concepts.form: a late-socialist city's satirical television graphic, a hand-cut photomontage head over a hard geometric ground with a station ident stamped into the corner and a scrolling caption band running crooked beneath
concepts.lineage: the Sarajevo New Primitivism movement and its satirical television and record graphics, hand-cut photomontage, 1980s
system: Palette/material: broadcast primaries printed flat over a coarse halftone photograph, colors slightly off from television-safe so everything looks marginally wrong
Type/composition: a hand-cut photomontage head over hard geometric fields, a station ident stamped in one corner, and a caption band set deliberately crooked
Topology/navigation: the crooked band carries the running commentary, so navigation follows the caption rather than the picture
Controls/state: controls are caption segments, the active one straightens briefly, and passed ones tilt further off level
Responsive/motion: the montage crops and the band re-angles at any width, and motion is a caption crawl with a slight wobble
concepts.spark: a head cut out with scissors and stuck on a flat orange field, a station ident stamped in the corner like an official approval, and a caption crawling underneath at three degrees off level.
concepts.webLeverage: css transforms re-angling the caption band, a wobbling crawl animation, and responsive montage cropping

concepts.form: a painted industrial plate reducing grain elevators and stacks to hard-edged planes, every form flattened into overlapping geometric shapes lit by one raking light, a stenciled numeral standing in for a title
concepts.lineage: American Precisionist painting and its industrial subject plates, hard-edge planar reduction and stenciled numeral titling, 1920s
system: Palette/material: chalk white, slate and rust in flat unmodulated planes, one raking light source producing hard shadow shapes with no soft edge
Type/composition: forms reduced to overlapping geometric planes, a large stenciled numeral placed as the only typographic element, no human figure anywhere
Topology/navigation: planes overlap in a fixed depth order, so navigation slides one plane aside to reveal what it was covering
Controls/state: controls are planes, the active one takes the light, and inactive ones fall into their own hard shadow
Responsive/motion: planes re-overlap to any frame, and motion is a light source rotating and the shadow shapes swinging with it
concepts.spark: a grain elevator reduced to six flat shapes and one hard shadow, painted with such conviction that it becomes architecture, with a stenciled number where the title should be.
concepts.webLeverage: svg planar shapes re-overlapping responsive, a rotating light source recomputing shadows, and plane state in the depth order

concepts.form: a manuscript carpet page where interlace fills every square millimeter, ribbon bands knotting through themselves in panels of different weave, a single small void left near one corner as the only place the eye can rest
concepts.lineage: Insular manuscript carpet pages, ribbon and zoomorphic interlace panels, Irish revival republishing of the plates
system: Palette/material: vellum cream with orpiment yellow, verdigris and oxblood, every color bounded by a fine dark interlace line and no area left unfilled
Type/composition: panels of differently weighted interlace butted against each other, framed by a knotted border, with one small void reserved near a corner
Topology/navigation: the weave is continuous, so navigation follows a single ribbon as it passes over and under across panels
Controls/state: controls are ribbon strands, the active one lifts over its crossings, and inactive ones pass beneath
Responsive/motion: interlace panels retile in whole weave units, and motion is a ribbon traced along its full path
concepts.spark: every square millimeter is filled with ribbon knotting through itself, four different weaves butted together, and one tiny empty patch near the corner that is the only place your eye is allowed to stop.
