Controls/state: controls are modifications, the active one draws its leader and rule, and non-conforming ones are marked with a struck line
Responsive/motion: callouts reposition around the figure at any width, and motion is a leader line drawing out to its label
concepts.spark: the skirt lengthened by exactly this much, the top shortened by exactly that much, every deviation measured and annotated, and the stripe on the collar telling you who she answers to.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg figure with animated leader-line callouts, responsive callout repositioning, and conformance state per modification

concepts.form: a stadium end assembling one enormous image from thousands of held cards, each seat issued a single colored square and a seat number, the picture existing only while every person holds their card up at once
concepts.lineage: European supporters' tifo card mosaics, seat-numbered card issue and choreography sheets, painted stand banners
system: Palette/material: a restricted set of six card colors printed matte, held against dark clothing so the mosaic reads only in aggregate
Type/composition: the image resolves at stand scale from a square grid, with a painted banner strip carrying hand-lettered caps beneath it
Topology/navigation: the grid is the map and every cell is a seat, so navigation zooms between the whole picture and one person's square
Controls/state: controls are seats, the active one raises its card into the image, and an empty seat leaves a visible hole in the picture
Responsive/motion: the mosaic re-resolves at any grid size, and motion is a wave of cards rising row by row across the stand
concepts.spark: eleven thousand people each holding up one colored square, and from across the pitch it is a face; from where you are sitting it is a piece of card with a seat number on the back.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg grid mosaic that re-resolves responsive, per-cell state raising cards, and a row-by-row wave animation

concepts.form: a japanese fashion mook spread, coordinate photographs shingled across a printed lace ground with hand-drawn annotation ribbons naming every garment, and a bound-in paper pattern sheet folded into the gutter
concepts.lineage: Japanese gothic and lolita mook publishing, coordinate photography spreads, annotation ribbon captions and bound-in pattern sheets
system: Palette/material: ink black and blood red over a printed lace ground on cream stock, with one bound-in tissue sheet at a different paper weight
Type/composition: coordinate photographs shingled across the spread, hand-drawn ribbon captions naming each garment, and a folded pattern sheet in the gutter
Topology/navigation: the spread is a shingle of coordinates, so navigation pulls one photograph forward from under the others
Controls/state: controls are ribbon captions, the active one unfurls to full length, and inactive ones stay curled against the photograph
Responsive/motion: the shingle restacks vertically on narrow frames, and motion is a ribbon unfurling along its own curve
concepts.spark: every garment in the photograph has a hand-drawn ribbon curling out of it with its name written on, and folded into the middle of the book is a tissue pattern sheet for making the whole thing yourself.
concepts.webLeverage: responsive shingle restacking, svg ribbon paths that unfurl on hover state, and a fold-out sheet reveal

concepts.form: a pastel character sheet where a cute mascot is drawn with bandages, safety pins and a syringe as ordinary accessories, the whole thing set on candy pink with a hand-drawn cross motif repeating as border furniture
concepts.lineage: Japanese menhera character illustration and yami kawaii merchandise design, pastel-with-hardware motif vocabulary, 2014 onward
system: Palette/material: candy pink and mint at full strength with black hardware line, everything outlined heavily so the accessories read as clearly as the character
Type/composition: a rounded bubble face for labels, a centered character with hardware accessories, and a hand-drawn cross motif repeating as a border
Topology/navigation: the border is a repeating motif run, so navigation moves along cross motifs that each open a character variant
Controls/state: controls are motif crosses, the active one takes the black hardware line, and inactive ones stay pastel outline
Responsive/motion: the border repeats in whole motifs, and motion is a hardware element swinging on its pin
concepts.spark: a mascot as sweet as anything on a stationery shelf, wearing a bandage over one eye and a safety pin through its ear, on a pink so bright it hurts.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg motif border repeating in whole units responsive, a swing animation on hardware elements, and variant state per cross

concepts.form: a congolese dandy portrait plate, a figure posed full length against a plain painted backdrop in a precisely coordinated three-color suit, the label of every garment named in a caption ruled beneath the frame
concepts.lineage: Congolese sapeur portrait photography and its studio backdrop tradition, coordinated color dressing and named-label caption practice
system: Palette/material: a plain painted studio backdrop in one flat hue behind suiting in exactly three coordinated colors, everything photographed in even frontal light
Type/composition: a full-length figure centered on the backdrop, a ruled caption beneath naming each garment's label, and a thin printed frame around the plate
Topology/navigation: the plate is a portrait series, so navigation moves between figures whose color coordination changes against the same backdrop
Controls/state: controls are garment captions, the active one draws a leader to its garment, and named ones keep a small printed tick
Responsive/motion: the backdrop crops around the held figure, and motion is a backdrop hue change between plates
concepts.spark: a man standing perfectly still against a painted wall in a suit of exactly three colors that should not work together and completely do, with every label named in a line underneath.
concepts.webLeverage: svg leader lines from caption to garment on hover state, responsive backdrop cropping, and hue transitions between plates

concepts.form: a lowbrow gallery panel crowding hot-rod monsters, tiki idols and pin-up figures into one airbrushed tableau, every element outlined in black and lacquered to a show finish with a hand-lettered title panel across the base
concepts.lineage: the Lowbrow and pop-surrealist gallery movement, airbrushed hot-rod and tiki iconography, hand-lettered title panels, 1979 onward
system: Palette/material: candy lacquer color airbrushed to a show finish, every form held by a heavy black outline, and no unpainted area anywhere in the panel
Type/composition: a crowded tableau of outlined figures at competing scales, and a hand-lettered title panel ruled across the base of the board
Topology/navigation: the panel is packed, so navigation moves between figures competing for the same space rather than through a hierarchy
Controls/state: controls are figures, the active one gains a second outline and a lacquer highlight, and inactive ones flatten
Responsive/motion: the tableau repacks its figures at any width, and motion is a lacquer highlight travelling across the panel
concepts.spark: a monster driving a hot rod, a tiki idol, and a woman in cat-eye glasses all fighting for the same three square feet of board, every one outlined in black and lacquered until it shines.
concepts.webLeverage: a responsive repacking tableau, css lacquer highlight travel on pointer, and outline state per figure

concepts.form: a convention circle catalog printed on newsprint, thousands of hand-drawn thumbnail squares packed into a numbered hall grid, each square carrying a circle name, a table code and a drawing done at postage-stamp size
concepts.lineage: Japanese doujin convention circle catalogs, hall grid table-coding and hand-drawn thumbnail submission, newsprint catalog printing
system: Palette/material: single-ink black on cheap newsprint that grays under the thumb, with one spot color used only on the hall map dividers
Type/composition: postage-stamp thumbnails packed edge to edge in a numbered grid, circle names set tiny beneath, and a folded hall map keyed to the codes
Topology/navigation: the hall map and the grid are the same space, so navigation moves between a table code and its physical position
Controls/state: controls are thumbnail cells, the active one is circled in pen, and visited ones are struck through by hand
Responsive/motion: the grid repacks in whole cells, and motion is a jump from a catalog cell to its position on the hall map
concepts.spark: eight hundred drawings on one page, each one the size of a stamp, each with a table code, and somebody has gone through and circled forty of them in biro with a route planned between them.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-cell responsive thumbnail grid, marked state persisted local, and deep-linking between catalog cell and hall map

concepts.form: an amateur character reference sheet, a spiky creature drawn in four views with an accompanying palette of named swatches, adoption rules and a do-not-steal warning hand-lettered into the remaining space
concepts.lineage: online amateur character reference sheet convention, four-view turnarounds, named palette swatches and adoption terms, 2004 onward
system: Palette/material: clashing saturated fills with hard black outline over a busy tiled background, plus a row of named color swatches with hex-style labels
Type/composition: four views ranged across the sheet, a swatch row beneath, and hand-lettered terms crammed into whatever space is left
Topology/navigation: the sheet is a specification, so navigation moves between views and the swatch that governs each part
Controls/state: controls are swatches, the active one highlights every region it governs, and unused ones dim
Responsive/motion: views reflow in whole panels, and motion is a swatch flashing the regions it controls
concepts.spark: four views of a creature nobody asked for, a row of named colors underneath, and in the corner, hand-lettered and underlined twice, a warning about what happens if you steal it.
concepts.webLeverage: svg region highlighting driven by swatch state, whole-panel responsive reflow, and a flash animation linking swatch to region

concepts.form: a panel van airbrushed with a full wraparound fantasy scene, a wizard and a moon rendered in soft gradient across the flank, the composition continuing across the door seam and around the rear corner without a break
concepts.lineage: 1970s custom van airbrush murals, wraparound fantasy scene painting and door-seam continuous composition
system: Palette/material: airbrushed purples and burnt orange blending seamlessly over body paint, with a hard white star field pricked into the darkest area
Type/composition: one continuous scene wrapping the flank with no framing, the composition crossing panel seams as if they were not there
Topology/navigation: the scene wraps, so navigation travels around the form and eventually returns to where it started
Controls/state: controls are scene elements, the active one gains an airbrushed glow, and inactive ones sit back in the gradient
Responsive/motion: the scene rewraps to any surface length, and motion is a slow travel around the form
concepts.spark: A wizard the length of a van, airbrushed so smoothly you cannot find a brush mark, and his staff carries right across the door seam as if the door were not there.
concepts.webLeverage: a responsive wrapping scene that rejoins seamlessly, css gradient airbrush layers, and travel motion around the form

concepts.form: a wrestling bill where masked portraits are ranked by billing, each mask rendered in flat symmetrical color with its own laced silhouette, and the card's matches stacked underneath as a ladder of paired names
concepts.lineage: Mexican lucha libre fight bills and mask design, symmetrical mask color systems and paired-match card typography
system: Palette/material: flat screened silver, scarlet and gold on black, every mask built from mirrored color fields with a hard lace outline
Type/composition: masked portraits ranked by billing size, matches stacked below as paired names divided by a versus rule
Topology/navigation: the card is a ladder of pairings, so navigation moves down through matches toward the main event
Controls/state: controls are mask portraits, the active one gains its lace outline, and defeated ones lose their mask entirely
Responsive/motion: the ladder restacks in whole pairings, and motion is a mask flipping to reveal the face beneath
concepts.spark: Every mask is perfectly symmetrical and instantly identifiable at fifty meters, and the whole card underneath is just pairs of names with a rule between them.
concepts.webLeverage: svg mirrored mask geometry scaling responsive, a flip reveal animation on state, and billing-rank ordering

concepts.form: a collector album spread of numbered empty slots, each printed with a ghosted outline of the sticker that belongs there, filled positions sitting slightly proud of the page and gaps advertising exactly what is missing
concepts.lineage: collectible sticker album publishing, numbered ghost-outline slots and swap culture conventions
system: Palette/material: matte album paper printed with pale ghosted outlines, against glossy stickers that sit visibly proud of the page surface
Type/composition: numbered slots ranged on a fixed grid with team or section headers, and every empty slot printing what should fill it
Topology/navigation: the album is a fixed set, so navigation moves between numbered positions and absence is as informative as presence
Controls/state: controls are slots, a filled one gains gloss and a shadow, and an empty one keeps its ghost outline and number
Responsive/motion: the slot grid reflows in whole positions, and motion is a sticker pressing down into its outline
concepts.spark: Forty-two of the fifty slots are filled and glossy, and the eight that are not tell you exactly which ones you still need in pale gray outline.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-slot responsive grid, collection state persisted local, and a press-down animation seating each sticker

concepts.form: a band shirt whose back carries the entire tour as a ranked list of cities and dates, the front mark small by comparison, the print cracking along the fold lines from years of wear and washing
concepts.lineage: concert tour shirt printing, ranked city and date back prints and plastisol crack-and-fade wear patterns
system: Palette/material: cracked plastisol on faded black cotton, the print broken along wear lines so the cloth shows through the letterforms
Type/composition: a small front mark against a full back panel of cities and dates ranked chronologically in condensed caps
Topology/navigation: the back is a chronology, so navigation moves down a list of places in the order they happened
Controls/state: controls are date lines, the active one prints solid, and cancelled dates are struck through in the same ink
Responsive/motion: the date list reflows in whole lines, and motion is print cracking further along a fold
concepts.spark: The front is a small logo and the back is forty-one cities in order, cracked along the fold where it sat in a drawer for a decade.
concepts.webLeverage: a responsive whole-line date list, a crack-progression filter bound to wear state, and struck-through cancellation state

concepts.form: a small printed instruction card slotted under glass at the base of a machine, scoring rules ranked in a dense two-column list with award values in bold, the whole card sized to a fixed slot and printed to be read while playing
concepts.lineage: pinball instruction card printing, ranked scoring rule layout and fixed-slot card sizing under playfield glass
system: Palette/material: two spot inks on card stock behind scratched glass, colors chosen to stay legible under playfield lighting
Type/composition: a dense two-column rule list with award values set bold, headings in reversed bars, sized exactly to a fixed slot
Topology/navigation: everything must be visible at once, so navigation is scanning a fixed card rather than paging
Controls/state: controls are rule lines, the active one reverses out of its bar, and achieved awards take a struck value
Responsive/motion: the two columns hold within a fixed aspect and never reflow to one, and motion is a value flashing on award
concepts.spark: Every rule the machine has, printed small enough to fit under the glass and just legible enough to read with one hand on the flipper.
concepts.webLeverage: a fixed-aspect two-column card, award state striking achieved values, and a flash animation on scoring

concepts.form: a streaming catalog wall of horizontally scrolling rows, each poster tile expanding on focus to reveal a title, a rating chip and a short line, with the active row lifting slightly and the rest of the wall dimming behind it
concepts.lineage: contemporary streaming catalog interface design, horizontal poster rails with focus expansion and row-level emphasis
system: Palette/material: a deep neutral ground with full-bleed poster artwork as the only color, and a single accent on the focused tile border
Type/composition: rows of fixed-ratio poster tiles with a row heading above, and metadata revealed only inside the focused tile
Topology/navigation: rows scroll horizontally and the wall scrolls vertically, so navigation is a grid traversed one axis at a time
Controls/state: controls are tiles, the focused one expands and reveals metadata, and the active row lifts while others dim
Responsive/motion: rows keep their tile ratio and show fewer per screen, and motion is a scale on focus with neighbors sliding aside
concepts.spark: Rows and rows of artwork, and the one you land on grows and tells you what it is while everything else quietly gets out of the way.
concepts.webLeverage: keyboard and pointer focus state driving tile expansion, horizontal rail scrolling with snap, and row-level dimming

concepts.form: a full-bleed vertical media surface where one item owns the entire viewport, a right rail of stacked action affordances, an author line and caption anchored low, and the next item already waiting one snap away
concepts.lineage: contemporary vertical video feed interface design, full-viewport items with right-rail actions and snap paging
system: Palette/material: media fills the frame edge to edge with a soft bottom scrim carrying the text, and pure white glyphs as the only interface color
Type/composition: an author line and caption anchored to the lower left, a vertical stack of action glyphs on the right, and nothing in the center
Topology/navigation: one item at a time occupies everything, so navigation is a single vertical snap between complete states
Controls/state: controls are rail glyphs, an engaged one fills and counts up, and the caption expands in place when truncated
Responsive/motion: the item always fills the viewport whatever its aspect, and motion is a hard snap with no partial scroll position
concepts.spark: One thing fills the whole screen, four glyphs stacked down the right, and the next one is exactly one flick away and already loaded.
concepts.webLeverage: scroll-snap paging with preloading, engagement counts in live state, and full-viewport media fitting at any aspect

concepts.form: a painted cart side divided into narrative panels by carved and gilded framing, each panel holding one battle or legend in hot saturated colour, the carved frame itself painted in a second contrasting scheme
concepts.lineage: Sicilian carretto painting, carved and gilded panel framing, narrative battle-scene panels and workshop repertoires
system: Palette/material: hot chrome yellow, vermilion and cobalt on wood, with the carved frame painted in a second contrasting scheme and picked out in gold-free ochre
Type/composition: narrative panels ranged along the cart side, each fully framed by carving, with a painted scroll of the owner's name along the top rail
Topology/navigation: panels sit in a fixed order along the side, so navigation travels the length of the cart from scene to scene
Controls/state: controls are panels, the active one saturates while its frame darkens, and past scenes cool toward the ground
Responsive/motion: panels add or drop along the length in whole units, and motion is a travel along the cart side
concepts.spark: A battle from a poem nobody reads any more, painted in chrome yellow on the side of a cart that hauled lemons, inside a carved frame painted a completely different set of colours.
concepts.webLeverage: whole-panel responsive travel along a length, frame-and-field two-scheme theming, and per-panel saturation state

concepts.form: a passenger jeepney dressed front and flank, hand-cut chrome lettering and a row of ornaments crowding the hood while painted panels run the length of the body, the owner's chosen name arced across the front above everything
concepts.lineage: Philippine jeepney decoration, hand-cut chrome lettering, hood ornament rows and painted flank panel practice
system: Palette/material: enamel body colour with hand-cut chrome and mirrored steel lettering, plus painted panels in unmixed saturated colour
Type/composition: an arced chosen name across the front above a crowded hood, with painted narrative panels running the flank at window height
Topology/navigation: front and flank do different jobs, so navigation moves from an identifying face to a narrating side
Controls/state: controls are ornaments, the active one catches light, and the name arc stays constant across every view
Responsive/motion: flank panels add or drop along the length while the front holds, and motion is light travelling the cut chrome
concepts.spark: The front tells you the driver named this thing after his mother; the side tells you an entire other story in painted panels; neither of them is about transport.
concepts.webLeverage: an svg arced name with cut-chrome highlight travel, responsive flank panel count, and per-ornament light state

concepts.form: a numbered card slipped into every packet, a fixed series where the album is sold separately and one number in every set is printed short so the run can never be finished by luck alone
concepts.lineage: cigarette and confectionery insert card series, numbered set collecting, companion albums and deliberate short prints
system: Palette/material: small stiff card with a lithographed face and a dense letterpress back, the back always more crowded than the front
Type/composition: an illustrated face with the number set small in one corner, and a full block of explanatory text filling the reverse
Topology/navigation: the set is a fixed numbered run, so navigation moves through absence as much as presence
Controls/state: controls are numbers, the active one flips to its reverse text, and missing numbers show an empty numbered slot
Responsive/motion: the album reflows in whole slots, and motion is a card flipping to its dense reverse
concepts.spark: Forty-nine of the fifty are common as dirt, and everyone knows which number is the one you will never find, because that was always the plan.
concepts.webLeverage: a whole-slot responsive album with collection state, flip-to-reverse interaction, and scarcity marked per number

families.label: Signals & Instruments
families.description: Instruments and display hardware that already solved showing state and inviting manipulation: flap boards, dials, drums, cords, tubes, and phosphor.

concepts.form: a broadcast teletext magazine, three-digit pages of block-mosaic graphics and double-height headers held in a 40 by 24 character grid on black
concepts.lineage: Ceefax and ORACLE broadcast teletext, World System Teletext mosaics, Mode 7 microcomputer graphics
system: Palette/material: the fixed broadcast eight on flat black, white for body text, yellow for headlines, cyan for live figures, red reserved for alerts and REVEAL answers
Type/composition: one bitmap face in a rigid 40 by 24 cell grid, double-height rows for section headers, block-mosaic sixels drawing every graphic from the same cells
Topology/navigation: every page holds a three-digit address keyed directly; magazines group by hundreds and subpages rotate on a timed carousel you can hold
Controls/state: keying digits is the whole input; loading counts page numbers in the header, hidden answers wait behind REVEAL, held subpages show a HOLD flag
Responsive/motion: the 40-cell row is sacred, small screens scale the cell rather than reflow; motion is subpage rotation and blink, both stoppable to a held still
concepts.spark: You key 302 and the header counts pages in the corner; the screen blinks and a football score builds itself from cyan blocks on black, and behind the quiz question an answer waits invisible until your thumb finds REVEAL.
concepts.webLeverage: ch-unit CSS grid and a bitmap face keep the 40 by 24 cell lattice exact; keyboard digits route pages and a REVEAL state toggles hidden spans

concepts.form: a crt oscilloscope on a signal bench, phosphor trace riding an etched graticule while detented knobs set channel, timebase, and trigger
concepts.lineage: Tektronix 465 and Hewlett-Packard cathode-ray oscilloscopes, electronic test-bench practice, phosphor display engineering
system: Palette/material: phosphor green blazing on near-black glass, graticule gray etched beneath, a second channel in dimmer trace; amber readouts for armed and warning states
Type/composition: condensed instrument caps on knob skirts and bezels, glowing seven-segment readouts; everything on screen is measured against the ten-division graticule
Topology/navigation: one screen, many signals; you travel by timebase and vertical scale, and channels overlay in the same graticule space rather than separate views
Controls/state: detented knobs set scale and trigger level; an untriggered trace rolls free, a triggered one locks still, and freeze holds the waveform for cursors
Responsive/motion: the graticule stays square while readouts drop below on narrow screens; the sweep is continuous
concepts.spark: You clip the probe to the pin and a green line snaps out of the noise; a nudge of the trigger knob and the waveform stands still, breathing in phosphor over the etched grid, ten divisions wide, every one meaning something.
concepts.webLeverage: canvas draws the persistent phosphor trace from live Web Audio or sensor input, with pointer-dragged trigger level and keyboard-stepped cursors

concepts.form: a collider event display, particle tracks curving out of one frozen collision through onion rings of detector and into stacked calorimeter wedges
concepts.lineage: CERN bubble-chamber photography, ATLAS and CMS event displays, Fermilab track-reconstruction graphics
system: Palette/material: near-black vacuum ground, detector rings in muted steel blue, tracks in signal yellow and cyan by particle type, red calorimeter bars for deposited energy
Type/composition: spare technical grotesk labels pinned to tracks and wedges, momentum figures in tabular digits; the concentric ring section is the compositional law
Topology/navigation: space is concentric, beamline at center; you move outward through detector layers and along individual tracks, one event held at a time
Controls/state: select a track to isolate it and dim the rest; competing reconstruction hypotheses overlay as ghost tracks, confidence written as line weight
Responsive/motion: the ring section stays whole on phones while wedges and figures move to drawers; rotation is inertial 3D
concepts.spark: The event lands and the cross-section blooms: yellow tracks curl through the inner rings, two stiff blue lines punch straight to the muon chambers, and red energy bars stack in the calorimeter wedges like a sudden bar chart of violence.
concepts.webLeverage: WebGL renders thousands of curved tracks in one 3D scene, with drag rotation, zoom into detector layers, and picked tracks reporting momentum

concepts.form: a printing darkroom under amber safelight, where enlarger beams, timed baths, and drying lines stage photographs into slow deliberate existence
concepts.lineage: Silver-gelatin darkroom practice, enlarger and easel design, safelight and test-strip conventions
system: Palette/material: amber safelight washing every surface as the ground, wet-print silver grays deepening to black as the image ink, enamel tray white at the edges
Type/composition: grease-pencil notes and printed timer digits under amber, labels sparse on bottles and trays; test strips band the field into stepped exposures
Topology/navigation: work moves through fixed stations in order: compose, expose, develop, fix, wash, dry.
Controls/state: progress is chemical and irreversible past marked points; test strips preview before committing.
Responsive/motion: stations linearize on phones; the develop reveal is one continuous emergence, shown statically under
concepts.spark: In the developer tray, gray ghosts gather into a face; the timer ticks, and pulling the print too early is a real loss.
concepts.webLeverage: Canvas-simulated development curves let previews emerge in real time before an action commits.

concepts.form: a small aircraft's night instrument six-pack, where six luminous gauges hold a pilot's trust through cloud with nothing outside the glass
concepts.lineage: General-aviation six-pack instrument layout, artificial-horizon and altimeter design, night-flight cockpit lighting
system: Palette/material: matte black panel ground, instrument faces near-black with luminous white markings, radium-green glow for needles; amber and red lamps only for caution
Type/composition: white aviation numerals and tick scales on round dials, terse placard caps beneath each gauge; two ranked rows of three set the fixed composition
Topology/navigation: a fixed constellation of instruments, each owning one truth; the cross-check sweep is the reading order.
Controls/state: deviations tilt needles before alarms; every gauge shows trend as well as value.
Responsive/motion: the six-pack stacks by criticality on phones; needle motion is damped and physical, never snapped.
concepts.spark: Outside is ink; inside, six calm dials agree with each other, and the practiced eye sweeps them in a quiet ritual of cross-checks.
concepts.webLeverage: Real-time data binds to SVG gauges with damped spring physics and a screen-reader flight summary.

concepts.form: a nixie-tube laboratory counter, where stacked digits glow orange inside glass envelopes and every count arrives as visible plasma
concepts.lineage: Cold-cathode nixie display tubes, Cold War laboratory counters, decimal-digit instrument design
system: Palette/material: neon orange digit glow inside clear glass envelopes, blackened steel chassis as ground, hairline anode mesh gray; the lit digit is the only warm accent
Type/composition: stacked metal numerals of one engineered digit form, each tube a fixed decimal place; labels sit as engraved caps on the panel below the banks
Topology/navigation: quantities are the interface; each metric owns a tube bank with fixed digit positions.
Controls/state: value changes cross-fade between physical digit layers; overflow and reset are visible mechanical events.
Responsive/motion: banks drop to essential digits on phones; digit transitions are single cross-fades under
concepts.spark: Inside each glass tube ten metal numerals nest; the lit one hovers orange, and a count change is a tiny change of physical depth.
concepts.webLeverage: Layered DOM digits with depth-true cross-fades render tube physics in pure CSS.

concepts.form: a green-phosphor terminal in a midnight machine room, where a blinking cursor, scanline glow, and afterimage trails make text feel alive on glass
concepts.lineage: VT100-era CRT terminals, P1 phosphor persistence, command-line interface history
system: Palette/material: P1 phosphor green on near-black curved glass, dimmer green afterimage for history, bright bloom for the cursor line; the tube's dark ground holds all
Type/composition: one monospaced bitmap face in a fixed 80-column field, no other type exists; hierarchy is made of indentation, case, and full-width rules
Topology/navigation: the surface is one continuous scrolling transcript; place is position in the conversation's history.
Controls/state: input is a first-class typed dialogue; system states print themselves rather than appearing as chrome.
Responsive/motion: phosphor bloom and trails scale with capability
concepts.spark: The cursor breathes; each typed line lands with a faint bloom and its ghost lingers a half-second after the scroll.
concepts.webLeverage: A live transcript log with CSS phosphor glow, searchable history, and full keyboard-first operation.

concepts.form: a pinball machine's backglass and playfield, a tilted world of ramps and rollovers where score erupts on painted glass above the physics below
concepts.lineage: Bally and Williams electromechanical pinball, Gottlieb backglass art, arcade score reels
system: Palette/material: saturated backglass enamel reds, yellows, and blues over mirror silver, playfield lacquer and chrome ball below; lit inserts flare the active target
Type/composition: airbrushed carnival lettering and drop-shadow score numerals on the glass, playfield labels curving with the lanes; the tilted plane composes everything
Topology/navigation: one inclined plane holds every target; the ball's path is the traversal, and everything is reachable but nothing is guaranteed
Controls/state: two flippers and a plunger are the entire input; lamps, chimes, and score reels answer every hit with disproportionate ceremony
Responsive/motion: portrait shows the full incline, landscape splits playfield from backglass
concepts.spark: The ball rockets off the plunger, kisses two bumpers into a scream of chimes, and the painted magician on the backglass lights up as the score reels slam forward a thousand at a time.
concepts.webLeverage: pointer and keyboard flippers drive a real 2d physics simulation; the Vibration API answers slingshot hits on touch devices

concepts.form: the seven-segment display family, bedside clocks, gas-station price totems, scoreboards, and microwave panels all speaking one eight-cell mask where unlit segments are designed too
concepts.lineage: Texas Instruments and Hewlett-Packard LED segment displays, 1970s clock radios, gas-station price totems, stadium scoreboards
system: Palette/material: lit segments in LED red, amber, or scoreboard green on matte near-black ground, unlit segments held as faint ghost cells; red glow owns the night register
Type/composition: one eight-cell mask makes every glyph, digits ranked in fixed slots with the colon or decimal as its own cell; absence is drawn as deliberately as light
Topology/navigation: the layout is a rigid mask of cells, from four bedside digits to a price totem's stack; place never moves, only which segments light
Controls/state: modes cycle by held buttons, set digits blink while everything else holds; the flashing 12:00 of an unset clock is the canonical error state
Responsive/motion: cells scale as whole units and never reflow mid-glyph; every change is an instant segment swap
concepts.spark: At 3am the bedroom hour hangs as four red digits; by noon the same alphabet quotes gasoline at two meters tall, and at the stadium the score slams from 98 to 100 with nothing sliding, segments simply dying and igniting.
concepts.webLeverage: CSS grid and clip-path build a true segment mask with ghost cells, and a shared worker keeps blink phase synchronized across every open tab

concepts.form: a rail concourse split-flap board at rush hour, where cascading letter flaps, platform columns, and departure rhythm hold a thousand travelers in one gaze
concepts.lineage: Solari di Udine split-flap displays, mid-century rail concourse boards, departure-row information design
system: Palette/material: matte black flap faces with white paint letters, brushed steel board frame as ground, amber row lamps for delay; cancelled rows drop to dim red type
Type/composition: one condensed white sans on every flap, characters in fixed cells, destinations in caps; the board's ruled rows and columns are the entire composition
Topology/navigation: rows are live entities ranked by time; columns never move, only their flaps.
Controls/state: changes cascade character by character; delayed and cancelled states restyle the row without breaking the grid.
Responsive/motion: the board narrows column priority on phones; the cascade collapses to a single update under
concepts.spark: A ripple of clacks runs the board, Milan becomes Marseille, and every head in the concourse lifts at the same half-second.
concepts.webLeverage: WebSocket-fed rows animate per-character flips while remaining a semantic, sortable table underneath.

concepts.form: a telegraph office counter, printed telegram blanks with gummed message strips, punched register tape coiling off the sounder, and route stamps dating every hop
concepts.lineage: Western Union telegram blanks, Morse-Vail register tape, railroad wire offices and route stamping practice
system: Palette/material: manila blank and buff tape grounds, black form print, message text in typewriter and paste-strip ink, one violet route stamp as the state accent
Type/composition: printed form rules and small caps framing pasted uppercase message strips; the telegram blank's boxes and STOP-broken lines set the composition
Topology/navigation: each message is one blank; the office is a counter of forms in flight, and a message's route reads as its ladder of stamps
Controls/state: composing fills a priced blank word by word; sending punches tape, and received words arrive as strips pasted in order, stamps confirming each hop
Responsive/motion: the blank keeps its printed proportions at any width; strips paste on in reading rhythm, appearing whole and still under
concepts.spark: The sounder clatters and tape spools; the clerk shears the gummed strip, pastes the words line by line onto a printed blank, and thumps the route stamp twice, so the message arrives wearing every office it passed through.
concepts.webLeverage: words stream in over WebSocket as pasted strips animated by CSS, the blank prints cleanly, and each message's route survives in the URL

concepts.form: a vu-meter bridge across a recording desk, a long row of ballistic needles behind glass that all lean into the red on the same downbeat
concepts.lineage: Neve and API meter bridges, the ANSI VU ballistics standard, broadcast peak-programme metering
system: Palette/material: warm ivory meter faces behind glass, black scale arcs and needles as the working ink, walnut and steel desk frame; the arc past zero is the only red
Type/composition: the VU scale's flared numerals and minus-to-plus arc on every face, channel numbers in strip labels below; identical meters repeat as the row's ruler
Topology/navigation: identical channels stand shoulder to shoulder; you read the room by sweeping the whole row, never by opening one meter
Controls/state: each needle integrates the last 300ms with weighted overshoot; the arc past zero is the only red the instrument allows
Responsive/motion: narrow viewports stack the row into bar ballistics
concepts.spark: Twenty needles lie asleep against their left pins until the chorus hits, and then the whole bridge leans right together, trembling at the edge of the red like horses at a gate.
concepts.webLeverage: an AnalyserNode feeds real signal levels; canvas needles obey true VU ballistics with mass and damping, never instant values

concepts.form: a trading floor quote wall and its glass-domed ticker, abbreviated symbols and fractional prices running on paper tape while clerks chalk the ruled grid of listed names
concepts.lineage: Edison stock tickers, NYSE chalk quote boards, Trans-Lux moving tape displays
system: Palette/material: slate-black board and manila tape grounds, chalk white for posted quotes, ticker print in ink black, an up or down chalk mark as the change accent
Type/composition: abbreviated ticker symbols and fractional figures in stenciled caps, the wall ruled into name rows and quote columns, tape running as one unbroken line
Topology/navigation: the wall grid is the index of listed names while the tape is time; you read a name down its column of quotes or chase the session along the tape
Controls/state: a new print posts over the old chalk figure with its ghost still faint; up and down marks accumulate through the session, and halts chalk a flat line
Responsive/motion: narrow screens keep the tape running and fold the wall to watched names; the tape's crawl pauses to a stacked list under
concepts.spark: The dome chatters and tape piles into the basket, US STL 68 1/2; a boy calls it out and a clerk on the ladder rubs out the old chalk figure, posts the new one, and adds another up-tick to a column already leaning bullish.
concepts.webLeverage: WebSocket prints feed a canvas tape crawl while the chalk grid stays a semantic table, sortable and searchable by keyboard

concepts.form: a 1970s network election night big board, character-generator numerals keyed white over deep studio blue, state-by-state returns ranked in ruled columns, percent-reporting counters under every total and a projected-winner stamp that lands only when the desk is sure
concepts.lineage: 1976-era NBC and CBS election night sets, Vidifont and Chyron character generators, hand-updated studio tally walls
system: Palette/material: deep studio blue ground, keyed white CG numerals with a soft edge glow, one candidate color bar per row, red held back for the moment a race is called
Type/composition: condensed all-caps CG lettering in ruled rows, state name left with raw count and percentage right, a small percent-reporting figure under every total
Topology/navigation: the board ranks races by closeness; drilling into a state opens its county rows, and the anchor-desk lower third follows you to every view
Controls/state: totals tick upward as precincts report, an unsettled race alternates its color bar, the PROJECTED stamp lands once and never retracts
Responsive/motion: phones keep one race per screen with its reporting counter; numerals change by odometer roll, never by fade
concepts.spark: at 11:04 the board holds at 91 percent reporting, two rows a thousand votes apart, and when the PROJECTED stamp finally slams over the top line the studio behind the numbers erupts off camera
concepts.webLeverage: server-sent updates roll the CG numerals with css transforms while every race stays a semantic, sortable table

concepts.form: a night radar watch, a circular phosphor scope swept by a rotating trace, blips blooming on first paint and decaying by recency, range rings and a compass rose ordering the dark, grease-pencil tracks marked by hand on the glass
concepts.lineage: Cold War air-defense PPI scopes, air traffic radar rooms, grease-pencil plotting practice
system: Palette/material: near-black scope ground, phosphor green trace and blips, dimmer green afterglow grading recency, grease-pencil white for human annotation, amber only for warnings
Type/composition: terse alphanumeric tags beside each blip, range ring numerals at fixed bearings, a compass rose at the rim; density lives in the tags, quiet in empty sectors
Topology/navigation: the scope is a polar map centered on you; range rings are distance, bearing is direction, and switching range scales is the only zoom that exists
Controls/state: the sweep refreshes truth once per rotation, a fading blip is aging data, a grease-pencil line is a human promise, and a new contact blooms brightest on first paint
Responsive/motion: small screens keep the full circle and shed the outer rings; motion is the constant sweep and the slow decay behind it
concepts.spark: the trace comes around and paints a new bloom at forty miles, brighter than everything else on the glass, and the watch officer leans in with a grease pencil to give it a name before it fades
concepts.webLeverage: canvas draws the sweep and persistence decay in real time while contacts mirror into an accessible bearing-sorted list

concepts.form: a night-shift telemetry bay, bedside traces sweeping in fixed channel color, green heart line, cyan oxygen, yellow breath, large numeric tiles updating beside each wave, alarm limits bracketing every value in quiet confidence
concepts.lineage: 1990s patient monitor design, ECG sweep-and-erase convention, hospital ward central telemetry stations
system: Palette/material: matte black screen ground, one fixed color per channel, green, cyan, and yellow, alarm red reserved and rare, everything else in dim gray restraint
Type/composition: large numeric values beside each trace in a squarish digital face, small unit labels beneath, channels stacked in strict rows with the most vital on top
Topology/navigation: each bed is a stack of channels and the ward view tiles the beds; you move from many small truths to one large one and back, never losing the vitals row
Controls/state: traces sweep left to right behind an erase bar, values inside their limit brackets stay calm, and crossing a limit colors the number first and sounds later
Responsive/motion: phones keep one bed with its top two channels; motion is the sweep itself, steady, unhurried, and never decorative
concepts.spark: at 3 a.m. the bay is a wall of slow green waves, and one cyan number drifts two points below its bracket, recoloring itself a beat before the soft chime, so the nurse is already standing
concepts.webLeverage: real-time channel data drives canvas sweep-and-erase traces with aria live regions announcing limit crossings

concepts.form: an early-80s rhythm machine step row, sixteen candy-colored step keys under a running chase light, pattern banks behind them and a tempo readout above, accents lighting deeper as the loop swings around again
concepts.lineage: Roland TR-808 and TR-909 step sequencers, pattern-based rhythm programming, chase-light panel convention
system: Palette/material: charcoal panel ground, the step row quartered in red, orange, yellow, and white keys, lit LEDs as the only glow, silkscreen white labels for everything else
Type/composition: instrument names as small silkscreen caps above their rows, the tempo in a red segmented readout, the sixteen-step row as the page's one unbroken line
Topology/navigation: patterns are pages and banks are chapters; the step row is a timeline you write into place, and the chase light always tells you where now is
Controls/state: tapping a step arms it and lights it, a second tap accents it brighter, the chase light sweeps in tempo, and an empty pattern is sixteen dark keys of invitation
Responsive/motion: the sixteen-step row never wraps, it scales; motion is the chase light and a key's press flash, both locked to the clock
concepts.spark: you punch four steps into the red quarter of the row and hit run, the chase light comes around, and the empty machine suddenly has a pulse you made, so you lean in and accent the offbeat
concepts.webLeverage: web audio clocks the chase light and playback while each step key stays a toggle button operable by keyboard

concepts.form: a folding cardboard book punched with slots that a fairground organ reads as it draws the pages through, the music existing physically as holes so a tear in the card is a wrong note forever
concepts.lineage: fairground organ book music, punched folding cardboard scores and pneumatic reading practice
system: Palette/material: heavy buff cardboard punched with rectangular slots, folded zigzag into a stack, with pencilled title and register marks
Type/composition: parallel tracks running the card's length, each track one note or register, with slot length carrying duration
Topology/navigation: the book is drawn through at a fixed rate, so navigation is position in a physical stack rather than a timeline
Controls/state: controls are tracks, the active one opens its slots, and a torn slot plays wrong permanently
Responsive/motion: track count holds while the visible window narrows, and motion is the book folding through at reading speed
concepts.spark: The music is not written down anywhere; it is a stack of cardboard with holes in it, and if the card tears the tune is wrong from then on.
concepts.webLeverage: a track-based punched score read at fixed rate, damage state that persists per slot, and a fold-through reading animation

concepts.form: A mill's jacquard control deck rebuilt as a scheduling surface: a laced chain of manila punched cards hanging off one heavy selvedge rail over a procedurally woven iron-green ground, where every value, label and conflict is punch geometry read on a lifted card rather than ink laid on the cloth.
concepts.lineage: Lyon and Bradford jacquard weaving mills, 1840s to 1960s: laced card chains, lifting-hook harness rows, Verdol punched paper, oiled cast-iron frames.
concepts.spark: A card chain hanging in a lit mill aisle, one manila card pulled proud on its hook so its punched holes throw a longer shadow than its neighbours, oiled iron frame behind, spools of madder and indigo racked above.
system: Palette/material: ground is a procedurally woven iron-green twill; all marks ride manila cards, madder rails, indigo plates or sulphur tags above it; foreign media pins to manila.
Type/composition: stencil condensed caps for labels; running prose only on manila plates in plain grotesque; columns hang from one heavy left selvedge, weight massed off-centre.
Topology/navigation: a chain of punched cards runs down one edge as the only index; the current card hangs proud of the chain, the rest recede in an even overlap.
Controls/state: state is punch geometry: open hole live, blind boss disabled, struck bar blocked, doubled hole conflicting; rank is a card lifted proud casting a longer shadow.
Responsive/motion: cards hang on cords and settle with weighted swing after a pull, never idling; narrow widths drop cards from the chain rather than shrinking the punch grid.
concepts.webLeverage: Build the ground as a procedural twill on canvas or WebGL, cards as SVG punch masks on manila plates with spring-damped settle on interaction, and every state as hole, boss or struck bar before colour.
avoid: Dead mill greys: the iron-green ground must sit against live madder, indigo and sulphur, never a monochrome machine-shop wash.
Ink printed straight onto the woven ground; text without a manila or plate carrier under it is off-system and illegible.
Skeuomorphic brass hooks, rivet bevels and leather straps rendered as chrome; the hardware reads as flat cut shapes and shadow only.

concepts.form: A film cutting bench flattened into a sheet: a perforated select rail crossing a grain-orange field, each step a punched frame held between two pins, the place you stopped marked by a folded tape flag, and everything set aside still hanging on pins below the rail.
concepts.lineage: The mid-century cutting room, 1950s to 1980s: Moviola and Steenbeck benches, edge-coded work prints, trim bins, grease pencil and paper tape flags.
concepts.spark: A work print strung between two pins under a bench lamp, white grease crosses struck across three frames, a folded orange tape flag doubled over the perforation where the editor stopped, and a dozen trims hanging on pins in the bin below.
system: Palette/material: one ink, flag orange in coarse film grain on true black; orange holds a third of any screen. Running copy and foreign images sit only in punched white windows.
Type/composition: one size of condensed grotesk throughout, caps for labels; rank is cell count not size, a window may span twelve frame cells while edge ticks stay hairline.
Topology/navigation: a perforated rail crosses every sheet at a fixed height; sections string along it as frames, and anything set aside hangs below on pins in an open bin.
Controls/state: state is a mark, not a hue: grease cross done, punched corner unavailable, tape band committed, folded flag where you stopped, hung on a pin deferred.
Responsive/motion: the strip scrubs with inertia and settles on perforation pitch, never between frames; hung trims swing and damp. Narrow screens drop frame count, not size.
concepts.webLeverage: The rail is one virtual strip whose scrub snaps to a fixed frame pitch; the frame you left is persisted and re-flagged on return, and every discarded frame stays reachable on a pin below the rail.
avoid: No rainbow of coloured tapes: the flags are one ink and rank comes from the mark and the cell count, never from a second hue.
No sepia nostalgia wash, no projector flicker, no vignette; the grain is sharp, the black is true and the windows are paper white.
No cinema mascots: clapperboards, film reels and countdown leader are decoration, and a rail with nothing hung under it is a border.

concepts.form: A monitoring wall staged as a vision-mixing gallery: a brushed anodised panel carrying screwed-on black enamel plates arranged as a plan of the plant, the one live source standing proud under a lacquer tally ring while dead sources are struck through with an engraved line.
concepts.lineage: Broadcast production galleries and their tally systems, roughly 1965 to 1985: engraved source plates, cue-light bays and lever-key vision-mixer panels.
concepts.spark: A dim gallery at 2am: forty engraved source plates screwed in rows to a scuffed grey panel, one lifted proud with a red lacquer ring burning around it, one plate scored through by a fresh engraved line, faders resting mid-throw and the room otherwise unlit.
system: Palette/material: brushed anodised ground, black enamel plates engraved white, one hue only: tally red as lacquer, filament and oxblood. Foreign images recess behind a chamfer.
Type/composition: no ink touches the ground; every word rides an engraved plate on a modular bay grid, white in black enamel. One condensed gothic, one size; size never ranks.
Topology/navigation: the surface reads as a plan, items plotted where they stand, bays divided by milled channels rather than gaps; a numbered rail holds one edge at every width.
Controls/state: state is elevation and strike. Live sits proud under a lacquer bezel ring, one proud plate per view; held is flush, dead struck through with an engraved line.
Responsive/motion: plates and faders travel with weight and settle with one overshoot; nothing cross-fades. Narrow widths drop bays out of the plan, never shrink a plate.
concepts.webLeverage: Labels are plate elements with real elevation: state is z-position plus an engraved strike rule, never colour alone; foreign media mounts in an inset chamfered aperture; exactly one proud plate per view is enforced in code.
avoid: No dead battleship-grey mush: the anodised ground must keep a directional brush and a warm graphite value under raking light.
No brass, rivets or glassy chrome gradients; plates are matte enamel screwed flat, not beveled toolbar buttons.
Do not flood the wall in red or scatter blinking lamps; one thing is live at a time and the ground itself never takes ink.

families.label: The Medium Itself
families.description: The browser and computation as material: generative systems, textmode culture, shaders, glitch, and web-native traditions that can exist nowhere else.

concepts.form: an algorave floor, where projected live code edits the music mid-dance and every thrown bracket changes what a hundred bodies do next
concepts.lineage: TidalCycles and SuperCollider live coding, algorave performance culture, projected-source screening ethics
system: Palette/material: phosphor green and magenta syntax on projector black, the code buffer as ground; the pattern about to change flashes amber before it sounds
Type/composition: monospaced terminal type at stage scale with hard line breaks as musical bars, the composition one code buffer whose cursor line is the downbeat
Topology/navigation: the source is the stage; sections of code map to audible layers you can follow live.
Controls/state: edits apply on the next cycle boundary; upcoming changes are visible before they sound.
Responsive/motion: code and visuals share one clock; small screens follow a single highlighted pattern lane.
concepts.spark: The coder deletes half a line and the kick drops out; the crowd howls, the line comes back wrong on purpose, and the room lifts.
concepts.webLeverage: Web Audio scheduling ties editable patterns to a shared clock with live evaluation in the page.

concepts.form: a dial-up bulletin board at 2 a.m., where ANSI title screens in sixteen colors, block-character art, and one phone line make a neighborhood out of text
concepts.lineage: ANSI artscene and BBS door culture, CP437 block graphics, 2400-baud modem-era interface design
system: Palette/material: sixteen ANSI colors on terminal black, cyan and magenta block art as chrome, blinking white on blue reserved for new mail and live presence
Type/composition: CP437 block glyphs and box-drawing rules composing all chrome on an 80 by 25 cell grid, centered title art over numbered menu lines
Topology/navigation: everything is a text screen with numbered exits; the character grid is the only geometry.
Controls/state: presence is scarce and precious; who is online, new posts, and mail land as textmode events.
Responsive/motion: the grid rescales by character cell; the pour-in reveal respects
concepts.spark: The title screen pours in line by line at modem speed, cyan on black, and being the only caller connected feels like owning the night.
concepts.webLeverage: A true character-grid renderer with line-by-line streamed arrival and complete keyboard operation.

concepts.form: a live scene rendered as typewriter characters, where density of glyphs stands in for light and an at-sign can be a face if it moves correctly
concepts.lineage: AAlib and libcaca renderers, ASCII-art scene culture, teletext and line-printer picture tradition
system: Palette/material: single-ink phosphor, green or amber on black; tone is glyph density from period to at-sign, and the densest glyph is the highlight
Type/composition: one strict monospace grid as the entire composition, the luminance ramp serving as the typographic scale, captions living inside the same grid
Topology/navigation: the world is a fixed character grid; you move the camera, and the alphabet re-renders the view.
Controls/state: the luminance ramp is the palette; swapping ramps changes mood while geometry stays put.
Responsive/motion: cell count adapts to viewport while glyphs stay monospace-true
concepts.spark: A rotating skull made entirely of dollar signs and periods; you squint and it is sculpture, you focus and it is text, and it is both at every distance.
concepts.webLeverage: Canvas or camera frames sample down to a live glyph grid, so video, 3D, and pointer input all become selectable text.

concepts.form: a pixel-art arcade cabinet screen, where fat luminous pixels, scanlines, and phosphor bloom turn a 240-line grid into a stage with real glow
concepts.lineage: CRT arcade monitors, pixel-art sprite discipline, shadow-mask and scanline rendering culture
system: Palette/material: a sixteen-color sprite palette over phosphor black, scanline gaps doing half the shading, flashing white-gold reserved by law for power-ups
Type/composition: eight-by-eight pixel caps for score and menus pinned to the top edge, the playfield composing in whole tiles with nothing allowed off-grid
Topology/navigation: space is a tile grid with screen-by-screen rooms; the camera moves in whole-pixel steps.
Controls/state: states are sprite swaps with strict palette discipline; damage, power, and rarity are palette laws.
Responsive/motion: integer scaling preserves the grid at every size; bloom and scanlines are togglable capability layers.
concepts.spark: Up close it is just squares; at play distance the squares fuse into a hero, and the black between scanlines is doing half the work.
concepts.webLeverage: Crisp integer-scaled canvas with shader scanline glow, and every sprite state addressable in code.

concepts.form: a shallow basin of suminagashi ink, where a fingertip drags marbled currents across the surface and every swirl obeys real fluid law rather than decoration
concepts.lineage: Japanese suminagashi and Turkish ebru marbling, Navier-Stokes solvers, Jos Stam's stable fluids
system: Palette/material: indigo and carbon sumi ink marbling on paper-white water, dye thinning to gray where it has spread, the newest drop always the darkest region
Type/composition: a quiet humanist sans held to a still margin outside the basin, the surface itself composing only as current, whorl, and feathered rain
Topology/navigation: the basin is one continuous surface; regions are dye colors that remember where they have flowed.
Controls/state: stir, drop, fan, and still are the verbs; viscosity and vorticity are dials with honest physical names.
Responsive/motion: simulation grid scales to GPU budget
concepts.spark: One drop of indigo lands, the fan passes, and the surface writes chrysanthemums; a fingertip's slow drag pulls the whole pattern into feathered rain.
concepts.webLeverage: A GPU fluid solver in WebGL answers the pointer at sixty frames, making the page itself a liquid material.

concepts.form: a HyperCard shoebox stack, where black-and-white cards link through buttons anyone can paint and the tool for reading is also the tool for making
concepts.lineage: Bill Atkinson's HyperCard, Vannevar Bush's Memex trails, Myst-era stackware and one-bit Mac aesthetics
system: Palette/material: one-bit black on white with stipple-dither grays and no color anywhere, the pressed button inverting to solid black as its active state
Type/composition: bold Chicago-style pixel menus over Geneva-style body text, cards composing as fixed rectangles with hand-drawn borders and painted buttons
Topology/navigation: space is a stack of cards linked by visible buttons; back retraces your exact trail through them.
Controls/state: every card is editable in place; browse and author are two modes of the same object.
Responsive/motion: cards keep fixed proportions and dissolve between each other
concepts.spark: A shoebox of black-and-white cards where clicking a hand-painted button flips you somewhere the author felt you should go next, and the paint tools are one menu away.
concepts.webLeverage: History API and deep links make every card addressable, while in-place editing keeps reader and author one keypress apart.

concepts.form: a hand-built homepage neighborhood, where tiled backgrounds, guestbooks, under-construction signs, and webring badges link strangers into a lane of personal rooms
concepts.lineage: GeoCities-era personal homepages, webring navigation culture, guestbook and hit-counter conventions
system: Palette/material: tiled starfield black with neon lime text, royal-blue links purpling once visited, the under-construction amber stripe marking anything unfinished
Type/composition: default serif body under exuberant display headings, centered layout ruled by horizontal lines, badges and counters clustering at the page's foot
Topology/navigation: spaces link laterally through ring badges: previous, random, next; discovery beats hierarchy.
Controls/state: visitor traces are celebrated; counters, guestbook entries, and last-updated stamps are first-class.
Responsive/motion: rooms keep their handmade proportions with honest scrollbars; ornament loops pause under
concepts.spark: Every page is somebody's room: a starfield background, a song you can stop, and a webring badge promising a neighbor either way.
concepts.webLeverage: Real cross-page ring navigation with shared state via URL, plus a live guestbook as the social layer.

concepts.form: an early one-bit desktop, dithered gray patterns standing in for every tone, window chrome with title bars and close boxes, marching-ants selections, and 32-pixel icons drawn from two colors
concepts.lineage: Susan Kare's Macintosh System icons and Chicago, Xerox Star, Windows 1.0 bitmapped interfaces
system: Palette/material: black and white pixels only, ordered stipple dithers standing in for every gray, selection inverting to solid black over a fifty-percent dither ground
Type/composition: bold Chicago-style pixel caps in title bars over small Geneva-style labels, windows composing as overlapping rectangles with one-pixel black chrome
Topology/navigation: overlapping windows on one desktop plane, folders opening into new windows while a zoom rectangle animates the lineage between them
Controls/state: pressing inverts, dragging shows a dotted outline, selections wear marching ants; dimmed dither means disabled and a checkmark marks the chosen item
Responsive/motion: windows tile edge to edge on small screens at whole-pixel scale
concepts.spark: You drag a window and its gray dither shears into moire as it moves; the trash can's lid pops open pixel by pixel, and the marching ants around your selection never stop walking.
concepts.webLeverage: image-rendering pixelated canvas keeps dithers crisp at integer scale, and CSS steps() animation drives the marching-ants selection border

concepts.form: a plotter drawing suite, where a pen machine draws thousands of near-identical lines and the artwork lives in the programmed deviation
concepts.lineage: Vera Molnár's plotter series and the first generation of machine-drawn art
concepts.spark: Forty squares repeat across the sheet in trembling ballpoint; each drifts one degree further from perfect, and somewhere in the middle the grid quietly becomes weather.
system: Palette/material: plotter-paper white with one or two pen colors; every mark is a stroked line and nothing is ever filled
Type/composition: gallery-quiet grotesk captions beneath drawings; series laid out as numbered suites in equal frames
Topology/navigation: Move by series, by parameter value, and by deviation step.
Controls/state: Adjust a parameter and watch the suite redraw; states are seeds, and every seed is reproducible.
Responsive/motion: Drawings replot stroke by stroke at readable speed; reduced motion shows finished plots instantly.
concepts.webLeverage: SVG stroke drawing with animated path length and user-adjustable seed parameters that stay deterministic

concepts.form: a minihompy room, where a furnishable isometric miniature space, an acorn economy, and a visitor ledger make identity something you decorate
concepts.lineage: Cyworld's Korean minihompy culture, 2003 to 2009
concepts.spark: A pastel room holds a tiny record player bought last week; the visitor counter ticks past 1,004, today's mood is a small rain cloud, and a friend leaves a note in the guest ledger.
system: Palette/material: pastel wallpaper and floor tiles in an isometric frame, sticker-like furnishings with soft outlines; the room itself is the profile
Type/composition: compact rounded labels on panels around the room, the diary column beside it, counters and mood marks as small honest chrome
Topology/navigation: Move by room, by diary entry, and by friend link.
Controls/state: Furnish, rearrange, and visit; placing an item changes the room for every visitor.
Responsive/motion: The room stays whole at every size while panels restack around it; furnishing lands with one soft settle.
concepts.webLeverage: A persistent decoratable isometric scene as the identity surface, with real furnishing state

concepts.form: an interactive type specimen, where dragging an axis slider morphs a whole grid of glyphs in real time
concepts.lineage: Contemporary digital type foundries, variable-font specimen microsites, OpenType 1.8 axes, 2016 onward
concepts.spark: A single giant letter fills the screen. You drag the weight slider and it thickens from hairline to black under your finger, live. Below, a grid of every glyph breathes in step, and a monospace readout counts the axis values.
system: Palette/material: Near-white paper and ink black with one foundry accent; flat surfaces, generous negative space, no ornament so the letterforms carry everything.
Type/composition: The specimen face at enormous display size against tiny monospace UI labels; a strict measure and baseline grid; hierarchy by scale contrast alone.
Topology/navigation: Move by axis slider, by glyph cell, and by size and specimen view.
Controls/state: Drag, type, and pin; moving an axis remaps every glyph on the page continuously and updates the live coordinate readout.
Responsive/motion: reduced-motion snaps between named instances instead of animating the interpolation.
concepts.webLeverage: Bind range inputs to CSS font-variation-settings through a custom property, so one slider drives font-variation across the entire glyph grid with no per-glyph JavaScript.

concepts.form: a data-sublime field, where dense barcode columns and sine lattices strobe in pure black and white
concepts.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda, datamatics and test pattern series, austere audiovisual data art, 2006 onward
concepts.spark: A wall of hairline vertical bars, some black, some white, holds like a frozen barcode. Dense monospace numbers pack the margin. A single sine curve traces the lattice, and for one frame the whole field snaps to its negative.
system: Palette/material: Pure black and pure white only, no grey and no color; flat pixel-crisp bars, hairline rules, and monospace numerics; the occasional full-frame inversion.
Type/composition: One monospace face at data density, set in tight tabular columns; barcode bar-fields and sine curves structure the page
Topology/navigation: Move by data column, by frequency band, and by frame index.
Controls/state: Scan, sample, and invert; selecting a column pulls its numbers into focus while the surrounding field drops to a faint bar pattern.
Responsive/motion: Columns thin and drop from the edges as width shrinks; reduced-motion disables all strobing and holds a single high-contrast still.
concepts.webLeverage: Render the barcode and sine lattice on canvas from a seeded sequence, stepping frames on requestAnimationFrame that halts entirely under prefers-reduced-motion.

concepts.form: a scrollytelling explainer, where a graphic pins to the viewport while a column of stepping prose scrubs it through state after state
concepts.lineage: The Pudding, NYT Upshot, and the Bloomberg and Reuters interactive-journalism school, 2015 onward
concepts.spark: You scroll a column of short paragraphs and a chart holds fast beside them, bars regrouping and a highlighted cohort lighting up exactly as the sentence you are reading claims it does.
system: Palette/material: warm paper-white ground, ink-black body text, one editorial accent such as signal red or ochre reserved for the highlighted series
Type/composition: a workhorse serif for prose at a generous measure against a tight grotesk for chart labels and figure numbers
Topology/navigation: Move by scrolling the prose column, by stepping through numbered figures, and by jumping to section anchors in a slim progress rail.
Controls/state: Scroll position drives the active step; each step re-scrubs the pinned graphic and fades the previous annotation as the new one writes in.
Responsive/motion: scroll-linked transitions ease between keyframes, and reduced-motion swaps scrubbing for discrete cut-to-state.
concepts.webLeverage: Bind an IntersectionObserver step index to a single pinned graphic held with position:sticky, tweening between authored keyframe states rather than swapping images.

concepts.form: the launch hero of a developer tool, where a recorded shell types itself across gradient-lit box-drawing panes as if a human were driving it live
concepts.lineage: the Charm, Warp, and modern gradient-TUI marketing school, 2021 onward
concepts.spark: A rounded pane sits center stage and a prompt types itself, output blooming in soft ANSI gradients, a spinner resolving to a green check while a copy-chip waits below for the one command you actually need.
system: Palette/material: near-black terminal ground, a warm-to-cool ANSI gradient from magenta through cyan for emphasis, dim gray chrome
Type/composition: one humanist monospace for everything, aligned to a strict character grid; tabbed code blocks and framed panes stacked on a centered single-column stage.
Topology/navigation: Move by tabbing between command examples, by replaying the typed sequence, and by copying any chip straight into your own shell.
Controls/state: A play control drives the typing animation; spinners resolve to success or error glyphs, and copy-chips flash a copied confirmation.
Responsive/motion: the type-on animation respects prefers-reduced-motion by rendering the finished terminal state instantly.
concepts.webLeverage: Drive the type-on effect from a timed token stream over pre-rendered ANSI, mapping 256-color codes to CSS custom properties so the gradient theming stays swappable.

concepts.form: the full-bleed portal of an experiential studio, where a GPU shader scene fills the screen and the interface floats as thin type over living pixels
concepts.lineage: the Active Theory, Lusion, and Awwwards experiential-WebGL school, 2016 onward
concepts.spark: A full-screen shader breathes in slow color, a custom cursor trailing a soft distortion where it moves; a loader counts to one hundred, then thin uppercase links dissolve the mesh into the next scene as you click through.
system: Palette/material: a deep single-hue ground driven by a fragment shader, fine film grain, one incandescent accent for hovers
Type/composition: an oversized variable grotesk for a single hero word against tiny tracked-out labels at the margins
Topology/navigation: Move by hovering the shader to displace it, by clicking thin corner links, and by letting inertial scroll drift the camera through the scene.
Controls/state: The cursor warps the field under it; page changes trigger a mesh transition that dissolves one scene into the next behind a percentage loader.
Responsive/motion: physics-scroll inertia eases all movement, and reduced-motion freezes the scene and disables the custom cursor.
concepts.webLeverage: Render the background as a single fullscreen WebGL fragment shader with a mouse-uniform displacement, and drive route changes through a shader dissolve transition rather than DOM swaps.

concepts.form: a hand-drawn technical zine on the web, where marker lettering, doodle arrows, and mascots teach a hard concept the way a friend sketches it on a napkin
concepts.lineage: the wizardzines and Julia Evans hand-illustrated explainer school, 2018 onward
concepts.spark: A cheerful marker headline sits above a doodled diagram, hand-drawn arrows looping from a wide-eyed mascot to a boxed code snippet, highlighter swipes marking the one line that matters as you step through the comic panels.
system: Palette/material: cream paper ground, black marker ink, two or three flat highlighter accents in yellow, pink, and teal
Type/composition: a hand-lettered marker face for headings paired with a clean readable sans for body
Topology/navigation: Move by stepping through numbered comic panels, by clicking mascot-guided call-outs, and by a sketched table-of-contents sidebar.
Controls/state: Hovering a doodle reveals its explanation; highlighter swipes animate across the active line; a mascot changes expression to mark done, warning, and gotcha states.
Responsive/motion: draw-on animation traces arrows in on scroll, and reduced-motion renders them already drawn.
concepts.webLeverage: Author diagrams as inline SVG with hand-drawn paths and animate the doodle arrows via stroke-dashoffset draw-on tied to scroll position.

concepts.form: a risograph-textured web system, where two or three spot inks misregister and grain over a warm paper ground the way a real Riso print does
concepts.lineage: the born-web risograph-hybrid and small-press print school, 2017 onward
concepts.spark: Flat fluorescent pink and blue shapes sit slightly out of register on toothy paper, halftone grain crawling their overlaps; hover a card and its inks shift a hair off-alignment, blooming a third color where they cross.
system: Palette/material: warm paper-tone ground, two or three fluorescent Riso spot inks such as fluoro pink, federal blue, and sunflower that multiply where they overlap
Type/composition: a bold grotesk or condensed serif set in single spot colors; cut-paper shapes and blocky layouts with deliberate slight misregistration between the ink layers.
Topology/navigation: Move by scrolling through ink-layered sections, by clicking cut-paper shape buttons, and by a spot-colored index rail.
Controls/state: Hover shifts an element's ink layers out of register for a printed-shudder feel; active states swap which spot ink sits on top
Responsive/motion: misregister transitions are quick and subtle, and reduced-motion locks the layers in perfect registration.
concepts.webLeverage: Composite each spot-ink layer as a separate element with mix-blend-mode:multiply over an SVG halftone and grain filter, and drive the misregister on hover with small per-layer transforms.

concepts.form: a realtime demo screen running on a home computer, horizontal copper bars grading down the background while a sine-warped greeting scroller crosses the foot and a bouncing logo holds the upper field
concepts.lineage: Amiga and Atari demoscene cracktros and demos, copper-bar raster effects, sine scrollers and greetz culture, 1988 onward
system: Palette/material: pure saturated raster colors banded horizontally, black void behind, and a chrome-free logo built from beveled bitmap letters
Type/composition: a fixed bitmap font on a baseline that follows a sine, a static logo pinned above, and the whole field split into raster bands
Topology/navigation: content arrives as an endless horizontal run, so navigation is waiting for the scroller to bring the next part around
Controls/state: controls are scroller stops, pressing one snaps the run to that greeting, and the active bar band brightens
Responsive/motion: raster bands restripe to any height, and motion never stops, since the scroller and bars run continuously
concepts.spark: the background is nothing but horizontal color bands changing every scanline, a logo bounces above them forever, and along the bottom a sine-warped message is still greeting people who stopped reading in 1993.
concepts.webLeverage: a canvas raster-bar shader, a real-time sine scroller animation, and deep-link stops that scrub the running text

concepts.form: a technical documentation surface built for long residence, a persistent left tree beside a measured prose column with a right rail of anchors, code blocks carrying a language tab and a copy affordance at every step
concepts.lineage: the modern developer documentation school, persistent navigation trees, anchored right rails and tabbed code blocks, 2018 onward
system: Palette/material: near-white paper ground with one ink for prose, a cool tinted panel behind code, and a single accent reserved for the active anchor
Type/composition: a humanist sans for prose at a measured column width, monospaced code in tinted panels, and a right rail of section anchors
Topology/navigation: the tree persists at all times so position in a large body is never lost, and the right rail maps the page you are in
Controls/state: controls are anchors and language tabs, the active anchor takes the accent, and copied code confirms in place
Responsive/motion: the tree collapses to a drawer and the rail folds into a summary, and motion is a quiet scroll-spy handoff
concepts.spark: You can be forty pages deep and still know exactly where you are, because the tree never went away and the rail on the right is quietly tracking your scroll.
